original: Social media, magazines and shop windows bombard people daily with things to buy, and British consumers are buying more clothes and shoes than ever before. Online shopping means it is easy for customers to buy without thinking, while major brands offer such cheap clothes that they can be treated like disposable items – worn two or three times and then thrown away.
simplified:
Shops and social media show people many things to buy every day.
British people buy more clothes and shoes now.
It is easy to buy online, so people buy without thinking.
Big shops sell very cheap clothes.
People wear these clothes only a few times, then throw them away.
reference: Every day, people see many clothes and shoes on social media, in magazines, and in shops. In the UK, people are buying more than before. Online shopping makes it easy to buy without thinking. Big brands sell clothes that are very cheap. Some people wear them only a few times and then throw them away.

original: Cape Town can be a dangerous place for baboons. Some have been injured or killed in car accidents and others have been electrocuted as they played with electric cables. Baboons are an endangered species and to save them and minimise conflicts between humans and baboons, the city council has employed a team of Baboon Monitors. The monitors' job is to chase baboons out of urban areas or catch them and release them in the countryside. This policy has had some success, though it is proving hard to stop baboons from coming back to the city once they see it as a source of easy food.
simplified:
Cape Town is not safe for baboons. Cars hit some baboons. They get hurt or die. Other baboons touch electric wires. They get a shock and die.

Baboons are rare animals. They need help. People and baboons sometimes have problems. So, the city hired people to help. They are called Baboon Monitors.

These people move baboons away from the city. They chase them or catch them. Then they let them go in the country.

This plan helps a little. But it is hard to stop baboons. They come back to the city. They find food easily there.
reference: Cape Town can be dangerous for baboons. Some are hurt or die in car accidents. Some die from playing with electric wires. Baboons are animals that are in danger of disappearing. To help them, the city now has a team called Baboon Monitors. These people try to move baboons out of the city and take them back to the countryside. This plan works a little, but the baboons often come back because they find food in the city.

original: A large number of bridge accidents occur during the construction of the bridge itself. These accidents are often due to an error made by the engineers, such as a miscalculation. The bridge collapses under its own weight, and this can be deadly for the workers on it at the time.
simplified:
Many accidents happen when people build bridges.
Engineers often make mistakes. For example, they might count wrong.
Then the bridge falls down because it is too heavy.
Workers on the bridge can die.
reference: Many accidents with bridges happen while they are being built. These accidents often happen because engineers make mistakes, like wrong numbers. The bridge can fall down from its own weight. This is very dangerous for the workers on the bridge.

original: Chloe has two pet rats, Zena and Roxy. Chloe knows they're not typical pets and she has lost count of the times she's patiently tried to explain to people that rats aren't dirty and they make fantastic pets if you look after them correctly. But she understands why people react badly. She didn't like rats either until her friend Martin showed her his pet rats and she saw how affectionate and intelligent they were. Last year, when one of Martin's rats had babies, Chloe decided she'd like to have two of them.
simplified:
Chloe has two pet rats, Zena and Roxy.
Chloe knows her rats are not common pets.
She often tells people that rats are clean.
She says they are good pets if you take care of them.
But she understands why people don't like them.
Chloe didn't like rats before.
Then her friend Martin showed her his rats.
She saw they were friendly and smart.
Last year, Martin's rat had babies.
Chloe wanted two of them.
reference: Chloe has two pet rats, called Zena and Roxy. She knows that rats are not usual pets, and many people think they are dirty. Chloe often tells people that rats can be very good pets if you take care of them. She didn't like rats before, but her friend Martin showed her his rats. She saw they were kind and clever. Last year, one of Martin's rats had babies. Chloe chose two of them to keep.

original: What does the art world think of graffiti and street art? Recently, there has been a growing recognition of its value as an art form. There have been major exhibitions of street art in galleries in Paris, London and Los Angeles. The American artist Elura Emerald organised a street art exhibition at a New York gallery in 2008. She defended street artists, saying 'artists who paint on the street are merely expressing themselves, not hurting anyone. They should be appreciated and celebrated'.
simplified: Many people now think street art is real art. There were big art shows in Paris, London, and Los Angeles. An American artist, Elura Emerald, had a street art show in New York in 2008. She said street artists just show their feelings. They don't hurt anyone. People should like their art.
reference: What do people in the art world think about street art and graffiti? Today, more people see it as a true kind of art. Big art shows in Paris, London, and Los Angeles have shown street art. In 2008, an American artist, Elura Emerald, made a street art show in New York. She said street artists only want to share their ideas and are not doing anything wrong.

original: Many city residents in Berlin, Germany complained that shooting pigs was unnecessarily cruel and there were heated arguments between hunters and animal lovers. In response to protests, the city council decided to take more peaceful action against pigs. Instead of shooting them, they have put up fences and made it illegal to feed the pigs. Time will tell if this strategy works, though it may be a losing battle as warmer winters mean that pig numbers are greater than in the past.
simplified:
Many people in Berlin, Germany, were angry. They said shooting pigs was too mean. Hunters and animal lovers argued a lot.

So, the city leaders made a new plan. They did not shoot the pigs. They built fences. And they said: "Do not feed the pigs!"

We don't know if this plan will work. It might be hard. There are more pigs now because winters are warmer.
reference: In Berlin, Germany, many people were upset because hunters were killing pigs. They thought it was too cruel. The city listened and changed the plan. Now people cannot feed pigs, and fences have been built. This is a kinder way to stop pigs. But there are still many pigs, because the winters are getting warmer.

original: Wonder is New Yorker RJ Palacio's first novel. On her website, she explains that the idea for the book came to her after seeing a girl with facial deformities on the street one day. Wonder has been a bestseller in the United States and has already won several awards. Many schools are using it as a starting point for discussions about bullying, friendship and what it's like to be different. A film version is being made, and many, including me, are waiting eagerly to see what RJ Palacio writes next.
simplified:
Wonder is the first book by RJ Palacio. She is from New York.
She says she got the idea for the book after seeing a girl with a different face.
Wonder is a very popular book in the USA. It has won many prizes.
Many schools use this book. They talk about being mean, friendship, and how it feels to be different.
They are making a movie of the book. Many people, like me, want to know what RJ Palacio will write next.
reference: Wonder is the first book by RJ Palacio, a writer from New York. She got the idea after seeing a girl with a face that looked different. The book is very popular in the United States and has won many awards. Many schools use the book to talk about bullying, friendship, and being different. A movie is now being made, and many people want to know what RJ Palacio will write next.

original: George Lucas was one of the early film directors to directly base his story on the 17 stages of the hero's journey. Typically the hero starts the story living an ordinary life, but something happens that calls them to an adventure that changes everything. At the beginning of Star Wars, Luke lives an ordinary life with his aunt and uncle, repairing robots. When he finds Princess Leia's message to Obi-Wan Kenobi inside the robot R2D2, it is 'the call to adventure' that starts the hero on his journey.
simplified:
George Lucas made movies. He used a story idea called 'the hero's journey'.

Usually, the hero lives a normal life. But then something happens. It makes them go on an adventure. This adventure changes their life.

In Star Wars, Luke lives a normal life. He lives with his aunt and uncle. He fixes robots.

He finds a message from Princess Leia in a robot, R2D2. This tells him to go on an adventure. It starts his journey.
reference: George Lucas was one of the first movie makers to use 'the hero's journey' idea. In this story, the hero starts with a normal life. Then something happens that begins an adventure. In Star Wars, Luke lives with his aunt and uncle and fixes robots. One day, he finds a message from Princess Leia. This is the start of his journey.

original: The Hunger Games takes place in the future, after the destruction of North America. The country is called Panem and is made up of twelve poor districts governed by the wealthy Capitol. The Capitol holds absolute power over the nation. Each district is responsible for producing different things for the Capitol. District 12, where the story begins, provides all the coal for the country. There used to be a thirteenth district but they rebelled against the Capitol in the past and were destroyed.
simplified:
The Hunger Games happens in the future. North America is gone.
The country is called Panem. It has 12 poor areas.
A rich city, the Capitol, rules them. The Capitol has all the power.
Each area makes different things for the Capitol.
District 12, where the story begins, gives all the coal.
There was a 13th area before. But they fought the Capitol and were destroyed.
reference: The Hunger Games happens in the future, after North America is gone. The new country is called Panem. It has 12 poor districts and one rich city, the Capitol. The Capitol has full power. Each district makes something for the Capitol. District 12, where the story starts, gives coal. There was a District 13, but it fought against the Capitol and was destroyed.

original: In the 1990s, graffiti continued but there was also an explosion in street art around the world. Some artists wanted to make political points and produced art that tried to make people think about war, inequality and discrimination. Other street artists were more concerned with producing beautiful, attractive work. In South America, many street artists went to work in poor areas adding colour, life and beauty to grey, city walls.
simplified:
In the 1990s, people still made graffiti. But street art also grew a lot everywhere.

Some artists wanted to show important problems. They made art to make people think about war, unfairness, and not treating people well.

Other artists just wanted to make beautiful art.

In South America, many artists went to poor areas. They put colour, life, and beauty on grey city walls.
reference: In the 1990s, street art became more popular. Some artists wanted to show ideas about war, unfair treatment, and other problems. Other artists only wanted to make the streets look beautiful. In South America, many artists painted in poor areas. Their art added colour and life to the grey walls.

original: One of the most interesting cases of wild animals living in a city are the wild dogs of Moscow. In Moscow, there are approximately 35,000 wild dogs living on the streets. Some of the dogs were born wild, while others are pets that have been abandoned by their owners. Some dogs live alone and others live in packs. In 2010, scientists studied the dogs and found that the dogs have adapted remarkably successfully to urban life. They have learned that it is safer to cross the street with people and some dogs appear to understand traffic lights.
simplified:
The wild dogs of Moscow are a special example of animals living in a city.
About 35,000 wild dogs live on the streets in Moscow.
Some dogs were born wild. Other dogs were pets, but their owners left them.
Some dogs live alone, and others live in groups.
In 2010, people studied these dogs. They found that the dogs are very good at living in the city.
They learned it is safer to cross the street with people.
Some dogs also seem to know about traffic lights.
reference: There are many wild dogs in Moscow, about 35,000. Some were born wild, and some were pets but left by their owners. Some live alone and others live in groups. In 2010, scientists studied the dogs. They found that the dogs have learned how to live in the city. Some dogs wait and cross the street with people. A few dogs even seem to know traffic lights.

original: Is graffiti art or vandalism? This depends on your point of view, but in many countries, writing or painting on public or private property is considered vandalism. Many street artists have been stopped by the police and some have had to pay fines. Many city councils complain about the high cost of cleaning graffiti off buildings, buses and trains.
simplified:
Is graffiti art or bad? People have different ideas.
In many countries, painting on public or private places is not allowed.
Police stop many people who do graffiti. These people must pay money.
City leaders say it costs a lot to clean buildings, buses, and trains from graffiti.
reference: Some people think graffiti is art. Others think it is bad. In many countries, painting on public or private places is not allowed. The police often stop street artists, and some must pay fines. Many cities say that cleaning graffiti from buildings and buses costs a lot of money.

original: Your dreams might show you all kinds of insights into things that you didn't realise you were thinking about. Common dreams like being able to fly or falling, your teeth falling out or having no clothes on in a public place probably mean something similar in most people. But the key to understanding exactly what they mean to you is to connect them to the events and feelings in your daily life.
simplified:
Dreams can show you things you think about, but don't know it.

Some dreams are common. For example, you might dream you can fly, or you are falling. You might dream your teeth fall out, or you have no clothes on in public. These dreams often mean the same thing for many people.

But to know what your dreams mean for *you*, think about your daily life. Think about what happens and how you feel each day.
reference: People have different dreams when they sleep. Some common dreams are flying, falling, losing teeth, or being outside with no clothes. These dreams often mean the same thing for many people. To know what your dream means, think about what is happening in your life and how you feel.

original: If most people have four to six dreams every night after the age of ten, that's as many as 2,000 dreams per year. So, by the time they reach 80 years old the average person might have had 140,000 dreams. Even if we forget 95–99 per cent of our dreams, that's still a few thousand remembered dreams across a lifetime. It's not too difficult to believe that, by coincidence, a dream event is followed by a real-life event that's similar to it, especially if the subject of the dream is something that happens often in everyday life.
simplified:
Most people have 4 to 6 dreams every night after they are 10 years old. This means about 2,000 dreams each year.
When a person is 80 years old, they might have 140,000 dreams.
We forget almost all our dreams (95-99%). But we still remember a few thousand dreams in our life.
It is easy to think that sometimes a dream happens in real life. This happens more if the dream is about normal things we do every day.
reference: Most people have 4 to 6 dreams every night after they turn 10. That means around 2,000 dreams every year. By age 80, a person may have about 140,000 dreams. Even if we forget 95?C99% of our dreams, we still remember many. So, it's not strange if something we dream later happens in real life, especially if it is something we often see in daily life.

original: An important inspiration for the Hunger Games book comes from Suzanne's love of classical Greek mythology. When she was a child, one of her favourite stories was Theseus and the Minotaur. In this story the city of Athens is ruled by Crete, but the Athenians rebel. As a punishment, Minos the king of Crete forces the Athenians to send seven boys and seven girls to Crete every year. The youths are thrown into the labyrinth and eaten by a monster that lives there called the Minotaur. But one of the youths, named Theseus, fights the Minotaur and kills it. Suzanne sees Katniss Everdeen as a futuristic Theseus.
simplified:
Suzanne loved old Greek stories. These stories gave her an important idea for The Hunger Games book.

When she was a child, she loved the story of Theseus and the Minotaur. In this story, the city of Athens was controlled by Crete. But the people of Athens fought back.

So, King Minos of Crete made Athens send seven boys and seven girls to Crete every year. These young people went into a big maze. A monster called the Minotaur lived there and ate them.

But one young man, Theseus, fought the Minotaur and killed it. Suzanne thinks Katniss Everdeen is like Theseus, but in the future.
reference: The writer of The Hunger Games, Suzanne, got the idea from old Greek stories. When she was young, she liked the story of Theseus and the Minotaur. In the story, the city of Athens must send children to a monster called the Minotaur every year. The Minotaur lives in a maze and eats the children. One boy, Theseus, fights the monster and kills it. Suzanne thinks Katniss, the main character in The Hunger Games, is like Theseus, but in the future.

original: By bringing people and animals together, zoos have the potential to educate the public about conservation issues and inspire people to protect animals and their habitats. Some zoos provide a safe environment for animals which have been mistreated in circuses, or pets which have been abandoned. Zoos also carry out important research into subjects like animal behaviour and how to treat illnesses.
simplified:
Zoos bring people and animals together. They can teach people about animals. They can help people want to protect animals and their homes.

Some zoos give a safe home to animals. These animals were hurt in circuses or left by people.

Zoos also do important studies. They learn about how animals act. They also learn how to help sick animals get better.
reference: Zoos bring people and animals together. They help people learn how to protect animals and nature. Some zoos give homes to animals that were hurt in circuses or left by their owners. Zoos also study animal behavior and how to help sick animals.

original: Often wild animals come into cities to look for food. In Cape Town, South Africa, baboons have started coming into residential areas on the edge of the city to feed. They open rubbish bins and eat fruit from gardens and orchards. Some brave baboons have even come into people's houses and taken food from kitchen cupboards and fridges! Baboons can be aggressive and have attacked a lot of pet animals, so understandably, many city residents don't welcome their presence.
simplified: Wild animals often come to cities to find food. In Cape Town, South Africa, baboons now come to houses near the city to eat. They open trash cans and eat fruit from gardens and trees. Some baboons are not scared. They even go into houses and take food from kitchen shelves and fridges! Baboons can be mean. They have hurt many pets. So, people in the city do not want them there.
reference: Wild animals often go into cities to look for food. In Cape Town, South Africa, baboons now go into areas near people's homes. They open rubbish bins and eat fruit from gardens. Some baboons are very brave and go into houses to take food from kitchens. Baboons can be dangerous and sometimes hurt pet animals. Many people in the city do not want them around.

original: Sam squinted against the sun at the distant dust trail raked up by the car on its way up to the Big House. The horses kicked and flicked their tails at flies, not caring about their owner's first visit in ten months. Sam waited. Mr Carter didn't come out here unless he had to, which was just fine by Sam. The more he kept out of his boss's way, the longer he'd have a job. Mr, Carter wiped the sweat from the back of his neck. The damp patches on his shirt drew together like shapes in an atlas. His skin was already turning ruddy in the June sun. Otherwise he had the indoor tan of a man that made money while other people did the work.
simplified:
Sam looked at the sun. He saw dust from a car far away. The car was going to the big house.

The horses moved their legs and tails because of flies. They did not care that their owner was visiting. He had not come for ten months.

Sam waited. Mr Carter only came here if he needed to. Sam liked this. If Sam stayed away from his boss, he would keep his job longer.

Mr Carter wiped sweat from his neck. His shirt was wet. His skin was getting red in the sun. He usually stayed inside. He looked like a man who worked inside.
reference: Sam looked at a car coming to the Big House. The car made a lot of dust. The horses moved their tails to stop the flies. They didn't care that their owner was coming after ten months. Sam waited. Mr. Carter came only when he had to, and Sam liked that. If he stayed away from his boss, he could keep his job. Mr. Carter wiped his neck. His shirt was wet from sweat. His skin was red from the hot June sun. Normally, he stayed inside and made money while others worked.

original: Underutilised items may seem useless to some, but could be an asset to others. With the advent of the internet, online communities have figured out a way to generate profit from the sharing of those underused assets. Using websites and social media groups that facilitate the buying and selling of second-hand goods, it is now easier than ever for peer-to-peer sharing activities to take place. And this is known as the sharing economy.
simplified:
You might not use some things. Other people might want them.

Now we have the internet. People online found a way to make money. They share things they don't use.

Websites and social media help people buy and sell used things. It is very easy for people to share things with each other.

This is called the sharing economy.
reference: Things that we don't use much may look useless, but other people may need them. With the internet, people have found a way to share these things and make money. Website and social media groups now help people to buy and sell used goods. It is easy for people to share with each other in this way. This is the sharing economy.

original: According to Campbell, the hero at first refuses the call to adventure, but a mentor appears who helps them and they decide to 'cross the threshold' and travel into the 'special world' where the adventure happens. The next stage consists of passing tests, fighting enemies and meeting friends as the hero prepares to face their biggest challenge. For Luke the mentor is, of course, Obi-Wan, the friends are Han Solo and the robots R2D2 and C3PO and the enemy is Darth Vader inside the special world of the Death Star.
simplified:
First, the hero does not want to go on an adventure.
Then, a helper comes. The helper helps the hero.
So, the hero goes to a special new place. This is where the adventure happens.
Next, the hero must do hard things. They fight bad people and meet friends.
This makes the hero ready for a very big problem.

For Luke, Obi-Wan is the helper.
His friends are Han Solo, R2D2, and C3PO.
Darth Vader is the bad guy.
The special place is the Death Star.
reference: Campbell says that first, the hero does not want to go on the adventure. Then a teacher, also a mentor, comes to help. The hero then goes into a "special world" where the adventure happens. In this world, the hero has to do tests, fight enemies, and meet new friends before the biggest fight. Luke's teacher is Obi-Wan, his friends are Han solo and the robots R2D2 and C3PO, and his enemy is Darth Vader inside the Death Star.

original: A different trend is springing up in opposition to consumerism – the 'buy nothing' trend. The idea originated in Canada in the early 1990s and then moved to the US, where it became a rejection of the overspending and overconsumption of Black Friday and Cyber Monday during Thanksgiving weekend. On Buy Nothing Day people organise various types of protests and cut up their credit cards. Throughout the year, Buy Nothing groups organise the exchange and repair of items they already own.
simplified:
A new idea is starting. It is called 'buy nothing'. It means people do not want to buy too many things.

This idea started in Canada in the 1990s. Then it came to the US. People did not like buying too much on Black Friday and Cyber Monday. These days are after Thanksgiving.

On Buy Nothing Day, people protest in different ways. They also cut their credit cards.

All year, Buy Nothing groups help people swap and fix things they already have.
reference: Some people are starting a new idea called the 'buy nothing' trend. It began in Canada in the 1990s and then went to the USA. These people don't like buying too much on days like Black Friday and Cyber Monday. On 'Buy Nothing Day', people protest and cut their credit cards. During the year, they also fix and trade things instead of buying new ones.

original: Another suggested defence against a PHA on course to hit Earth is to blow it up using a nuclear weapon. It may sound like a plot from a film, and it was the subject of the 1998 film Armageddon, but the Hypervelocity Asteroid Mitigation Mission for Emergency Response (HAMMER) is a genuine NASA proposal. The eight-ton rockets would be fired at an approaching asteroid with the hope of bumping it off course. If the asteroid was too close to Earth for this plan to work, the rockets would carry nuclear bombs to blow it up instead.
simplified:
One idea to stop a space rock coming to Earth is to blow it up with a nuclear bomb. This sounds like a movie story, like in the film Armageddon. But NASA has a real plan for this. It's called HAMMER.

They would shoot big rockets at the space rock. The rockets would push it away from Earth. If the space rock is too close, the rockets would have nuclear bombs to blow it up.
reference: One way to stop an asteroid from hitting Earth is to break it with a strong bomb, which is nuclear weapon. This may sound like a movie, and it was in the 1998 film Armageddon. But NASA had a real plan on this. The plan was to send big rockets, about eight tons, to hit the asteroid and push it away. If the asteroid is already too close to Earth, the rocket would take the nuclear bomb to blow it up.

original: Religion is important to Pi. Though his family is Hindu, he is curious about other religions and he makes friends with a Christian priest and a Muslim baker. To everyone's surprise, Pi declares himself to be simultaneously Hindu, Muslim and Christian. When his family and teachers ask him to choose just one religion, Pi refuses, saying 'I just want to love God'. From that moment, his family and teachers decide to let him make his own mind up about religion.
simplified: Religion is important to Pi. His family is Hindu. But Pi wants to know about other religions. He makes friends with a Christian priest and a Muslim baker. Everyone is surprised. Pi says he is Hindu, Muslim, and Christian. His family and teachers ask him to choose one religion. Pi says no. He says, 'I just want to love God.' After that, his family and teachers let him choose his own religion.
reference: Religion is important for Pi. His family is Hindu, but he is also interested in other religions. He makes friends with a Christian priest and a Muslim baker. One day, Pi says that he is Hindu, Muslim, and Christian at the same time. His family and teachers ask him to choose only one religion, but Pi says, "I just want to love God." After this, his family and teachers let him choose his way.

original: In her previous work environment, Gabriela was used to a high power distance culture where power and authority are respected and everyone has their rightful place. In such a culture, leaders make the big decisions and are not often challenged. Her Swedish team, however, were used to working in a low power distance culture where subordinates often work together with their bosses to find solutions and make decisions. Here, leaders act as coaches or mentors who encourage independent thought and expect to be challenged.
simplified:
Gabriela's old job was a place where bosses were very important. People respected the bosses. Bosses made all the big decisions, and workers did not question them.

But her team in Sweden was different. Here, workers often worked with their bosses. They found solutions and made decisions together. Bosses helped people. They wanted workers to think for themselves and ask questions.
reference: In her old job, Gabriela worked in a place with high power distance. This means people respect authority, and leaders make the big decisions. Workers do not usually question their bosses. But her Swedish team worked in a low power distance culture. Here, workers and bosses make decisions together. Leaders act like coaches or teachers, and they want workers to think for themselves and even question them.

original: I work for a global IT company, but because their headquarters is in the States, I do all my work online from home. That means that I don't waste time commuting or making idle chit-chat with colleagues. I work on a project basis, and this flexibility is very valuable to me because it means that I can easily take some time off when my children need me to go to their school performances or if I need to schedule an appointment with the dentist. The downside is that without clear office hours, I tend to work well into the evening, sometimes skipping dinner to finish a task.
simplified:
I work for a big computer company. Its main office is in America. So, I work from home on the internet.
I don't travel to work. I also don't talk a lot with co-workers.
I work on different jobs. This is good for me. I can take time off easily. For example, when my children have school shows. Or when I need to go to the dentist.
But there is a problem. I don't have clear work hours. So, I often work late. Sometimes I don't eat dinner to finish my work.
reference: I work for a large IT company, but I work from home because the office is in the USA. I do everything online. This is good because I don't waste time going to work or talking too much with coworkers. I work on different projects, and this is helpful. I can take time off if my children have a school show or if I need to see the dentist. But there is a problem: I don't have fixed hours, so I often work late and sometimes skip dinner to finish my work.

original: Some people think writing your dreams down can open your mind to lucid dreaming. Lucid dreams are dreams where you're not only aware you're dreaming but you can make decisions to affect the events of your dreams. So, maybe you can turn a nightmare into a safe-feeling dream, or you can direct the plot of your dream like a film director. Then, instead of just working out the meaning of your dreams, you'll be creating them, though you might want to continue having some dreams that allow your subconscious to tell you what's on your mind!
simplified:
Some people think writing your dreams helps you have lucid dreams.
Lucid dreams are when you know you are dreaming.
In these dreams, you can choose what happens.
You can change a bad dream to a good one.
You can control your dream, like a movie director.
So, you make your dreams. You don't just think about what they mean.
But sometimes, it's good to let your mind show you things in dreams.
reference: Some people think that writing down dreams in a notebook can help them have lucid dreams. A lucid dream is when you know you are dreaming, and you can change what happens. For example, you can make a bad dream feel safe, or you can control the story like a movie director. In this way, you are not only looking for the meaning of your dreams, but also making them. But sometimes, you may still want dreams that show what is in your mind.

original: I'm a freelancer and work for myself. This is great because I am in control of what I do and how I spend my time. At first, I was working from home, but I found it really hard to concentrate. There were just too many distractions around: housework that needed doing, another cup of tea, my family members wanting my attention for various things. So I started to go to a nearby café to work, but the Wi-Fi connection wasn't ideal and I found myself drinking too much coffee. In the end, I decided to rent a desk in a co-working space with five other freelancers like myself. I liked getting dressed to go to work in the morning and being able to focus in an office environment.
simplified:
I work for myself. This is good because I choose my work and my time.

First, I worked at home. But it was hard to focus. Many things stopped me. I had housework, tea, and my family needed me.

So I went to a cafe to work. But the internet was bad, and I drank too much coffee.

Finally, I rented a desk in a shared office. Five other people like me worked there.

I liked getting ready for work in the morning. I could focus well in the office.
reference: I am a freelancer, so I work for myself. This is good as I can choose what to do and how to spend my time. At first, I worked at home, but it was hard to focus. There were many things around me, like housework, making tea and families asking for attention. Then I tried to work in a cafe, but the internet was not good and I drank too much coffee. In the end, I rented a desk in a co-working space with five other freelancer. I liked dressing up for the office and going to work in the morning.

original: Faith47 is from Cape Town in South Africa. She paints big, colourful pictures of people and animals and likes to explore different locations. Her work is found on pavements, in empty factories and on abandoned cars. She likes the fact that most street art is temporary and will soon be removed by weather or cleaners from the city council. For her, this reflects how life is full of change with its cycle of endings and new beginnings.
simplified: Faith47 is from Cape Town in South Africa. She paints big, colourful pictures of people and animals. She likes to see new places. You can see her art on streets, in empty buildings, and on old cars. She likes that most street art does not stay for a long time. The rain or city workers clean it away soon. For her, this shows that life changes a lot. Things end, and new things start.
reference: Faith47 comes from Cape Town in South Africa. She paints big, colourful pictures of people and animals. She likes to paint in many places, like on pavements, in empty factories, and on old cars. And we can see her work in these places. She enjoys that street art does not last forever and will be removed by rain or by city cleaners. For her, this shows that life is always changing, with things ending and new beginnings.

original: Around the 18th and 19th centuries two main ideas about dreams became popular. One was the idea that the things we see in our dreams represent things hidden from our conscious mind. Freud believed that if we understand what dreams are telling us, we can understand our hidden feelings and the problems they cause. However, the other theory was the opposite. It said that dreams are just a collection of random activity in the brain while it's organising memories and events from the day. When we wake up, we try to make sense of these random images and feelings and put them into some sort of story.
simplified:
A long time ago, in the 1700s and 1800s, people had two main ideas about dreams.

One idea was that what we see in dreams means things we don't know when we are awake. A man called Freud thought that if we know what our dreams mean, we can understand our secret feelings and why we have problems.

But the other idea was very different. It said dreams are just random things our brain does when it puts together memories and things from the day. When we wake up, we try to understand these mixed-up pictures and feelings and make them into a story.
reference: In the 18th and 19th centuries, people had two main ideas about dreams. The first idea was that dreams show things that we dont know in our mind. Freud believed that if we look at dreams, we can understand our hidden feelings and problems. The second idea was opposite. It said dreams are only random things in the brain when it is cleaning and organising the day's memories. When we wake up, we try to make a story from these pics and feelings.

original: Blek le Rat started out painting rats on the walls of his home city, Paris. Nowadays, he tries to make people think about different social issues and problems. He paints pictures of homeless people in big cities to encourage residents to think about the problem of homelessness.
simplified: Blek le Rat first painted rats on walls in his city, Paris. Now, he wants people to think about problems for people. He paints people with no home in big cities. He wants people in the city to think about this problem.
reference: Blek le Rat began by painting rats on the walls of Paris, his home city. Now, he uses his art to talk about social problems. In big cities, he paints pictures of homeless people to make others think about homelessness.

original: The 'buy nothing' trend has now reached influencers on social media who usually share posts of clothing and make-up that they recommend for people to buy. Some YouTube stars now encourage their viewers not to buy anything at all for periods as long as a year. Two friends in Canada spent a year working towards buying only food. For the first three months they learned how to live without buying electrical goods, clothes or things for the house. For the next stage, they gave up services, for example haircuts, eating out at restaurants or buying petrol for their cars. In one year, they'd saved $55,000.
simplified:
Social media stars often tell people to buy clothes and make-up. But now, some of them like the 'buy nothing' idea.

Some YouTube stars now tell their fans not to buy anything for a long time, even a year.

Two friends in Canada tried to buy only food for one year.

For the first three months, they learned to live without buying electric things, clothes, or things for their home.

Next, they stopped paying for services. For example, they did not get haircuts, eat in restaurants, or buy fuel for their cars.

In one year, they saved $55,000.
reference: The "buy nothing" idea is now gaining popularity among social media influencers. Normally, they show clothes and make-up for people to buy. But now, some YouTubers tell their fans not to buy anything, even for one year. Two friends in Canada did this and only bought food for a year. In the first three months, they stopped buying electronics, clothes, and things for the house. Later, they also stopped paying for services, like haircuts, eating in restaurants, and petrol for their cars. In one year, they saved $55,000.

original: People might not realise they are part of the disposable clothing problem because they donate their unwanted clothes to charities. But charity shops can't sell all those unwanted clothes. 'Fast fashion' goes out of fashion as quickly as it came in and is often too poor quality to recycle; people don't want to buy it second-hand. Huge quantities end up being thrown away, and a lot of clothes that charities can't sell are sent abroad, causing even more economic and environmental problems.
simplified:
People might not know they cause a clothes problem. They give old clothes to charity shops. But shops cannot sell all these clothes.

'Fast fashion' clothes are cheap and new. They go out of style quickly. They are often bad quality. So, you cannot recycle them. People do not want to buy them used.

Many clothes are thrown away. Shops also send many unsold clothes to other countries. This makes more problems for money and nature.
reference: Some people don't know they are part of the clothing waste problem because they give old clothes to charities. But charity shops cannot sell all of them. Fast fashion quickly goes out of style and is often poor in quality, so people don't want to buy second-hand. A lot of clothes are thrown away, and many clothes that charities cannot sell are sent to other countries. This causes money and environmental problems.

original: In some areas, councils have tried to encourage artists not to paint graffiti randomly on walls by allowing them to work in designated areas. Taiwan is one such place and there are 'graffiti zones' where artists are free to paint and write on walls. In São Paulo in Brazil, the city council has even allowed some graffiti artists to paint on the city's subway trains.
simplified:
Some cities let artists paint. But they ask them to paint in special places. They don't want artists to paint on any wall.

Taiwan is one of these places. It has 'graffiti zones'. Artists can paint on walls there.

In São Paulo, Brazil, the city even lets some artists paint on subway trains.
reference: In some places, councils want artists to stop painting graffiti anywhere on the walls. Instead, they give them special places to paint. In Taiwan, there are "graffiti zones" where artists can paint and write on walls. In São Paulo, Brazil, the council also lets some graffiti artists paint on the city's subway trains.

original: Not content with one amazing trip, some of today's adventurers go from challenge to challenge. Meagan McGrath from Canada has climbed the highest mountain on each continent, ridden a bike across Canada and run a long-distance race in the Sahara Desert in 45ºC heat. But perhaps her most remarkable journey was a skiing trip to the South Pole. On the first day, she fell into a glacier and had to be rescued. Many of us would have given up at that point, but Meagan decided to carry on. She reached the South Pole forty days later, having pulled a sledge with a tent and all her food behind her through freezing conditions and ice storms.
simplified:
Some brave people like to do many hard things. One trip is not enough for them.

Meagan McGrath is from Canada. She climbed the tallest mountain on every continent. She rode a bike across Canada. She also ran a very long race in the Sahara Desert. It was 45 degrees hot there.

But maybe her best trip was skiing to the South Pole. On the first day, she fell into a big piece of ice. Someone had to save her. Many people would stop then. But Meagan decided to go on.

She got to the South Pole after 40 days. She pulled a sled with her tent and food. The weather was very cold, with ice and snow.
reference: Some adventurers today like to do many difficult trips. Meagan McGrath from Canada climbed the tallest mountain on each continent, rode her bike across Canada, and ran a long race in the Sahara Desert, where it was 45ºC. But maybe her most special trip was skiing to the South Pole. On the first day, she fell into a glacier and needed help to get out. Many people would stop there, but Meagan continued. After forty days, she reached the South Pole, pulling a sledge with her tent and food through very cold weather and ice storms.

original: When Gabriela became aware of the cultural differences between her and her team, she took the initiative to have an open conversation with them about their feelings about her leadership. Pleased to be asked for their thoughts, Gabriela's team openly expressed that they were not used to being told what to do. They enjoyed having more room for initiative and creative freedom. When she told her team exactly what she needed them to do, they felt that she didn't trust them to do their job well. They realised that Gabriela was taking it personally when they tried to challenge or make changes to her decisions, and were able to explain that it was how they'd always worked.
simplified:
Gabriela saw that she and her team worked in different ways. She talked to them about how they felt about her as their leader.

The team was happy she asked. They said they didn't like being told what to do all the time. They liked to be creative and decide things for themselves.

When Gabriela told them exactly what to do, they felt she did not trust them to do their job well. They understood that Gabriela got upset when they tried to change her ideas. They told her that this was how they always worked.
reference: When Gabriela saw that she and her team had cultural differences, she chose to talk with them openly about her leadership. The team was glad to be asked and said they were not used to being told what to do. They liked having more freedom and space to be creative. When Gabriela told them exactly what to do, they felt she didn't trust them to do their job. They also saw that Gabriela felt upset when they questioned her decisions. They explained that this was just the way they normally worked.

original: Os Gêmeos are identical twin brothers from São Paulo. They paint everything from tags to huge, colourful pictures of people on the sides of buildings. Their work is often so big that they need cranes to help them work. In 2007, they covered the whole of a castle in Scotland with paint.
simplified:
Os Gêmeos are twin brothers from São Paulo.
They paint big, colorful pictures of people on buildings.
Their pictures are often very big.
They need cranes to help them.
In 2007, they painted a whole castle in Scotland.
reference: Os Gêmeos are identical twin brothers from São Paulo.  They paint many things, from small tags to very big, colourful pics of people bu buildings. Their work is often so big that they need cranes to help them. In 2007, they painted a whole castle in Scotland.

original: Writing about your dreams will mean you start to remember more details about the dream, so think about the people and place where the dream happened as they might add to the meaning too. Over the period of a week you'll be surprised how much you've written down. Now you can start connecting your dreams to the events and feelings in your daily life.
simplified: Write about your dreams. You will remember more. Think about the people and places in your dream. This can help you understand it. After one week, you will see how much you wrote. You will be surprised. Now you can link your dreams to your life and feelings every day.
reference: When you write down your dreams, you remember more things. Think about the people and the place in the dream, because they can mean something. After one week, you will see that you have written a lot. Then, you can see how your dreams link to your feelings in your daily life.

original: The first is DART – the Double Asteroid Redirection Test. Plans are scheduled to test DART on the moon of an asteroid called Didymos. 'Didymoon' is 150 metres wide, orbiting its 800-metre mother, and hopefully the impact of DART will knock it out of its orbit enough for Earth-based telescopes to pick up.
simplified: DART is a test. It will hit a small space rock. This rock is called Didymoon. Didymoon is 150 metres wide. It moves around a bigger rock. We hope DART will hit Didymoon. This hit should push Didymoon a little. Then, telescopes on Earth can see it move.
reference: The first project is DART- the Double Asteroid Redirection Test. It will be tested on the moon of an asteroid called Didymos. This moon is called "Didymoon." It is 150 metres wide and goes around its bigger "mother" asteroid, which is 800 metres wide. Scientists hope that when DART hits Didymoon, it will change its path enough for telescopes on Earth to see.

original: People have been painting and writing on walls throughout history. In prehistoric times, people in Africa and Europe used to paint pictures of animals and people in caves. Graffiti has been found on buildings at ancient sites in Greece, Italy, Syria and Iraq. In the Roman town of Pompeii, archaeologists have found numerous examples of graffiti written in Latin. These include religious, political and romantic messages, and even some magic spells!
simplified:
People painted and wrote on walls for a very long time.
A long time ago, people in Africa and Europe painted animals and people in caves.
People found graffiti on old buildings in Greece, Italy, Syria, and Iraq.
In an old Roman town called Pompeii, people found a lot of graffiti in Latin.
These were messages about religion, politics, and love.
There were even some magic words!
reference: People have painted and written on walls for a very long time. In early times, people in Africa and Europe painted animals and people inside caves. Graffiti has also been found on old buildings in Greece, Italy, Syria, and Iraq. In the Roman town of Pompeii, archaeologists found many graffiti messages in Latin. These messages were about religion, politics, love, and even magic spells!

original: Historically, more bridges were made of wood and were much more susceptible to fire. This was particularly true of old-fashioned train bridges, where the spark created by the steel wheels and steel tracks could sometimes cause a bridge to catch fire and burn to the ground.
simplified: In the past, many bridges were made of wood. They could easily catch fire. This was often a problem for old train bridges. Sparks from the train's metal wheels and tracks could sometimes make the bridge burn down.
reference: In the past, many bridges were made of wood. Wood can burn easily. Train bridges had a big problem, because the steel wheels on the steel tracks made sparks. The sparks could make the wooden bridge burn.

original: Suzanne Collines has always found news programmes of wars upsetting. When she was a child, her father was a pilot in the US Air Force and he fought in Vietnam. Her mother tried to protect her by not telling her what was happening in the war, but she still saw news programmes about the war and knew that her dad was there. It was a very frightening experience for her.
simplified:
Suzanne Collines always felt sad when she saw war news on TV.
When she was little, her dad was a pilot for the US army. He fought in the Vietnam War.
Her mum tried to keep her safe. She didn't tell Suzanne about the war.
But Suzanne still saw war news on TV. She knew her dad was there.
It was a very scary time for her.
reference: Suzanne Collines alwasy felt sad when she saw war news on TV. When she was a child, her father was a  pilot in the US Air Force and fought in Vietnam. Her mother did not tell her much about the war to keep her safe, but she still saw the news and knew her dad was there. It was very scary for her.

original: Whether NASA can find the remaining middle-sized NEOs depends on getting the money to build NEOCam, a 0.5-metre space telescope which would use infrared light to locate asteroids. If it did get the money, it could probably achieve its goal in ten years. Once logged, the planetary defence team would still need to work out how to defend the planet against being hit by the truly worrying asteroids – the PHAs.
simplified:
NASA wants to find more space rocks that are not too big. For this, NASA needs money to build a special telescope called NEOCam. This telescope uses special light to find the rocks.

If NASA gets the money, it can find them in 10 years.

After they find the rocks, a special team still needs to think how to protect Earth. They need to stop the most dangerous space rocks from hitting Earth.
reference: NASA needs money to build NEOCam, a space telescope with a small lens, to find the rest of the middle-sized asteriods. This telescope would use infrared light to look for them. If NASA gets the money, it could finish this in 10 years. After that, the team must still plan how to stop the very dangerous asteriods, called PHAs, from hitting Earth.

original: The heroine of the story, a sixteen year old girl called Katniss Everdeen, has lost her father in a mining accident and has to provide food for her family. She hunts in the woods around District 12 with her friend Gale and becomes very skilful with a bow and arrow. When her younger sister, Prim, is chosen as one of the tributes, Katniss volunteers to go instead. The other tribute from District 12 is a boy named Peeta and Katniss soon finds herself in a complicated relationship with him.
simplified:
The main girl is Katniss Everdeen. She is 16. Her father died in a mine. So, she must find food for her family. She hunts in the forest near District 12 with her friend, Gale. She is very good with a bow and arrows.

Her little sister, Prim, is chosen for a dangerous game. Katniss says she will go instead. The other person from District 12 is a boy named Peeta. Katniss has a difficult relationship with him.
reference: Katniss is 16 years old. Her father died in a mining accident, so she has to help her family and bring them food. She hunts in the forest near District 12 with her friend Gale. Katniss is very good at shooting with a bow and arrow. One day, her sister Prim is chosen to fight in the Games. Katniss says she will go instead. The other tribute is a boy called Peeta, and Katniss has a strange and hard relationship with him.

original: Erik Weihenmayer from the United States is a multi-adventurer. He's ridden a bike through the deserts of Morocco, kayaked through the Grand Canyon and climbed Everest. Amazingly, Erik has been blind since the age of 13. Apart from his travels, he tries to encourage people with disabilities to live active lives and takes groups of young blind people on climbing expeditions.
simplified:
Erik Weihenmayer is from the USA. He does many exciting things.
He rode his bike in the desert in Morocco. He went kayaking in the Grand Canyon. He climbed Mount Everest.
Erik is blind. He has been blind since he was 13.
He also helps people with disabilities. He tells them to be active.
He takes young blind people climbing.
reference: Erik Weihenmayer is from the United States and loves adventures. He rode a bike in the deserts of Morocco, went in a kayak in the Grand Canyon, and climbed Mount Everest. He has been blind since he was 13 years old. Erik also helps people with disabilities. He takes groups of blind young people on climbing trips to show them they can be active too.

original: It is impossible to know how street art will develop in the future but certain trends are emerging. While most street artists are young people who paint in their city or neighbourhood, more and more street artists are travelling and working around the globe. Other artists are using the internet to talk to each other and share photos of their work. Also, the art world is giving more recognition to street art as a legitimate art form. Although we don't know what will happen to street art in the future, we can be sure that it is here to stay!
simplified:
We don't know what street art will be like in the future. But we see some new things.
Most street artists are young. They paint in their town. But now, more artists travel. They paint in many countries.
Some artists use the internet. They talk to other artists and show pictures of their art.
And people who like art now think street art is important. They say it is real art.
We don't know what will happen to street art later. But we know it will always be here!
reference: We don't know what street art will be like in the future, but we can see some changes now. Most street artists are young and paint in their own city. But more artists are travelling and making art in other countries. They also use the internet to talk and show pictures of their work. Today, street art is starting to get more respect as real art. We don't know what will happen, but street art is htere.

original: In 2010, the planetary defence team at NASA had identified and logged 90 per cent of the asteroids near Earth measuring 1km wide. These 'near-Earth objects', or NEOs, are the size of mountains and include anything within 50 million kilometres of Earth's orbit. With an estimated 50 left to log, NASA says none of the 887 it knows about are a significant danger to the planet.
simplified:
In 2010, a NASA team looked for big rocks in space.
They found 90% of the rocks that are 1 kilometer wide.
These rocks are called NEOs. They are like mountains.
They fly close to Earth, within 50 million kilometers.
NASA thinks there are about 50 more to find.
NASA says the 887 rocks they know are not a big danger to Earth.
reference: In 2010, NASA found 90% of the big asteroids near Earth that are 1km wide. They are callled 'near-Earth objects'. They are very large like mountains and they move close to Earth's path. NASA thinks about 50 are still missing, but the 887 already found are not dangerous to Earth.

original: In a global survey conducted by PricewaterhouseCoopers (PwC), more than 40,000 millennial (born between 1983 and 1993) and non-millennial responses were collected on the topics of workplace culture, communication and working styles, pay structure, career development, work–life balance, etc. In a separate global survey conducted by Deloitte, more than 10,000 millennials participated in a study about their perceptions of the threats and opportunities in the complex world of work.
simplified:
PwC did a big survey.
More than 40,000 people answered questions.
Some were young people (born 1983-1993), and some were older.
They talked about work.
They talked about: how people work together, how they talk, their pay, how they can get better jobs, and time for work and life.

Deloitte did another big survey.
More than 10,000 young people answered questions.
They talked about good and bad things at work.
reference: PwC (a company) did a survey around the world. They asked more than 40,000 people, born between 1983 and 1993 (millennials) and some other years.  The questions were about work life, like pay, career, the balance between work and life, and communication. Another company, Deloitte, also made a world survey. They asked more than 10, 000 millennials what they think about the problems and chances nowadays.

original: Democratised online platforms are providing a chance for people to make a quick buck or two. To give an example, busy parents previously might not have bothered with setting up a stall at the local market or car boot sale to sell their children's old equipment, but with online marketplaces, parents are now able to sell on those hardly worn baby clothes that their children have outgrown and the expensive pushchairs and baby equipment they have invested in, so as to put some cash back into their pockets.
simplified: Online websites help people earn money easily. For example, busy parents used to find it hard to sell old things at a market. But now, with online shops, parents can sell baby clothes that are too small. They can also sell expensive prams and baby things. This helps them get some money back.
reference: Online websites let people make money. Previously, busy parents did not have time to go ta a market to sell their children's old things. Now, with online shops, they can sell baby clothes which baby doesn't worn anymore, as well as the pushchairs. This helps them get some money back.

original: Having decided to go to school, Auggie then has to face his first day. Like every child starting at a new school, he is really anxious. But because of the way he looks, it's an agonising experience. Nobody wants to sit next to him and he notices other kids staring at him or talking about him behind their hands. Fortunately, he makes friends with Jack, a boy in his class, and Summer, a girl he chats with at lunch. But it's not just the first day that's hard. Auggie soon learns that his classmates don't want to touch him for fear of catching 'the plague'. As he goes through the school year, Auggie goes through many intense ups and downs till finally an unexpected and traumatic event at a school camp changes things completely.
simplified:
Auggie decides to go to school. He has his first day.
He is very worried, like other children on their first day.
But Auggie looks different. So, it is a very hard time for him.
No one wants to sit with him. He sees other children look at him. They talk about him quietly.

Luckily, he makes two friends. Jack is a boy in his class. Summer is a girl he talks to at lunch.
But the hard time does not stop after the first day.
Auggie learns that other children do not want to touch him. They are scared they will get sick, like 'the plague'.

Auggie has good times and bad times during the school year.
Then, something big and sad happens at a school camp. This changes everything.
reference: Auggie decides to go to school and face his first day. He is very nervous, like other new students. But because of how he looks, it is very hard. No one wants to sit near him, and he sees children looking at him and talking about him. He is lucky to make two friends: Jack, a boy in his class, and Summer, a girl he meets at lunch. Still, life at school is not easy. Some kids think they will get a sickness, called "the plague," if they touch him. During the school year, he has many good and bad moments. Then, at a school camp, something shocking and difficult happens that changes everything.

original: Have you ever dreamt of climbing Mount Everest or walking to the South Pole? If so, you're not alone. Every year, thousands of people try to climb the world's highest mountains or walk across continents. Unlike the explorers of the past who used maps and compasses, today's adventurers travel with modern technology like GPS and satellite phones. Many adventurers are nature lovers who use their travels to help raise awareness about a range of environmental issues, while others are keen to help people in need and raise money for charities.
simplified:
Do you ever want to climb Mount Everest or walk to the South Pole? Many people do.

Every year, many people try to climb very high mountains or walk across large areas of land.

Long ago, explorers used maps and compasses. But today, these adventurers use new tools like GPS and special phones.

Many of them love nature. They travel to tell people about problems with the Earth. Others want to help people who need it and get money for groups that help others.
reference: Have you ever dreamed of climbing Mount Everest or going to the South Pole? Many people have. Every year, thousands of people try to climb the highest mountains or walk across continents. In the past, explorers used maps and compasses, but now they use modern tools like GPS and satellite phones. Many of them love nature and want to tell people about environmental problems. Others want to help people in need and collect money for charities.

original: Pi and Richard Parker spend 227 days in the lifeboat. They live through hunger, illness and exhaustion. They endure violent storms and the burning heat of the Pacific sun, but somehow they survive. At times, Pi finds comfort in his three religions, but at other times he is overcome with loneliness and despair. Finally, the Mexican coast appears on the horizon and everything changes. It would be a shame to give away the ending, so you will have to read the book yourself to find out what happens to Pi and Richard Parker once land is in sight.
simplified: Pi and Richard Parker spend 227 days in the lifeboat. They are hungry, sick, and very tired. They face bad storms and very hot sun. But they survive. Sometimes, Pi's religions help him. But sometimes he feels very lonely and sad. Then, they see land in Mexico. Everything changes. I cannot tell you the end of the story. You must read the book. Then you will know what happens to Pi and Richard Parker when they see land.
reference: Pi and Richard Parker stay in a lifeboat for 227 days. They are usually hungry, sick and very tired. They live through big storms and the hot sun of the Pacific Ocean, but they are alive. Sometimes Pi feels better because of his three religions, but other times he feels very sad and alone. One day, he sees the land of Mexico, and things start to change. To know the ending, you must read the book yourself.

original: Throughout history and across cultures, dreams have been associated with prophecy. People thought dreams were messages from the gods, sent to give us knowledge or insight. Even today, many people can recall a time they dreamed about an event, place or person and then, later, the dream came true in real life.
simplified: For a long time, people everywhere thought dreams could tell the future. They believed gods sent dreams to tell people things. Even today, many people remember a dream. They dreamed about something, a place, or a person. Later, it happened in real life.
reference: In history, people in many cultures believed dreams could tell the future. They thought dreams were messages from gods. Even now, some people say they dream about a person, place or event and later it really happeded.

original: Over 4,000 climbers, aged from thirteen to eighty have been to the top of Everest. Though climbing high mountains in freezing conditions and violent storms is still extremely dangerous, the world's best climbers now look for new challenges. Gerlinde Kaltenbrunner from Austria fell in love with mountain climbing as a teenager. When she left school, she worked as a nurse, but kept climbing in her free time.
simplified: More than 4,000 people, from 13 to 80 years old, climbed Mount Everest. Climbing big mountains is very dangerous. It is very cold and there are bad storms. reference: Over 4,000 climbers, aged between 13 to 80,  have been to the top of Mount Everest. Climbing high mountains is still very dangerous due to the cold and storms. The best climbers now look for new challenges. Gerlinde Kaltenbrunner from Austria started to love climbing when she was a teenager. After school, she became a nurse, but she still climbed in her free time.

original: Chloe arrived home from school, made herself a cup of coffee and took it up to her bedroom. She had some homework to do, but that could wait for later. She wanted to enjoy the quiet hour before her parents arrived home and the house filled up with the evening sounds of chatter, television or her dad listening to his beloved jazz while he cooked dinner. She liked this time of day too because she could play with her pet rats.
simplified: Chloe came home from school. She made coffee and took it to her room. She had homework, but she wanted to do it later. She wanted to enjoy the quiet time. Her parents would come home soon. Then the house would be noisy. They would talk, the TV would be on, or her dad would listen to his jazz music when he cooked dinner. She also liked this time because she could play with her pet rats.
reference: Chloe got home from school and made a cup of coffee. She went to her room. She had homework, but she wanted to do it later. She enjoyed the quiet hour before her parents came home. In the evening, the house was full of talking, TV, and her dad's jazz music while he cooked. Chloe also liked this time as she could play with her pet rats.

original: Some of the biggest and most expensive transportation projects in the world have involved building bridges. Bridges are crucial links that carry cars, trucks and trains across bodies of water, mountain gorges or other roads. As a result, they are one of the most important aspects of civil engineering and are subject to intense scrutiny, especially when they collapse.
simplified: Building bridges can be very big and cost a lot of money. Bridges are very important. They help cars, trucks, and trains go over water, mountains, or other roads. So, people who build things must make them well. People watch bridges very closely, especially if they fall down.
reference: Some of the biggest and most expensive transport projects are bridges. Bridges are important because they let cars, trucks and trains cross rivers, mountains or other roads, They are an important part of building work, and people look after them carefully, especially when a bridge falls down.

original: The two men looked towards the northern end of the property. It stretched as far as the eye could see. Even the fences were barely visible from where they stood. However bored and rebellious a teenage boy might get, it wasn't possible to escape on foot. Sam looked at the biggest of the horses, kicking at the ground with its heavy hooves. Could the boy ride? he wondered. There was a whole load of trouble a good rider could get into out here, miles away from anyone. But maybe there was even more trouble for someone who knew nothing about horses and wanted to get away from his father.
simplified: The two men looked to the far end of the land. It went on for a long way. They could hardly see the fences from their place. A teenage boy might be bored or angry, but he could not run away by foot. Sam looked at the biggest horse. It was kicking the ground. Could the boy ride a horse? Sam thought. A good rider could find many problems here, far from people. But maybe there were even bigger problems for someone who didn't know about horses and wanted to leave his father.
reference: The two men looked at the north side of the land. It was so big that they could hardly see the fences. A teenage boy might to run away, but he could not do it on foot. Sam looked at the biggest horse, stamping the ground with its heavy feet. He asked himself: could the boy ride? A good rider could still find touble here, far from anyone. But a boy who could not ride and wanted to escape his father might find it even more dangerous.

original: After weeks of frustration, Gabriela emailed her Swedish manager about the issues she was facing with her team. Her manager simply asked her if she felt her team was still performing, and what she thought would help her better collaborate with her team members. Gabriela found her manager vague and didn't feel as if he was managing the situation satisfactorily.
simplified: After many weeks, Gabriela was unhappy. She sent an email to her Swedish boss. She wrote about problems with her team. Her boss asked her if her team was working well. He also asked what she needed to work better with them. Gabriela thought her boss was not clear. She felt he was not helping to solve the problem.
reference: Gabriela was unhappy for many weeks, so she sent an email to her Swedish manager about the problems with her team. The manager only asked if the team was still working and what could help her work better with them. Gabi thought his reply was not clear, and he was not fixing the problem well.

original: Having climbed Everest, Gerlinde decided to climb all fourteen of the world's 8,000 metre peaks. To increase the challenge, Gerlinde climbs without using oxygen tanks. This is risky as low oxygen levels at the top of high mountains can affect brain and body functioning. Gerlinde uses her fame as a climber to support a charity for poor children and orphans in Nepal.
simplified:
Gerlinde climbed Everest. She decided to climb all 14 mountains in the world that are 8,000 metres high.
She climbs without oxygen tanks. This makes it harder.
It is dangerous. On high mountains, there is little oxygen. This can hurt her brain and body.
Gerlinde is a famous climber. She helps a charity for poor children and orphans in Nepal.
reference: After climbing Mount Everest, Gerlinde wanted to climb all fourteen mountains in the world that are over 8,000 metres high. She does it harder by not using oxygen tanks. This is very risky, because at the top there is little oxygen, and it can hurt our brain and body. Gerlinde also helps a charity in Nepal to care poor children and orphans.

original: If we look around us at the things we have purchased at some point in our lives, we would no doubt notice that not everything we own is being put to good use: the thick woollen coat which we thought looked trendy despite the fact that we live in a tropical country, the smartphone that got put away when we bought ourselves the newest model, the car that only gets used at the weekends, or even the guest room in our house that somehow got turned into a storeroom.
simplified:
Look around you. Think about things you bought. You might see that you don't use everything well.

For example:
*   A thick coat you liked, but you live in a hot country.
*   Your old phone, when you bought a new one.
*   The car you only use on weekends.
*   The guest room in your house that is now a storage room.
reference: When we look at the things we bought, we see that we don't use everything. Maybe we have a thick coat that we liked but don't need in a hot country. Or we have an old phone we don't use after buying a new one. Some people have a car that they only use on weekends. Others have a guest room that turned into a storeroom.

original: Ed Stafford from the UK is the first person to walk the length of the Amazon River. He started by a small stream in the Andes mountains of Peru and arrived at the river's mouth in Brazil, two years and four months later, having walked 6,000 kilometres. The Amazon rainforest is home to poisonous snakes, crocodiles and jaguars, so Ed was in constant danger. Luckily, he survived with nothing worse than a few thousand mosquito and ant bites.
simplified:
Ed Stafford from the UK is the first person to walk all of the Amazon River.
He started where the river begins in the Andes mountains in Peru.
He finished where the river ends in Brazil.
This took him two years and four months. He walked 6,000 kilometres.
The Amazon rainforest has dangerous snakes, crocodiles, and jaguars.
So, it was very dangerous for Ed.
Luckily, he was okay. He only got many mosquito and ant bites.
reference: Ed Stafford is from the UK. He is the first person to walk along the Amazon River. He started in the Andes mountains in Peru and finished in Brazil. The journey took two years and four months, and he walked 6,000 kilometres. The Amazon rainforest is dangerous. There are snakes with poison, big crocodiles, and jaguars. Ed was in danger, but he only got bitten by mosquitoes and ants.

original: Businesses have caught on to the profitability of the sharing economy and are seeking to gain from making use of those underutilised resources. A business model that has rapidly risen in popularity sees companies providing an online platform that puts customers in contact with those who can provide a particular product or service. Companies like Airbnb act as a middleman for people to cash in on their unused rooms and houses and let them out as lucrative accommodation. Another example is Uber, which encourages people to use their own personal cars as taxis to make some extra cash in their free time.
simplified:
Companies see they can make money from things people don't use much.

Many companies now use a website or app. This helps people find others who can give them a product or service.

For example, Airbnb helps people make money from their empty rooms and houses. They rent them out.

Uber is another example. People can use their own cars like taxis. They earn extra money when they are free.
reference: Many businesses know they can make money from the sharing economy. This means using things that people are not using all the time. One idea is to make a website or app to connect people who can provide a service. For example, Airbnb helps people rent out their free rooms or houses to travellers. Another example is Uber. It lets people use their own cars as taxis and earn some extra cash.

original: In Britain, the average person spends more than £1,000 on new clothes a year, which is around four per cent of their income. That might not sound like much, but that figure hides two far more worrying trends for society and for the environment. First, a lot of that consumer spending is via credit cards. British people currently owe approximately £670 per adult to credit card companies. That's 66 per cent of the average wardrobe budget. Also, not only are people spending money they don't have, they're using it to buy things they don't need. Britain throws away 300,000 tons of clothing a year, most of which goes into landfill sites.
simplified:
In Britain, people spend over £1,000 on new clothes each year. This is about 4% of their money.

This may not seem like a lot. But there are two big problems for people and for nature.

First, people buy many clothes with credit cards. Each adult in Britain owes about £670 to banks for credit cards. This is 66% of the money they spend on clothes.

People spend money they do not have. They buy things they do not need.

Britain throws away 300,000 tons of clothes every year. Most of these clothes go to big rubbish dumps.
reference: In Britain, people spend more than £1,000 on clothes each year. This is about four per cent of the money they earn. It looks fine, but there are big problems. Many people use credit cards to buy clothes. On average, each adult owes £670 to the credit card companies. This is about two-thirds of what they spend on clothes. People also buy clothes they do not need. Every year, Britain throws away 300,000 tons of clothes, and most of it goes to rubbish places called landfills.

original: Maybe dreams are the result of our mind organising the thoughts we have during the day, but they appear in dreams with symbolic meaning. When we're awake, our thoughts mostly appear in our minds as words, like conversations we have with ourselves. But when we're asleep, the part of our brain that controls language becomes less active while the part that controls emotions becomes more active.
simplified:
Dreams might be our brain sorting thoughts from the day. But in dreams, these thoughts have a special meaning.

When we are awake, we think in words. It's like we talk to ourselves.

But when we sleep, the part of our brain for words works less. The part for feelings works more.
reference: Dreams might come from our minds, putting our daily thoughts in order. In dreams, these thoughts often look like symbols, not clear words. When we are awake, we usually think in words, like talking to ourselves. But when we sleep, the part for language rests, and the part for feelings are more active.

original: Ed's walk would have been impossible without technology. He used a radio to ask the people of the rainforest for food and permission to cross their land. Many of them came to meet him and helped guide him through the most difficult terrain. As he walked Ed wrote a blog, recording his day-to-day experiences. He used the media interest in his trip to protest about the destruction of the rainforest and raise money for environmental and children's charities in Brazil and Peru.
simplified:
