Ed could not walk without technology. He used a radio to ask people in the forest for food. He also asked to walk on their land. Many people came to see him. They helped him find the way in hard places.

When he walked, Ed wrote a blog. He wrote about his days. The news talked about his trip. Ed used this to say people were cutting down the forest. He also got money for groups that help nature and children in Brazil and Peru.
reference: Ed finished his walk with the help of technology. He had a radio to talk to people in the rainforest. He asked them for food and to let him cross their land. Some people came to meet him and showed him the way through hard places. As he walked, Ed wrote a blog about his days. He used the media's interest in his trip. He used this to tell people about the cutting of the rainforest and to raise money for charities for nature and children in Brazil and Peru.

original: Dogs that live in packs have learnt that humans are more likely to give food to smaller, cuter dogs so those dogs are sent to beg for food for the whole pack. Some dogs have even learnt to use the city's metro system to get from one part of their territory to another! Scientists are not sure how the dogs know when to get off the train. One idea is that they use their excellent sense of smell and have learnt to recognise the scents of their favourite destinations. Another possibility is that they have learnt to recognise the names of stations they hear in announcements. Either way, metro passengers have now got so used to the sight of dogs on the trains that they travel largely unnoticed by locals.
simplified:
Dogs in groups learn that people give food to small, cute dogs. So, these dogs go to get food for their group.

Some dogs can even use the city metro. They go to different places in their area. Scientists don't know how dogs know when to get off the train.

Maybe they use their good nose and learn the smell of places they like. Or maybe they learn the names of stations from sounds on the train.

People on the metro are used to seeing dogs. So, they don't really notice them now.
reference: Dogs that live in groups know that people give food more easily to small, cute dogs. So the group sends those dogs to ask for food. Some dogs can even use the city metro to go from one place to another! Scientists do not know how they know when to get off the train. Maybe they use their strong smell to know their favourite places. Or maybe they listen to the names of the stations. Today, people on the metro are so used to the dogs.

original: Both of these kinds of accidents are extremely rare, but boats and trains can cause a bridge to collapse for different reasons. With trains, it's the velocity of the impact that can bring a bridge down. With boats, it's the very large mass they have that can bring about the collapse, even if they are moving very slowly when it occurs. The best way to avoid bridge failures is to plan for them. Modern technologies that can detect structural weakness, safer working environments and better designs can all help to reduce these terrible accidents.
simplified:
These accidents do not happen often. But boats and trains can make a bridge fall down for different reasons.

Trains can make a bridge fall if they hit it very fast. Boats are very big and heavy. This can make a bridge fall, even if the boat moves slowly.

To stop bridges from falling, we should plan. New tools can find weak parts. Safer work places and better plans can help stop these bad accidents.
reference: Accidents with bridges do not happen often. But sometimes trains or boats can make a bridge fall. A fast train crash can break a bridge. A boat is very heavy, so even a slow boat can make a bridge collapse. The best way to stop this is to plan good. New technology can find weak parts of a bridge. Safer building work and better designs can also help prevent these accidents.

original: At first, Pi is terrified of the animals and jumps into the ocean. Then he remembers that there are hungry sharks in the water around him and realises his only option is to climb back into the lifeboat. One by one, the animals in the lifeboat kill and eat each other, till only Pi and the tiger are left. Fortunately for Pi, the tiger, who he names Richard Parker, is seasick and has no immediate interest in eating him.
simplified:
First, Pi is very scared of the animals. He jumps into the sea.
Then he remembers there are hungry sharks in the water. He knows he must go back to the lifeboat.
The animals in the lifeboat fight. They eat each other.
Only Pi and the tiger are left.
Luckily for Pi, the tiger is sick from the sea. Pi calls the tiger Richard Parker.
The tiger does not want to eat Pi now.
reference: First, Pi is afraid of the animals and jumps into the sea. But there are sharks in the water, so he must go back to the lifeboat. In the boat, the animals fights. They kill and eat each other. Soon, only pi and a tiger are left. Pi names the tiger Richard Parker. The tiger feels sick from the sea, so he does not want to eat Pi yet.

original: When Pi is 16, a new government is elected that his parents don't support. Worried about the future, Pi's parents decide to close the zoo and emigrate to Canada. Some of the animals are sold to zoos in North America and the family travel by ship to Canada taking the animals with them. On the way, there is a terrible storm and the ship sinks. Tragically, Pi's family and the ship's sailors all drown, but Pi finds himself in a lifeboat with a hyena, zebra, orang-utan and an enormous tiger.
simplified: When Pi is 16, a new government starts. His parents do not like it. They are worried. So, Pi's parents close their zoo. They move to Canada. They sell some animals to other zoos. The family goes to Canada by ship. They take some animals with them. On the way, there is a big storm. The ship sinks. Pi's family and the sailors die. But Pi is in a small boat. He is with a hyena, a zebra, an orangutan, and a very big tiger.
reference: When Pi is 16, a new government starts in his country. His parents do not like it and are worried about the future. They decide to close their zoo and move to Canada. Some animals are sold to zoos in North America, and the family takes the other animals on a ship. On the trip, there is a big storm. The ship sinks. Sadly, Pi's family and the sailors die. Pi is alone in a lifeboat with a hyena, a zebra, an orang-utan, and a very big tiger.

original: The rover analyses the air around it periodically, and in 2014 it found the air contained another of the most basic organic molecules and a key ingredient of natural gas: methane. One of the characteristics of methane is that it only survives a few hundred years. This means that something, somewhere on Mars, is replenishing the supply. According to NASA, Mars emits thousands of tons of methane at a time. The level of methane rises and falls at seasonal intervals in the year, almost as if the planet is breathing it.
simplified:
The rover looks at the air. In 2014, it found methane. Methane is a simple gas, like in natural gas.

Methane only stays for a few hundred years. So, something on Mars makes more methane.

NASA says Mars sends out a lot of methane.

The amount of methane goes up and down with the seasons. It is like the planet is breathing.
reference: The rover tests the air on Mars from time to time. In 2014, it found methane. Methane is a simple organic molecule and is also in natural gas. Methane cannot stay long, so something on Mars is making more of it. NASA says Mars gives out thousands of tons of methane at a time. The amount of methane changes with the seasons, like the planet is breathing.

original: One of the most important modern functions of zoos is supporting international breeding programmes, particularly for endangered species. In the wild, some of the rarest species have difficulty in finding mates and breeding, and they might also be threatened by poachers, loss of their habitat and predators. A good zoo will enable these species to live and breed in a secure environment. In addition, as numbers of some wild species drop, there is an increased danger of populations becoming too genetically similar. Breeding programmes provide a safeguard: zoo-bred animals can be released into the wild to increase genetic diversity.
simplified:
Zoos have an important job today. They help animals have babies. This is especially for animals that are in danger.

In nature, it is hard for rare animals to find partners and have babies. Bad people hunt them. Their homes can disappear. Other animals might eat them.

A good zoo helps these animals live and have babies in a safe place.

Also, when there are fewer wild animals, they can become too much alike. This is not good for them.

Zoos help with this problem. Animals born in zoos can go back to nature. This makes the animal groups stronger.
reference: Zoos has an important role. They help animals that are endangered, which means very few in the world, by running breeding programmes. In the wild, rare animals often cannot find a mate to have babies. They can also be killed by hunters, lose their homes, and be eaten by other animals. In a good zoo, they can live safely and have babies. When the number of wild animals gets very small, they can become too similar in their genes. Breeding in zoos helps this. Later, the young animals can go back to the wild and make the group stronger.

original: No matter what kind of house it is, the basement is a scary place in horror films. That's usually where something is hiding or where the evil psychopath has hidden their tools. Basements are always dark and often damp. You can only reach them by a narrow staircase. And basements are always creepy, even when there isn't anything down there.
simplified: In scary movies, basements are scary places. Often, something hides there. Or a bad person hides their tools there. Basements are always dark and often wet. You go down small stairs to get there. Basements are always a bit scary, even if nothing is there.
reference: In horror films, the basement is always a scary place. It doesn't matter what house it is. Often, something is hiding there, or a bad person hides their tools. Basement are dark and sometimes wet. You can go down a small staircase to reach them. Even when they are empty, basements feel creepy.

original: The Hunger Games is a hugely successful book for teenagers and young adults by the American author Suzanne Collins. Since it was published in 2008 it has been translated into 26 different languages and has sold millions of copies around the world. It is also the first book for young readers to sell more than a million electronic copies. The Hunger Games is now a major Hollywood film and is just as successful. It made 152.5 million dollars in its opening weekend in North America alone!
simplified:
The Hunger Games is a very popular book for young people. Suzanne Collins from America wrote it.

It came out in 2008. You can read it in 26 languages. Millions of people around the world bought it. It was the first book for young people to sell over a million e-books.

Now, The Hunger Games is also a big movie from Hollywood. It is very popular too. In its first weekend, it made 152.5 million dollars. This was only in North America!
reference: The Hunger Games is a very popular book for teenagers and young adults. It was written by Suzanne Collins, an American writer. The book came out in 2008. It has been translated into 26 languages and has sold millions of copies around the world. It is also the first book for young people to sell over one million electronic copies. Later, it became a Hollywood film. The movie is also a big success and made 152.5 million dollars in North America in the first weekend.

original: Having good relationships is a big part of being happy. In one study, most happy people were found to have strong ties to friends and family and they made sure they spent time with them regularly. You also need at least one person who you discuss personal feelings with – called 'self-disclosure'. Just one person for a heart-to-heart is enough, together with a network of other relationships. It's not enough to have lots of friends just to do things with or chat to about music or football. That deeper connection is all-important. Some people need to learn how to listen effectively to others in order to develop stronger relationships.
simplified:
Good friends make you happy.
A study says happy people have good friends and family. They spend time with them often.
You also need one person to talk about your feelings with. One person to talk about everything with is good. You can have other friends too.
It's not enough to just have friends for fun, like talking about music or sports. A real friendship is very important.
Some people need to learn to listen well. This helps them make better friends.
reference: Good relationships help us to be happy. A study showed that happy people usually have close family and friends, and they visit them often. You also need at least one person to share your personal feelings with. It is called 'self-disclosure'. One close friend for deep talks is enough, together with other friends. It is not enough to only have many friends to chat with about music or football. What is important is a deeper connection. Some people also need to learn to listen to others to make stronger friendships.

original: It was a fascinating talk and the speaker really hit the nail on the head with a couple of things. Take parental influence, for instance. How can we expect teenagers not to text while doing their homework when they witness their parents posting on social media while cooking the evening meal or waiting at a red light? She also made a valid point about people wanting to be in two or several places at once. So they switch back and forth between their real-life and online conversations. I see it all the time with my teenage daughter and her friends. They arrange to meet and then sit together in silence while each one engages in a different conversation online.
simplified:
The talk was good. The speaker said some true things.

For example, about parents. How can we think teenagers will not text when they do homework? Their parents use social media when they cook dinner or wait in the car.

The speaker also said something true. People want to do many things at the same time. So they talk to people here and also talk to people online.

I see this often with my daughter and her friends. They meet. Then they sit together and do not talk. Each one talks to different people online.
reference: The talk was very interesting, and the speaker said some important things. One example was about the example of parents. Teenagers see their parents using social media while cooking or waiting for a red light, so how can we expect teenagers not to text while doing homework? The speaker also said that people want to be in two places at once. They change between real life and online talks. I see this with my teenage daughter and her friends. They meet together, but then they sit quietly, each one busy with a different online chat.

original: Early in her career, the psychologist Carol Dweck of Stanford University gave a group of ten-year-olds problems that were slightly too hard for them. One group reacted positively, said they loved challenge and understood that their abilities could be developed. She says they had a 'growth mindset' and are focused on what they can achieve in the future. But another group of children felt that their intelligence was being judged and they had failed. They had a 'fixed mindset' and were unable to imagine improving. Some of these children said they might cheat in the future; others looked for someone who had done worse than them to boost their self-esteem.
simplified:
Carol Dweck, a smart lady, gave some 10-year-old children hard puzzles.

One group was happy. They liked hard things and knew they could get better. She called this a 'growth mindset'. These children thought about what they could do later.

But another group felt bad. They thought people were judging them. They felt they failed. She called this a 'fixed mindset'. They did not think they could get better. Some children said they might cheat next time. Others looked for someone who did worse than them to feel better.
reference: When Carol Dweck started her work as a psychologist at Stanford University, she gave some ten-year-old children some easy problems. One group of children reacted well. They liked the challenge and believed they could learn more in the future. Dweck called this a 'growth mindset'. But the other group felt bad. They thought the problems showed they were not smart, and they could not imagine improving. Dweck called this a 'fixed mindset'. Some children with this mindset said they might cheat next time, and others tried to feel better by looking at kids who did worse than they.

original: Gary Collins, an off-duty policeman, was watching the London riots on TV. He immediately recognised several people and cut his holiday short to help with identification. He ended up spending six months going through the CCTV film and managed to identify 190 people, many from their eyes alone. His help was of decisive importance in the investigation. Even with 200,000 hours of footage, facial recognition software managed to identify just one person.
simplified: Gary Collins is a policeman. He was at home and watched the London riots on TV. He saw some people he knew. So, he stopped his holiday early to help. He spent six months watching camera videos. He found 190 people. He knew many just from their eyes. His help was very important for the police. There were 200,000 hours of video, but a computer program only found one person.
reference: Gary Collins, a policeman on holiday, was watching the London street fight on TV. He saw some people he knew and stopped his holiday to help. In six months, he studied CCTV videos and found 190 people, many just by looking at their eyes. His help was very important in the police work. The computer software for face identification only found one person in 200,000 hours of film.

original: In an attempt to inject some positivity into their feedback, many managers rely on sandwiching negative feedback between two positive comments. However, when feedback becomes such a routine, employees can start to perceive positive feedback as simply a form of sugarcoating the negatives, thus diminishing its value. Instead, positive feedback should not simply be seen as something to cushion the negative, but should be delivered so as to reinforce and encourage good performance.
simplified:
Managers often try to make feedback sound nice. They say something good, then something bad, then something good again.

But workers learn this trick. Then they think the good words are not real. They think the manager is just hiding the bad news.

Good words should help people do good work. They should not just hide bad news.
reference: Some managers give feedback in a "sandwich" format. They say something good, then something bad, and then something good again. But if they do this too many times, workers may think the good things are fake. They may also think the good ones are there to hide the bad ones. This makes the good feedback weak. Positive feedback should be real. It should help workers feel proud and keep doing the good work.

original: Personally, I think it's fascinating to consider how we'll speed up our evolution as a species by augmenting our bodies. Imagine if you could implant a computer inside our brain! Soon we'll be able to do just that and enhance our mathematical ability, audiovisual perception and our memory, and this idea is only going to become more and more commonplace.
simplified: I think it's interesting how we can make people better. Imagine putting a computer in your head! Soon we can do this. We can make our math skills better, see and hear better, and remember more. Many people will think this is normal.
reference: I think it exciting to think about how people can change with technology. One day, we might put a computer inside the brain. This could help us be better at maths, see and hear better, and remember more things. In the future, this idea will be more common.

original: The majority of people believe that developing countries are in a terrible situation: suffering from incredible poverty, governed by dictators and with little hope for any meaningful change. But, surprisingly, this is far from the truth. The reality is that a great transformation is occurring. Over the past 20 years, more than 700 million people have increased their income and come out of poverty. Additionally, six million fewer children die every year from disease, millions more girls are in school and millions of people have access to clean water.
simplified:
Many people think poor countries are in a bad situation. They think these countries are very poor, have bad leaders, and things will not get better.

But this is not true. A big change is happening.

In the last 20 years, 700 million people got more money and are not poor anymore. Also, every year, 6 million fewer children die from sickness. Many more girls go to school. And many people have clean water.
reference: Most people believe that poor countries have no hope. They think these countries only have poverty, bad leaders, and no change. But this is not true. A big change is happening. In the past 20 years, 700 million people got more money and are no longer poor. Every year, six million fewer children die from illness. More gilrls go to school now, and people can drink clean water.

original: Horror films love uninhabited places. This could be an abandoned hospital, a scary empty house or a ghost town. There's something about lonely, empty places. What was it like when people lived there? Why did they leave? Maybe it's also that they are so quiet, which can be very scary too. Of course, abandoned places are also handy for horror film directors in that it's more believable that you will have no phone coverage there either.
simplified:
Scary movies like places with no people.
For example, an old hospital, an empty house, or a town with no one.
These empty places feel strange.
What was it like when people lived there? Why did they leave?
Also, these places are very quiet. This can be scary.
Empty places are good for people who make scary movies. It is easy to believe your phone will not work there.
reference: Horror films often happen in empty places. They can be an old hospital, a house or a town without people. Empty places make us think what it was like when people lived there? Why did they leave? These places are also very quiet and scary. For film directors, such places are good too, as it makes sense that there is no phone signal.

original: Psychologist and 'growth mindset' proponent Carol Dweck spoke of the plasticity of the brain and our ability to develop skills and talents that we might not have been good at to start with. Many of us tend to focus our praise on the end result and seemingly innate talents, e.g. 'You really have an eye for details' or 'You have a real talent for organising events'. However, research suggests that by focusing on the process of how things are done – praising effort, experimentation and problem-solving strategies – we can encourage the development of new skills and the continued honing of talents.
simplified:
Carol Dweck is a scientist. She says our brain can change. This means we can learn new things. We can get better at things we were not good at before.

Often, we say "good job" when someone finishes something. We praise natural skills. For example, "You are good at seeing small things" or "You are good at planning parties."

But studies show something different. If we praise *how* people work – like trying hard, trying new ways, or finding answers to problems – they learn more. They get even better at their skills.
reference: Psychologist Carol Dweck talks about the 'growth mindset'. This means the brain can change, and we can learn skills even if we are not good at them at the start. Often, people give praise only for the final result or for natural talent. For example: "You notice small details well" or "You are good at organising events." But research shows it is better to praise the way people work. Saying something like "Good effort" or "Good for trying new ideas" helps people learn new skills and improve their talents.

original: I'm a member of the Campaign to Stop Killer Robots. Forget the movie image of a terrifying Terminator stamping on human skulls and think of what's happening right now: military machines like drones, gun turrets and sentry robots are already being used to kill with very little human input. The next step will be autonomous 'murderbots', following orders but ultimately deciding who to kill on their own. It seems clear to me that this would be completely unethical and dangerous for humanity. We need to be very cautious indeed about what we ask machines to do.
simplified:
I am in a group that wants to stop killer robots.
Don't think about scary robots from movies.
Real army machines like drones and robots with guns already kill people. People do not control them much.
Soon, robots will choose who to kill by themselves.
This is very bad and dangerous for all people.
We must be very careful with what we let machines do.
reference: I belong to the Campaign to Stop Killer Robots. Don't think about movie robots like the Terminator. Think about this now: armies already use machines like drones, big guns, and guard robots to kill with little help from people. The next step may be "murderbots". These are robots that take orders but then choose for themselves who to kill. I think this is very bad and dangous for people. We must be very careful about what we make the machine do.

original: Your manager stops you and says she needs to have a word about your performance in the recent project. You worry about it all weekend, wondering what you might have done wrong. When you step into her office on Monday morning she begins by praising you for the good work you've done on the project, and you wonder if this is the obligatory praise that starts off the typical 'feedback sandwich'. You know how the feedback sandwich goes: say something nice, say what you really want to say, say something nice again.
simplified:
Your boss stops you. She wants to talk about your work on the last project.
You feel bad all weekend. You think: "What did I do wrong?"
On Monday, you go to her office. She says your work was good.
You think: "Is this the start of the 'feedback sandwich'?"
You know what a 'feedback sandwich' is. First, they say something good. Then, they say the bad thing. Then, they say something good again.
reference: Your manager tells you she wants to talk to you about your work on the last project. You feel worried all weekend and think you may have done something wrong. On Monday, you go to her office. She begins by saying good things about your work. You are not sure if this is the "feedback sandwich." The feedback sandwich is when someone says something good, then says something bad, and then says something good to finish.

original: Wasfia has dedicated her life to supporting human rights and has witnessed numerous international humanitarian projects in her homeland to educate and train women and girls, but once too often they have been left with nothing when such projects have stopped running. Wasfia saw that Bangladesh needed to stand up for itself and so she brought together two of her passions, mountaineering and human rights, in order to try and change attitudes towards women in her country. She originally took up climbing while working on humanitarian campaigns in Tibet and Nepal, as in a coastal, primarily flat country like Bangladesh most people have never set eyes on a mountain. Her campaign seems to be doing the trick as fellow countrymen and women are sitting up and taking notice along with the rest of the world.
simplified:
Wasfia helps people. She saw many projects in her country. These projects taught women and girls. But often, when these projects finished, the women had nothing.

Wasfia thought Bangladesh needed to do more for itself. She loved climbing mountains and helping people. She used both to make things better for women in her country.

She started climbing when she worked in Tibet and Nepal. Bangladesh is flat, near the sea. Most people there have never seen a mountain.

Her work is helping. People in her country are paying attention. People around the world are also paying attention.
reference: Wasfia works hard to help people protect human rights. In Bangladesh, some projects came to teach and help women and girls, but when the projects stopped, they were left with nothing. Wasfia wanted her country to be strong on its own. She used her two passions, climbing mountains and human rights, to change how people see women. She first climbed mountains in Tibet and Nepal, because in Bangladesh, there are no mountains, only flat land near the sea. Her work is now successful. People in Bangladesh and in other countries are paying attention.

original: This horror film cliché was especially popular with horror films of the late 20th century. It starts with a group of teenagers all enjoying themselves, and it ends with everyone dead except one girl. At the beginning the girl is usually innocent, shy and not particularly strong. By the end, she has become the toughest and most resourceful person in the world. The last girl almost always wins in the end.
simplified: This is a common story in old horror films. It starts with young people having fun. Then, everyone dies, but one girl lives. At first, the girl is good, quiet, and not strong. But at the end, she is very strong and smart. This girl usually wins.
reference: This type of movie was very common in the late 20th century. At the beginning, many teenagers are having fun. At the end, only one girl is still active. At first, the girl is shy, quiet and not strong. But later, she becames brave and clever. In the end, the "last girl" usually wins.

original: A fast-paced, foot-tapping rock album, Born in the USA's lyrics nevertheless carry emotional weight. Behind the catchy rock melodies that drive these powerhouse classics are stories of the dark side of the American dream. Many tracks deal with the struggles of hard-working ordinary people and the bitterness and anger they feel as life doesn't bring them riches or glory. The song Glory Days, for example, is about people in a small town looking back at when they were young and had the world at their feet while Downbound Train tells the story of a young man whose life is ruined when he loses his job. It's not hard to imagine that the artist is channelling real people he knew and the life he might have had if he hadn't become a star. The album will leave you in no doubt of the unique and extraordinary talent of the Boss.
simplified:
"Born in the USA" is a fast rock album. You will want to tap your feet. But the songs also have strong feelings.

The music is catchy. But the songs tell sad stories about the American dream. Many songs are about normal people who work hard. They have problems. They feel sad and angry because they don't get rich or famous.

For example, "Glory Days" is about people in a small town. They remember when they were young and life was good. "Downbound Train" is about a young man. He loses his job, and his life becomes bad.

The singer knew these people. Maybe he sings about his own life if he was not famous. This album shows that the singer is very good. He is a great artist.
reference: Born in the USA is a rock album with fast music that makes you want to move, but the words of the songs are serious. They tell stories about the hard side of the American dream. Many songs are about working people who try hard but do not get rich or famous. For example, Glory Days is about people in a small town remembering when they were young, and Downbound Train is about a young man who loses his job and his life becomes sad. The singer seems to sing about real people he knew, and the life he might have had if he were not a star. The album shows that "the Boss" has special talent.

original: Best-selling author Terrie Sharp knows how to tell a good story or two, having twice won the Olive Crime Writer Award. Born on the housing estate with the highest crime rate in Glasgow, she learned to keep quiet, stay out of trouble and how to open car doors with a knife. Luckily, she only used her knowledge to write her novels and she's not so quiet these days, appearing on popular daytime shows like Police Today and at writing conferences throughout the UK.
simplified:
Terrie Sharp writes popular books. She is good at telling stories. She won an award two times.

She grew up in Glasgow in an area with a lot of crime. She learned to be quiet and stay safe. She also learned to open car doors with a knife.

But she only used these skills for her books. Now she talks a lot. She is on TV shows like Police Today and goes to writing events in the UK.
reference: Terrie Sharp is a very popular writer, and her books sell well. She has won the Olive Crime Writer Award two times. She was born in Glasgow, a place with a lot of crime. As a child, she learned to be quiet, stay safe, and even how to open car doors with a knife. Luckily, she only used this for her stories. Now she is not quiet, she goes on TV shows like Police Today and gives talks at writing conferences in the UK.

original: Overall, more people are learning English than the other languages combined and English is spoken in the highest number of countries. However, Chinese has by far the greatest number of native speakers. There seems to be little correlation between how many native speakers there are of a language and the number of learners, but there is a stronger link between the number of learners and how many countries have speakers.
simplified:
Many people learn English. English is used in more countries than any other language.

But more people speak Chinese as their first language.

The number of people who speak a language from birth does not really affect how many people learn it. But if a language is used in many countries, more people learn it.
reference: Today, more people learn English than all other languages. English is also spoken in most countries. But Chinese has the most native speakers, which means people who speak it from birth. There is no big link between the number of native speakers and learners. But there is a stronger link between the number of learners and how many countries speak that language.

original: In older horror films, when protagonists were in desperation, it was difficult or impossible for them to call for help or call the police. Mobile phones have made that situation a bit less believable now. What's the solution to maintain suspense? No phone coverage! If you're a hero in a horror film, it's almost certain that at a key moment, just when you absolutely need to call for help, you will not have any coverage at all. Or your phone battery will die just as you are making the call. Or both.
simplified:
In old scary movies, people in danger could not call for help.
Now, we have phones, so this is not very real.
How do movies stay scary?
No phone signal!
If you are the hero in a scary movie, you need to call for help.
But your phone will not work.
Or your phone battery will die when you call.
Sometimes, both happen.
reference: In old horror films, the main characters could not easily call for help or the police. But now people have mobile phones, so this problem looks less true. How do films keep the story scary? The answer is no phone signal! In many horror films, when the hero really needs to call, there is no signal. Or the phone battery dies while they are calling. Sometimes both happen.

original: Don't always follow positive feedback with negative feedback. When positive and negative feedback always appear to go hand in hand, the positives can become devalued and ignored. Ensure there are times when positive feedback is given for its own sake and resist the temptation to offer constructive criticism.
simplified:
Don't always say good things and then bad things.
If you always say good and bad things together, people might not think the good things are important. They might not listen.
Sometimes, just say good things. Don't always try to say how to make it better.
reference: Do not always say something bad after saying something good. If good and bad comments always come together, the good words may not feel real. Sometimes, give good feedback only, and try not to add any criticism.

original: In the 1950s, Central American commercial banana growers were facing the death of their most lucrative product, the Gros Michel banana, known as Big Mike. And now it's happening again to Big Mike's successor – the Cavendish. With its easily transported, thick-skinned and sweet-tasting fruit, the Gros Michel banana plant dominated the plantations of Central America. United Fruit, the main grower and exporter in South America at the time, mass-produced its bananas in the most efficient way possible: it cloned shoots from the stems of plants instead of growing plants from seeds, and cultivated them in densely packed fields.
simplified:
In the 1950s, banana farmers in Central America had a big problem. Their best banana, called Big Mike, was dying.

Now, the new banana, Cavendish, has the same problem.

Big Mike was good. It was easy to move. It had thick skin and tasted sweet. Many people grew it in Central America.

A big company called United Fruit grew many bananas. They grew them fast. They used parts of plants, not seeds. They grew many plants very close together.
reference: In the 1950s, banana farmers in Central America had a big problem. Their best banana, called Gros Michel or Big Mike, was dying. Now the same problem is happening to its replacement, the Cavendish. Big Mike was very popular because it was sweet, had a thick skin, and was easy to carry and sell. United Fruit, the biggest company, grew these bananas by taking shoots from the plant stems instead of seeds. They planted the bananas very close to each other in larger fields.

original: It is society, not nature, that tells us girls should favour arts and humanities and leave maths and physics to the boys. Coupled with this is the lack of positive female role models youngsters see doing science-related jobs. Cartoons and stories often show the crazy scientist, genius inventor, or adventurous astronaut as a man. Furthermore, there is an unfortunate perception that scientists are geeky, have poor social skills or that their work is lonely and detached from the rest of the world. These are false stereotypes portrayed by the media, but they may mean that girls do not identify with scientists, and see science as an unappealing career path. If girls saw more positive female role models in science it would give them more confidence and a greater sense of belonging in those subjects.
simplified:
People tell girls to like art, not science. Boys like science. This is not right.

Girls don't see many women who work in science. TV shows and books often show men as scientists.

Some people think scientists are strange. They think scientists don't talk to many people or work alone.

These ideas are not true. Girls might not want to be scientists because of this. They think science is not a good job for them.

If girls saw more women in science, they would feel more confident. They would feel like they belong in science.
reference: Society tells us that girls should choose arts and humanities, and boys should choose maths and physics. Another problem is that children do not often see women working in science. In cartoons and stories, the scientist, inventor, or astronaut is usually a man. People also think scientists are strange, not good at talking to others, or always working alone. These ideas are not true, but they can make girls feel that science is not for them. If girls saw more women in science, they would feel more confident and feel that they belong in those subjects.

original: Spider venom is present in most species and serves the purpose of stunning or killing their prey rather than attacking humans. In fact, only 25 of the known spider species produce venom which can actually harm humans, and although spider bites can be painful, they are rarely deadly. Australia's notorious Sydney funnel-web spider has not produced any fatalities since anti-venom was developed in 1981. However, take care not to rub hairy spiders like tarantulas up the wrong way. When they feel in danger, they defend themselves by ejecting a cloud of urticating hairs. These irritating hairs then embed themselves in the skin or eyes of the attacker.
simplified:
Most spiders have poison. They use it to catch food, not to hurt people.

Only 25 kinds of spiders have poison that can hurt people. Spider bites can hurt, but they almost never kill people.

The Sydney funnel-web spider in Australia is famous. No one has died from its bite since 1981. That was when doctors made special medicine for its bite.

But be careful with hairy spiders like tarantulas. Don't make them angry. If they feel scared, they throw out many small, sharp hairs. These hairs can stick in your skin or eyes.
reference: Most spiders have venom, but it is for catching food, not for hurting people. Only about 25 kinds of spiders can harm humans. A spider bite can be painful, but it rarely kills. In Australia, the Sydney funnel-web spider has not killed anyone since doctors made an anti-venom in 1981. But be careful with hairy spiders like tarantulas. If they feel danger, they throw out tiny hairs. These hairs can get into your skin or eyes and make them very sore.

original: Lewis would like to see the number of marine protected areas in the world increase from 3 per cent to 10 per cent in an attempt to reverse the damage caused by human activity such as overfishing, polluting and littering. During his expeditions, Lewis has witnessed this environmental destruction first-hand. He's swum over coral reefs bleached by the increase in water temperature, and observed underwater deserts beneath the shallow waters of the Red Sea, devoid of life and strewn with plastic. Pugh believes that nature can recover if it is given space to do so, but the clock is ticking. If we don't start looking after our seas, we may soon have an unsolvable problem on our hands.
simplified:
Lewis wants more safe places in the sea. Now, 3% of the sea is safe. He wants 10% to be safe. This will help fix problems caused by people. For example, too much fishing, dirty water, and rubbish.

When Lewis travels, he has seen this harm to nature with his own eyes. He swam over coral reefs. They were white because the water was too hot. He also saw places under the water like deserts. In the Red Sea, where the water is not deep, he saw no life. There was a lot of plastic.

Pugh thinks nature can get better if we give it room. But time is short. If we don't start taking care of our seas, we will soon have a problem we cannot fix.
reference: Lewis wants more parts of the sea to be protected. At the moment, only 3% is protected, and he wants this to be 10%. He hopes this will help fix the damage people cause, like too much fishing, pollution, and rubbish in the sea. On his trips, Lewis saw this damage himself. He swam over coral that had lost its colour because the water was too hot. In the Red Sea, he saw places with no fish, but plastic. Pugh believes nature can heal if we give it space, but we must do it quickly. If we do not take care of the sea now, it may soon be too late.

original: At Girox Foods, we are experiencing an annual employee turnover of about 12 per cent. Although this might not seem high at first glance, the industry standard is seven per cent. The principal objective of this report is to investigate the causes of employee engagement within the firm and, based on those, offer recommendations to improve the employees' experience of the workplace and increase employee retention.
simplified: At Girox Foods, 12% of our staff leave their jobs each year. This is more than other companies, where only 7% leave. This report will find out why staff leave or stay. Then, it will give ideas to make work better and help more staff stay.
reference: At Girox Foods, around 12% of workers leave the company every year. This looks small, but in the same industry, the normal number is only 7%. The goal of this report is to look at why workers feel they belong in the company and then give ideas to make the workplace better. The goal is that this will help more workers stay in the job.

original: As for news stories that make us think the world is an increasingly violent place, there is cause for some optimism too. Between the end of World War II and 1990, there were 30 wars that killed more than 100,000 people. Today there are still civil wars, but countries are mostly co-existing more peacefully than in the past. However, terrorism has shot up in the last few years and, since World War II, wars have killed many more civilians than soldiers. Even for civilians, though, the statistics are not all bad. Although deaths are nine times more likely to be a result of violent crime than political conflict, the global murder rate fell slightly, from 8 per 100,000 people in 2000 to about 5.3 in 2015.
simplified:
News makes us think the world is very violent. But there is also good news.

After World War II, until 1990, there were 30 big wars. Many people died. Today, there are still wars inside some countries. But most countries live together more peacefully now.

However, there is more terrorism today. Wars also kill more normal people than soldiers.

But for normal people, it is not all bad. More people die from crime than from wars. But fewer people are murdered now. In 2000, 8 people out of 100,000 were murdered. In 2015, this number was 5.3.
reference: The news often makes us think the world is getting more violent, but there is some hope. Between the end of World War II and 1990, 30 wars killed more than 100,000 people each. Today, there are still civil wars, but many countries live more peacefully than before. Terrorism has grown in the last years, and since World War II, wars have killed more peopl than soldiers. But not all statistics are bad. People are nine times more likely to die from violent crime than from war, but the world murder rate has gone down, from 8 per 100,000 people in 2000 to about 5.3 in 2015.

original: The Scallion is printed weekly and distributed free in faculty buildings, with a readership of approximately 10,000 students. It is written and produced entirely by students. The survey shows that the newspaper is highly valued by university students and staff for entertainment, cultural enrichment and work experience. The cost of printing newspapers is significant. Furthermore, some students do not have easy access to the paper, since the only way to obtain a copy is to physically go to university. An additional environmental issue is that a large number of copies end up as litter on campus.
simplified:
The Scallion is a newspaper. It comes out every week. It is free. You can find it in university buildings. About 10,000 students read it. Students write and make the newspaper.

People say students and teachers like the newspaper a lot. They like it for fun, to learn new things, and for students to get work experience.

Printing the newspapers costs a lot of money. Also, some students cannot get the paper easily. They must go to the university to get one. It is also bad for the environment. Many papers are left on the ground at the university.
reference: The Scallion is a student newspaper. It is printed every week and given out free in university buildings. Around 10,000 students read it. Students write and produce the paper. A survey says students and teachers like it for fun, culture, and work experience. But printing costs a lot. Some students cannot get the paper easily, as they have to go to the university to take a copy. There is also an environmental problem: many copies are left as rubbish on campus.

original: Are things getting worse every day? Is progress an impossible goal? In Enlightenment Now, Steven Pinker looks at the big picture of human progress and finds good news. We are living longer, healthier, freer and happier lives. The real problem, Pinker argues, is that the Enlightenment values of reason and science are under attack. When commentators and demagogues appeal to people's tribalism, fatalism and distrust, then we are in danger of causing irreparable damage to important institutions like democracy and world co-operation.
simplified:
Are things getting worse every day? Is it impossible to make things better?

In his book, Steven Pinker looks at how people are doing. He sees good news.
We live longer, healthier, freer, and happier lives.

But Pinker says there is a problem. People are not always using their brains and science.
Some people make others angry or not trust each other. This can hurt important things like good government and countries working together.
reference: Are things getting worse? Is progress impossible? In his book Enlightenment Now, Steven Pinker says there is good news. People now live longer, healthier, and happier lives with more freedom. But Pinker also warns us. He says that clear thinking and science are under attack. Some people make people follow only their own group, lose hope, and stop trusting others. If this happens, imporatant things like democracy and countries working together may be badly damaged.

original: So much of what the speaker said rang true. I honestly believe there's a danger that the more connected we are, the more isolated we feel. I don't think this is such an issue for my generation who've lived without technology for so long. We know how to be alone and, more importantly, we know that it's OK to be alone. But the under 20s are another kettle of fish. They're so busy communicating that they never experience the feeling of solitude and run the risk of not learning how to enjoy their own company. In addition, they're learning conversation through messages that can be edited and changed at the expense of learning the art of real conversation in real time with the person in front of you.
simplified:
Many things the speaker said were true. I think it's a problem. We connect a lot, but we feel alone.

This is not a big problem for people my age. We lived without phones for a long time. We know how to be alone. We know it's okay to be alone.

But young people are different. They are always talking online. They never feel alone. They don't learn to be happy by themselves.

Also, they learn to talk by writing messages. They can change these messages. But they don't learn to talk to people face-to-face, right now.
reference: I agreed with much of what the speaker said. I think that when people are more connected, they can sometimes feel lonelier. For my generation, this is not such a big problem, because we lived many years without modern technology. We know how to be alone, and we know it is OK. But for people under 20, it is different. They spend so much time sending messages that they do not feel real solitude. They may not learn how to enjoy being alone. They also talk by messages that can be changed, instead of learning face-to-face conversations.

original: If we want to know where our capability for complex language came from, we need to look at how our brains are different from other animals. This relates to more than just brain size; it is important what other things our brains can do and when and why they evolved that way. And for this there are very few physical clues; artefacts left by our ancestors don't tell us what speech they were capable of making. One thing we can see in the remains of early humans, however, is the development of the mouth, throat and tongue. By about 100,000 years ago, humans had evolved the ability to create complex sounds. Before that, evolutionary biologists can only guess whether or not early humans communicated using more basic sounds.
simplified:
If we want to know how we learned to speak, we need to see how our brains are different from animal brains. It's not just about brain size. What our brains can do is important, and when and why they changed.

We don't have many clues. Old things from people long ago do not tell us how they spoke. But in old human bones, we can see how their mouth, throat, and tongue changed.

About 100,000 years ago, humans could make many different sounds. Before that, scientists can only guess if early humans used only simple sounds to talk.
reference: To know how humans learned complex language, we must look at how our brains are different from animals' brains. It is not only about the size of the brain, but also about what it can do, and when and why it changes. There are not many clues, as old subjects cannot tell us what kind of speech early humans had. But we can see changes in the mouth, throat, and tongue of early human bones. Around 100,000 years ago, humans got the ability to make complex sounds. Before that, scientists could only guess if early humans used simple sounds to talk.

original: Your dreams might show you all kinds of insights into things that you didn't realise you were thinking about. Common dreams like being able to fly or falling, your teeth falling out or having no clothes on in a public place probably mean something similar in most people. But the key to understanding exactly what they mean to you is to connect them to the events and feelings in your daily life.
simplified: Your dreams can show you things you didn't know you were thinking. Common dreams, like flying, falling, losing teeth, or being naked in public, often mean similar things for many people. But to understand what your dreams mean for you, you should connect them to your daily life and feelings.
reference: Dreams can tell us something about our thoughts and feelings, even if we don't realise it. Many people have similar dreams, like flying, falling, losing teeth, or being in public without clothes. These dreams often have the same meaning for most people. To really understand your dream, you should think about your daily life and emotions.

original: One of the most interesting cases of wild animals living in a city are the wild dogs of Moscow. In Moscow, there are approximately 35,000 wild dogs living on the streets. Some of the dogs were born wild, while others are pets that have been abandoned by their owners. Some dogs live alone and others live in packs. In 2010, scientists studied the dogs and found that the dogs have adapted remarkably successfully to urban life. They have learned that it is safer to cross the street with people and some dogs appear to understand traffic lights.
simplified:
The wild dogs of Moscow are an interesting example of animals living in a city. About 35,000 wild dogs live on the streets in Moscow. Some dogs were born wild. Other dogs were pets, but their owners left them. Some dogs live alone, and others live in groups.

In 2010, scientists studied the dogs. They found that the dogs learned to live very well in the city. They learned it is safer to cross the street with people. Some dogs also seem to understand traffic lights.
reference: One interesting example of wild animals in a city is the wild dogs in Moscow. There are around 35,000 wild dogs living on the streets. Some of them were born in the wild, and others were once pets but were left by their owners. Some dogs live alone, and some stay in groups. In 2010, scientists studied them and found that the dogs have learned to live well in the city. They often cross the street with people, and some even seem to understand traffic lights.

original: Chloe has two pet rats, Zena and Roxy. Chloe knows they're not typical pets and she has lost count of the times she's patiently tried to explain to people that rats aren't dirty and they make fantastic pets if you look after them correctly. But she understands why people react badly. She didn't like rats either until her friend Martin showed her his pet rats and she saw how affectionate and intelligent they were. Last year, when one of Martin's rats had babies, Chloe decided she'd like to have two of them.
simplified:
Chloe has two pet rats, Zena and Roxy.
She knows that rats are not typical pets.
She has often told people that rats are clean and make very good pets if you care for them well.
But she understands why some people don't like them.
Chloe didn't like rats herself until her friend Martin showed her his pets.
Then she saw how friendly and clever they were.
Last year, one of Martin's rats had babies, and Chloe decided she wanted two of them.
reference: Chloe owns two pet rats named Zena and Roxy. She knows rats are not common pets, and she has tried many times to explain that rats are not dirty and can be great pets if you care for them properly. She understands why people are unsure about rats: she didn't like them either until her friend Martin showed her his. After seeing how loving and smart they were, she changed her mind. When one of Martin's rats had babies last year, Chloe decided to keep two of them.

original: Social media, magazines and shop windows bombard people daily with things to buy, and British consumers are buying more clothes and shoes than ever before. Online shopping means it is easy for customers to buy without thinking, while major brands offer such cheap clothes that they can be treated like disposable items – worn two or three times and then thrown away.
simplified: Every day, social media, magazines, and shop windows show people many things to buy. People in Britain are buying more clothes and shoes than ever before. It's easy to buy things online without thinking. Also, big brands sell clothes that are so cheap. People often wear these clothes only a few times and then throw them away, like things you don't keep.
reference: Social media, magazines, and shop windows show people many things to buy every day. In the UK, people are now buying more clothes and shoes than ever. Online shopping makes it quick and easy to buy things, sometimes without thinking. Big brands often sell very cheap clothes, so many people wear them only two or three times and then throw them away like rubbish.

original: Wonder is New Yorker RJ Palacio's first novel. On her website, she explains that the idea for the book came to her after seeing a girl with facial deformities on the street one day. Wonder has been a bestseller in the United States and has already won several awards. Many schools are using it as a starting point for discussions about bullying, friendship and what it's like to be different. A film version is being made, and many, including me, are waiting eagerly to see what RJ Palacio writes next.
simplified: Wonder is RJ Palacio's first book. On her website, she says she got the idea for the book after seeing a girl with a different face on the street one day. Wonder is a very popular book in America. It has also won many prizes. Many schools use it to talk about bullying, friendship, and being different. They are making a movie of the book. Many people, including me, are excited to see what RJ Palacio writes next.
reference: Wonder is the first novel by RJ Palacio, who comes from New York. She says that she got the idea for the story after seeing a girl with a facial difference on the street. The book became a bestseller in the United States and has already won several awards. Many schools use it to start conversations about bullying, friendship, and how it feels to be different. A film version is now in progress, and many people are excited to read her next book.

original: In the 1990s, graffiti continued but there was also an explosion in street art around the world. Some artists wanted to make political points and produced art that tried to make people think about war, inequality and discrimination. Other street artists were more concerned with producing beautiful, attractive work. In South America, many street artists went to work in poor areas adding colour, life and beauty to grey, city walls.
simplified: In the 1990s, graffiti was still happening. But street art also became very popular all over the world. Some artists wanted to share their political ideas. They made art to make people think about war, unfairness, and how some people are treated badly. Other street artists just wanted to make beautiful art. In South America, many street artists painted in poor areas. They added colour, life, and beauty to the grey city walls.
reference: During the 1990s, graffiti continued, but street art also became much more popular around the world. Some artists used street art to talk about politics and serious issues like war, inequality, and discrimination. Others focused on making beautiful and interesting art. In South America, many street artists painted in poor neighbourhoods to bring colour and beauty to the grey walls of the cities.

original: Many city residents in Berlin, Germany complained that shooting pigs was unnecessarily cruel and there were heated arguments between hunters and animal lovers. In response to protests, the city council decided to take more peaceful action against pigs. Instead of shooting them, they have put up fences and made it illegal to feed the pigs. Time will tell if this strategy works, though it may be a losing battle as warmer winters mean that pig numbers are greater than in the past.
simplified:
Many people in Berlin, Germany, were unhappy. They said shooting pigs was too cruel. Hunters and people who love animals argued a lot about it.

Because people protested, the city leaders decided to try a calmer way to deal with the pigs. They didn't shoot the pigs. Instead, they built fences. They also made it against the law to feed the pigs.

We will see if this plan works. But it might be hard to win. This is because winters are warmer, so there are more pigs now than before.
reference: In Berlin, Germany, many local people complained that shooting pigs was too cruel. This caused strong arguments between hunters and animal lovers. Because of the protests, the city council chose a more peaceful solution. They put up fences and made it against the law to feed wild pigs. It's not clear if the plan will work, since warmer winters have caused the number of pigs to grow more than before.

original: Cape Town can be a dangerous place for baboons. Some have been injured or killed in car accidents and others have been electrocuted as they played with electric cables. Baboons are an endangered species and to save them and minimise conflicts between humans and baboons, the city council has employed a team of Baboon Monitors. The monitors' job is to chase baboons out of urban areas or catch them and release them in the countryside. This policy has had some success, though it is proving hard to stop baboons from coming back to the city once they see it as a source of easy food.
simplified:
Cape Town can be a dangerous place for baboons. Some baboons get hurt or die in car accidents. Others are hurt by electricity when they play with electric cables.

Baboons are an endangered species. To save them and reduce problems between people and baboons, the city council has a team of Baboon Monitors.

The monitors' job is to chase baboons away from cities. They also catch baboons and let them go in the countryside.

This plan has had some success. But it is difficult to stop baboons from coming back to the city. They come back because they can find food easily there.
reference: Cape Town is a risky place for baboons. Some are injured or killed by cars, and others are electrocuted when they touch electric wires. Because baboons are an endangered species, the city has hired a group called Baboon Monitors. Their job is to keep baboons out of the city by chasing them away or catching them and releasing them in the countryside. This plan has worked somewhat, but it's difficult to stop the baboons from returning since they see the city as a place to find easy food.

original: By bringing people and animals together, zoos have the potential to educate the public about conservation issues and inspire people to protect animals and their habitats. Some zoos provide a safe environment for animals which have been mistreated in circuses, or pets which have been abandoned. Zoos also carry out important research into subjects like animal behaviour and how to treat illnesses.
simplified:
Zoos bring people and animals together. They can teach people about how to protect animals and nature. They also make people want to help animals and their homes.

Some zoos give a safe home to animals that were treated badly in circuses, or pets that people left alone.

Zoos also do important studies about things like how animals act and how to help sick animals.
reference: Zoos connect people with animals and help teach the public about protecting animals and the environment. Some zoos give a safe home to animals that were treated badly in circuses or pets that were abandoned. Zoos also do important research on animal behaviour and how to treat their illnesses.

original: A different trend is springing up in opposition to consumerism – the 'buy nothing' trend. The idea originated in Canada in the early 1990s and then moved to the US, where it became a rejection of the overspending and overconsumption of Black Friday and Cyber Monday during Thanksgiving weekend. On Buy Nothing Day people organise various types of protests and cut up their credit cards. Throughout the year, Buy Nothing groups organise the exchange and repair of items they already own.
simplified:
There is a new idea called 'buy nothing'. It is against buying too many things.

This idea started in Canada in the early 1990s. Later, it came to the US. There, people used it to protest against spending and buying too much on Black Friday and Cyber Monday, which are after Thanksgiving.

On Buy Nothing Day, people have different protests. They even cut up their credit cards. All year, 'Buy Nothing' groups help people swap and fix things they already have.
reference: A new movement against consumerism is growing – it's called the 'buy nothing' trend. It started in Canada in the early 1990s and then spread to the US. People involved in this movement want to avoid overspending, especially during shopping events like Black Friday and Cyber Monday. On Buy Nothing Day, they hold protests and even cut up their credit cards. Throughout the year, they also organise activities to repair or exchange used items instead of buying new ones.

original: An important inspiration for the Hunger Games book comes from Suzanne's love of classical Greek mythology. When she was a child, one of her favourite stories was Theseus and the Minotaur. In this story the city of Athens is ruled by Crete, but the Athenians rebel. As a punishment, Minos the king of Crete forces the Athenians to send seven boys and seven girls to Crete every year. The youths are thrown into the labyrinth and eaten by a monster that lives there called the Minotaur. But one of the youths, named Theseus, fights the Minotaur and kills it. Suzanne sees Katniss Everdeen as a futuristic Theseus.
simplified:
Suzanne loved old Greek stories. This gave her a big idea for The Hunger Games book. When she was a child, she really liked the story of Theseus and the Minotaur.

In this story, Crete ruled Athens. But the people of Athens fought back. To punish them, King Minos of Crete made Athens send seven boys and seven girls to Crete every year. These young people went into a maze called the Labyrinth. A monster called the Minotaur lived there and ate them.

But one young man, Theseus, fought the Minotaur and killed it. Suzanne thinks Katniss Everdeen is like a Theseus from the future.
reference: One big inspiration for The Hunger Games came from Suzanne Collins' love of ancient Greek myths. As a child, one of her favourite stories was Theseus and the Minotaur. In the story, Athens is controlled by Crete, and every year the king of Crete, Minos, makes the Athenians send seven boys and seven girls. These children are sent into a maze where a monster, the Minotaur, lives. Theseus, one of the children, kills the monster. Suzanne sees her character Katniss as a modern version of Theseus.

original: Often wild animals come into cities to look for food. In Cape Town, South Africa, baboons have started coming into residential areas on the edge of the city to feed. They open rubbish bins and eat fruit from gardens and orchards. Some brave baboons have even come into people's houses and taken food from kitchen cupboards and fridges! Baboons can be aggressive and have attacked a lot of pet animals, so understandably, many city residents don't welcome their presence.
simplified: Wild animals often come into cities to find food. In Cape Town, South Africa, baboons now come into parts of the city where people live to eat. They open bins and eat fruit from gardens. Some baboons are very brave. They even go into people's houses and take food from kitchens. Baboons can be dangerous. They have attacked many pets. So, many people in the city do not want them there.
reference: Wild animals often enter cities in search of food. In Cape Town, South Africa, baboons have begun coming into areas where people live. They open rubbish bins and eat fruit from gardens and orchards. Some even go into homes and take food from kitchen cupboards and fridges. Since baboons can be aggressive and have attacked many pets, it's easy to understand why many city residents don't want them nearby.

original: Is graffiti art or vandalism? This depends on your point of view, but in many countries, writing or painting on public or private property is considered vandalism. Many street artists have been stopped by the police and some have had to pay fines. Many city councils complain about the high cost of cleaning graffiti off buildings, buses and trains.
simplified: Is graffiti art or vandalism? It depends on what you think. But in many countries, writing or painting on public or private places is seen as vandalism. Police have stopped many street artists, and some have had to pay fines. Many city councils complain that it costs a lot of money to clean graffiti from buildings, buses, and trains.
reference: Some people see graffiti as art, while others think it is vandalism. In many countries, painting or writing on public or private property is against the law. Street artists are often stopped by the police, and some are fined. City councils often complain about how expensive it is to clean graffiti from walls, buses, and trains.

original: If most people have four to six dreams every night after the age of ten, that's as many as 2,000 dreams per year. So, by the time they reach 80 years old the average person might have had 140,000 dreams. Even if we forget 95–99 per cent of our dreams, that's still a few thousand remembered dreams across a lifetime. It's not too difficult to believe that, by coincidence, a dream event is followed by a real-life event that's similar to it, especially if the subject of the dream is something that happens often in everyday life.
simplified: Most people have 4 to 6 dreams each night after they are ten years old. That's about 2,000 dreams every year. So, when someone is 80 years old, they might have had 140,000 dreams. We forget most of our dreams, about 95-99%. But we still remember a few thousand dreams in our life. It's easy to think that something in a dream might also happen in real life by chance. This is especially true if the dream is about things that happen often every day.
reference: After the age of ten, most people have between four and six dreams each night. That adds up to about 2,000 dreams a year. By the time someone turns 80, they may have had around 140,000 dreams. Even though we forget most dreams–about 95 to 99 percent–we still remember thousands over a lifetime. So, it's not hard to believe that sometimes a dream is followed by a real-life event that feels similar, especially when it's about something that happens often in everyday life.

original: The Hunger Games takes place in the future, after the destruction of North America. The country is called Panem and is made up of twelve poor districts governed by the wealthy Capitol. The Capitol holds absolute power over the nation. Each district is responsible for producing different things for the Capitol. District 12, where the story begins, provides all the coal for the country. There used to be a thirteenth district but they rebelled against the Capitol in the past and were destroyed.
simplified:
The Hunger Games happens in the future, after North America was destroyed. The country is called Panem. It has twelve poor districts. The rich Capitol rules these districts. The Capitol has all the power in the country.

Each district makes different things for the Capitol. District 12, where the story starts, gives all the coal to the country.

There was once a thirteenth district. But they fought against the Capitol a long time ago and were destroyed.
reference: The Hunger Games is set in the future, after North America has been destroyed. The new country is called Panem, which includes twelve poor districts ruled by the rich Capitol. The Capitol controls the entire country. Each district has its own job and sends goods to the Capitol. The story begins in District 12, which produces coal. There used to be a District 13, but it rebelled and was later destroyed by the Capitol.

original: What does the art world think of graffiti and street art? Recently, there has been a growing recognition of its value as an art form. There have been major exhibitions of street art in galleries in Paris, London and Los Angeles. The American artist Elura Emerald organised a street art exhibition at a New York gallery in 2008. She defended street artists, saying 'artists who paint on the street are merely expressing themselves, not hurting anyone. They should be appreciated and celebrated'.
simplified:
What does the art world think of graffiti and street art?
Recently, more people in the art world see it as important art.
There have been big shows of street art in galleries in Paris, London, and Los Angeles.
In 2008, the American artist Elura Emerald held a street art show at a New York gallery.
She defended street artists. She said, 'Artists who paint on the street are just showing their feelings. They are not hurting anyone. People should like and celebrate them.'
reference: How does the art world view graffiti and street art? Recently, more people have started to see it as a real form of art. Large exhibitions featuring street art have been held in cities like Paris, London, and Los Angeles. In 2008, American artist Elura Emerald organised a street art exhibition in a New York gallery. She supported street artists, saying they are simply expressing themselves and not doing harm, and that they should be respected and celebrated.

original: George Lucas was one of the early film directors to directly base his story on the 17 stages of the hero's journey. Typically the hero starts the story living an ordinary life, but something happens that calls them to an adventure that changes everything. At the beginning of Star Wars, Luke lives an ordinary life with his aunt and uncle, repairing robots. When he finds Princess Leia's message to Obi-Wan Kenobi inside the robot R2D2, it is 'the call to adventure' that starts the hero on his journey.
simplified: George Lucas was one of the first film directors to use the 'hero's journey' idea for his stories. Usually, the hero lives a normal life. But then something happens that makes them go on an adventure. This adventure changes their life completely. In Star Wars, Luke lives a normal life with his aunt and uncle. He fixes robots. He finds a message from Princess Leia inside the robot R2D2. The message is for Obi-Wan Kenobi. This is the start of Luke's adventure.
reference: George Lucas was one of the first film directors to base a story on the 17 stages of the hero's journey. In this type of story, the hero begins with a normal life, but something happens that sends them on an adventure. In Star Wars, Luke Skywalker lives with his aunt and uncle and works on robots. When he finds Princess Leia's message in the robot R2D2, it becomes his 'call to adventure' and marks the beginning of his journey.

original: Sam squinted against the sun at the distant dust trail raked up by the car on its way up to the Big House. The horses kicked and flicked their tails at flies, not caring about their owner's first visit in ten months. Sam waited. Mr Carter didn't come out here unless he had to, which was just fine by Sam. The more he kept out of his boss's way, the longer he'd have a job. Mr, Carter wiped the sweat from the back of his neck. The damp patches on his shirt drew together like shapes in an atlas. His skin was already turning ruddy in the June sun. Otherwise he had the indoor tan of a man that made money while other people did the work.
simplified:
Sam looked at the car with difficulty because of the sun. The car was far away, going up to the Big House, and it made a lot of dust. The horses moved their legs and tails to get rid of flies. They did not care that their owner was visiting for the first time in ten months.

Sam waited. Mr Carter only came here when it was necessary. Sam liked this. If Sam stayed away from his boss, he would keep his job longer.

Mr Carter wiped sweat from his neck. His shirt was wet with sweat in different places. His skin was already getting red in the June sun. He had pale skin, like a man who works inside and lets other people do the hard work.
reference: Sam narrowed his eyes at the dust in the distance. A car was coming up to the Big House. The horses kicked and moved their tails to stop the flies, not caring that their owner hadn't visited for ten months. Sam stood and waited. Mr. Carter only came when necessary, and Sam was happy about that. The less he saw his boss, the safer his job was. Mr. Carter wiped sweat from his neck. His shirt had wet spots, and his skin was getting red from the summer sun. Normally, he stayed indoors, making money while others did the hard work.

original: A large number of bridge accidents occur during the construction of the bridge itself. These accidents are often due to an error made by the engineers, such as a miscalculation. The bridge collapses under its own weight, and this can be deadly for the workers on it at the time.
simplified:
Many accidents happen when bridges are being built.
Engineers sometimes make mistakes, for example, with their calculations.
Then, the bridge can fall down because it is too heavy.
This is very dangerous for the workers on the bridge at that time.
reference: Many bridge accidents happen during construction. These are often caused by mistakes made by engineers, such as wrong calculations. When this happens, the bridge may collapse under its own weight, which can be deadly for the workers on it at the time.

original: Another suggested defence against a PHA on course to hit Earth is to blow it up using a nuclear weapon. It may sound like a plot from a film, and it was the subject of the 1998 film Armageddon, but the Hypervelocity Asteroid Mitigation Mission for Emergency Response (HAMMER) is a genuine NASA proposal.
