original: Often wild animals come into cities to look for food. In Cape Town, South Africa, baboons have started coming into residential areas on the edge of the city to feed. Some baboons are very brave and go into houses to take food from kitchens. Baboons can be dangerous and sometimes hurt pet animals. Many people in the city do not want them around.

original: An important inspiration for the Hunger Games book comes from Suzanne's love of classical Greek mythology. When she was a child, one of her favourite stories was Theseus and the Minotaur. original: Is graffiti art or vandalism? This depends on your point of view, but in many countries, writing or painting on public or private property is considered vandalism. original: George Lucas was one of the early film directors to directly base his story on the 17 stages of the hero's journey. original: By bringing people and animals together, zoos have the potential to educate the public about conservation issues and inspire people to protect animals and their habitats. original: A different trend is springing up in opposition to consumerism – the 'buy nothing' trend. The idea originated in Canada in the early 1990s and then moved to the US, where it became a rejection of the overspending and overconsumption of Black Friday and Cyber Monday during Thanksgiving weekend. On Buy Nothing Day people organise various types of protests and cut up their credit cards. Throughout the year, Buy Nothing groups organise the exchange and repair of items they already own.
simplified:

On Buy Nothing Day, people do different protests. They also cut up their credit cards.

All year long, Buy Nothing groups help people. They help them swap things. They also help them fix things. These are things they already have.
reference: Some people are starting a new idea called the 'buy nothing' trend. It began in Canada in the 1990s and then went to the USA. These people don't like buying too much on days like Black Friday and Cyber Monday. On 'Buy Nothing Day', people protest and cut their credit cards. During the year, they also fix and trade things instead of buying new ones.

original: A large number of bridge accidents occur during the construction of the bridge itself. These accidents are often due to an error made by the engineers, such as a miscalculation. The bridge collapses under its own weight, and this can be deadly for the workers on it at the time.

Many bridge accidents happen.
They happen when people build bridges.
Engineers often make mistakes.
Their math can be wrong.
The bridge falls down.
It is too heavy.
This can kill workers.
reference: Many accidents with bridges happen while they are being built. These accidents often happen because engineers make mistakes, like wrong numbers. The bridge can fall down from its own weight. This is very dangerous for the workers on the bridge.

original: Religion is important to Pi. Though his family is Hindu, he is curious about other religions and he makes friends with a Christian priest and a Muslim baker. One day, Pi says that he is Hindu, Muslim, and Christian at the same time. His family and teachers ask him to choose only one religion, but Pi says, "I just want to love God." original: What does the art world think of graffiti and street art? Recently, there has been a growing recognition of its value as an art form. There have been major exhibitions of street art in galleries in Paris, London and Los Angeles. The American artist Elura Emerald organised a street art exhibition at a New York gallery in 2008. simplified:
What do art people think of graffiti and street art?

She said good things about street artists.

reference: What do people in the art world think about street art and graffiti? Today, more people see it as a true kind of art. Big art shows in Paris, London, and Los Angeles have shown street art. In 2008, an American artist, Elura Emerald, made a street art show in New York. She said street artists only want to share their ideas and are not doing anything wrong.

original: I'm a freelancer and work for myself. This is great because I am in control of what I do and how I spend my time. At first, I was working from home, but I found it really hard to concentrate. There were just too many distractions around: housework that needed doing, another cup of tea, my family members wanting my attention for various things. So I started to go to a nearby café to work, but the Wi-Fi connection wasn't ideal and I found myself drinking too much coffee. In the end, I decided to rent a desk in a co-working space with five other freelancers like myself. I liked getting dressed to go to work in the morning and being able to focus in an office environment.
simplified:
I am a freelancer. This means I work for myself. This is good. I choose my work. I choose my hours.

First, I worked from home. It was hard to focus. Many things stopped my work. I had housework. My family needed me. I drank too much tea.

So I went to a cafe. The Wi-Fi was not good. I drank too much coffee.

reference: I am a freelancer, so I work for myself. This is good as I can choose what to do and how to spend my time. At first, I worked at home, but it was hard to focus. There were many things around me, like housework, making tea and families asking for attention. Then I tried to work in a cafe, but the internet was not good and I drank too much coffee. In the end, I rented a desk in a co-working space with five other freelancer. I liked dressing up for the office and going to work in the morning.

original: Another suggested defence against a PHA on course to hit Earth is to blow it up using a nuclear weapon. It may sound like a plot from a film, and it was the subject of the 1998 film Armageddon, but the Hypervelocity Asteroid Mitigation Mission for Emergency Response (HAMMER) is a genuine NASA proposal. The eight-ton rockets would be fired at an approaching asteroid with the hope of bumping it off course. If the asteroid was too close to Earth for this plan to work, the rockets would carry nuclear bombs to blow it up instead.
simplified:
There is an idea to stop a space rock. This rock is coming to Earth. We could blow it up. We would use a special bomb.

Big rockets would go to the space rock. They would push it away. This would change its path.

If the rock is too near Earth, this plan will not work. Then, the rockets would have special bombs. They would blow up the rock.
reference: One way to stop an asteroid from hitting Earth is to break it with a strong bomb, which is nuclear weapon. This may sound like a movie, and it was in the 1998 film Armageddon. But NASA had a real plan on this. The plan was to send big rockets, about eight tons, to hit the asteroid and push it away. If the asteroid is already too close to Earth, the rocket would take the nuclear bomb to blow it up.

original: According to Campbell, the hero at first refuses the call to adventure, but a mentor appears who helps them and they decide to 'cross the threshold' and travel into the 'special world' where the adventure happens. Luke's teacher is Obi-Wan, his friends are Han solo and the robots R2D2 and C3PO, and his enemy is Darth Vader inside the Death Star.

original: If most people have four to six dreams every night after the age of ten, that's as many as 2,000 dreams per year. So, by the time they reach 80 years old the average person might have had 140,000 dreams. Even if we forget 95–99 per cent of our dreams, that's still a few thousand remembered dreams across a lifetime. It's not too difficult to believe that, by coincidence, a dream event is followed by a real-life event that's similar to it, especially if the subject of the dream is something that happens often in everyday life.
simplified:
Most people dream every night.
They have 4 to 6 dreams.
This starts after age ten.
So, they have about 2,000 dreams each year.
By age 80, a person may have had 140,000 dreams.

We forget most dreams.
We forget 95 to 99 percent.
But we still remember some.
We remember a few thousand dreams.
This is over our whole life.

It is easy to think that a dream can be like real life.
Sometimes, a dream is like something that happens later.
This is a coincidence.
A coincidence means two things happen by chance.
They seem connected, but they are not.
This happens more with dreams about normal things.
Things that happen every day.
reference: Most people have 4 to 6 dreams every night after they turn 10. That means around 2,000 dreams every year. By age 80, a person may have about 140,000 dreams. Even if we forget 95?C99% of our dreams, we still remember many. So, it's not strange if something we dream later happens in real life, especially if it is something we often see in daily life.

original: Around the 18th and 19th centuries two main ideas about dreams became popular. One was the idea that the things we see in our dreams represent things hidden from our conscious mind. Freud believed that if we understand what dreams are telling us, we can understand our hidden feelings and the problems they cause. However, the other theory was the opposite. It said that dreams are just a collection of random activity in the brain while it's organising memories and events from the day. When we wake up, we try to make sense of these random images and feelings and put them into some sort of story.
simplified:
A long time ago, people had two main ideas about dreams.
One idea said dreams show us hidden thoughts.
Freud thought dreams tell us about our secret feelings and problems.
But the other idea was different.
It said dreams are only random things happening in the brain.
The brain sorts memories from the day.
When we wake up, we see random pictures and feelings.
We try to make a story from them.
reference: In the 18th and 19th centuries, people had two main ideas about dreams. The first idea was that dreams show things that we dont know in our mind. Freud believed that if we look at dreams, we can understand our hidden feelings and problems. The second idea was opposite. It said dreams are only random things in the brain when it is cleaning and organising the day's memories. When we wake up, we try to make a story from these pics and feelings.

original: Some people think writing your dreams down can open your mind to lucid dreaming. Lucid dreams are dreams where you're not only aware you're dreaming but you can make decisions to affect the events of your dreams. So, maybe you can turn a nightmare into a safe-feeling dream, or you can direct the plot of your dream like a film director. Then, instead of just working out the meaning of your dreams, you'll be creating them, though you might want to continue having some dreams that allow your subconscious to tell you what's on your mind!
simplified: Some people write down their dreams. They think this helps with lucid dreaming. What is lucid dreaming? In a lucid dream, you know you are dreaming. You can also choose what happens. You can change a bad dream. You can make it a good dream. You can control your dream story. Like a movie director. You will make your own dreams. You are not just finding their meaning. But some dreams are still important. They show you your hidden thoughts.
reference: Some people think that writing down dreams in a notebook can help them have lucid dreams. A lucid dream is when you know you are dreaming, and you can change what happens. For example, you can make a bad dream feel safe, or you can control the story like a movie director. In this way, you are not only looking for the meaning of your dreams, but also making them. But sometimes, you may still want dreams that show what is in your mind.

original: Whether NASA can find the remaining middle-sized NEOs depends on getting the money to build NEOCam, a 0.5-metre space telescope which would use infrared light to locate asteroids. If it did get the money, it could probably achieve its goal in ten years. Once logged, the planetary defence team would still need to work out how to defend the planet against being hit by the truly worrying asteroids – the PHAs.
simplified:
NASA wants to find space rocks.
These rocks are near Earth.
NASA needs money for a new telescope.
The telescope is called NEOCam.
It will fly in space.
It uses special light to find rocks.
If NASA gets the money, they can do this.
They think it will take 10 years.
After finding the rocks, there is more work.
A special team protects Earth.
They must plan how to save our planet.
Some space rocks are very dangerous.
They need to stop these big rocks.
reference: NASA needs money to build NEOCam, a space telescope with a small lens, to find the rest of the middle-sized asteriods. This telescope would use infrared light to look for them. If NASA gets the money, it could finish this in 10 years. After that, the team must still plan how to stop the very dangerous asteriods, called PHAs, from hitting Earth.

original: The 'buy nothing' trend has now reached influencers on social media who usually share posts of clothing and make-up that they recommend for people to buy. Some YouTube stars now encourage their viewers not to buy anything at all for periods as long as a year. Two friends in Canada spent a year working towards buying only food. For the first three months they learned how to live without buying electrical goods, clothes or things for the house. For the next stage, they gave up services, for example haircuts, eating out at restaurants or buying petrol for their cars. In one year, they'd saved $55,000.
simplified:
The 'buy nothing' idea is popular now. This idea is for not buying new things. People called influencers are on social media. They often show clothes and make-up. They tell people to buy these things. But now, some influencers follow the 'buy nothing' idea.

Some famous people are on YouTube. They tell their viewers to buy nothing. They say 'buy nothing' for a year.

Two friends in Canada tried this. For one year, they bought only food. For three months, they bought no new things. They bought no electric items. They bought no clothes. They bought no home items.

Then, they stopped paying for services. Services are things like haircuts. They did not eat in restaurants. They did not buy gas for their cars. After one year, they saved $55,000.
reference: The "buy nothing" idea is now gaining popularity among social media influencers. Normally, they show clothes and make-up for people to buy. But now, some YouTubers tell their fans not to buy anything, even for one year. Two friends in Canada did this and only bought food for a year. In the first three months, they stopped buying electronics, clothes, and things for the house. Later, they also stopped paying for services, like haircuts, eating in restaurants, and petrol for their cars. In one year, they saved $55,000.

original: In her previous work environment, Gabriela was used to a high power distance culture where power and authority are respected and everyone has their rightful place. In such a culture, leaders make the big decisions and are not often challenged. Her Swedish team, however, were used to working in a low power distance culture where subordinates often work together with their bosses to find solutions and make decisions. Here, leaders act as coaches or mentors who encourage independent thought and expect to be challenged.
simplified:
Gabriela had an old job. She knew a "high power distance culture". This means people respect power. Leaders are very important. Everyone has a clear place. In this culture, leaders make important choices. People do not question them.

But her new team was Swedish. They worked in a "low power distance culture". This means leaders and workers are more equal. Workers and leaders often work together. They solve problems and decide things. Here, leaders are like helpers. They are like teachers. They want people to think for themselves. They want people to ask questions.
reference: In her old job, Gabriela worked in a place with high power distance. This means people respect authority, and leaders make the big decisions. Workers do not usually question their bosses. But her Swedish team worked in a low power distance culture. Here, workers and bosses make decisions together. Leaders act like coaches or teachers, and they want workers to think for themselves and even question them.

original: Writing about your dreams will mean you start to remember more details about the dream, so think about the people and place where the dream happened as they might add to the meaning too. Over the period of a week you'll be surprised how much you've written down. Now you can start connecting your dreams to the events and feelings in your daily life.
simplified: Write about your dreams. You will remember more details. Think about the people in your dream. Think about the place. This can help you understand the dream. Do this for one week. You will write a lot. You will be surprised. Now, link your dreams. Think about your daily life. Think about what happens. Think about your feelings.
reference: When you write down your dreams, you remember more things. Think about the people and the place in the dream, because they can mean something. After one week, you will see that you have written a lot. Then, you can see how your dreams link to your feelings in your daily life.

original: It is impossible to know how street art will develop in the future but certain trends are emerging. While most street artists are young people who paint in their city or neighbourhood, more and more street artists are travelling and working around the globe. Other artists are using the internet to talk to each other and share photos of their work. Also, the art world is giving more recognition to street art as a legitimate art form. Although we don't know what will happen to street art in the future, we can be sure that it is here to stay!
simplified:
We don't know how street art will change. But new things are starting.
Many street artists are young. They paint in their town. But now, more artists travel. They work in many countries.
Some artists use the internet. They talk together. They show pictures of their art.
Also, people who like art see street art. They think it is real art now.
We don't know what will happen later. But we know it will stay.
reference: We don't know what street art will be like in the future, but we can see some changes now. Most street artists are young and paint in their own city. But more artists are travelling and making art in other countries. They also use the internet to talk and show pictures of their work. Today, street art is starting to get more respect as real art. We don't know what will happen, but street art is htere.

original: People have been painting and writing on walls throughout history. In prehistoric times, people in Africa and Europe used to paint pictures of animals and people in caves. Graffiti has been found on buildings at ancient sites in Greece, Italy, Syria and Iraq. In the Roman town of Pompeii, archaeologists have found numerous examples of graffiti written in Latin. These include religious, political and romantic messages, and even some magic spells!
simplified:
People painted and wrote on walls. They did this for a very long time.

A very long time ago, people lived. They were in Africa and Europe. They painted pictures in caves. They painted animals and people.

We found graffiti. Graffiti is writing or drawing on walls. It was on old buildings. These buildings were in Greece, Italy, Syria, and Iraq.

There was a Roman town. Its name was Pompeii. People found many graffiti there. They were written in Latin. Latin is an old language.

The graffiti had different messages. Some were about religion. Some were about politics. Some were about love. There were even magic words.
reference: People have painted and written on walls for a very long time. In early times, people in Africa and Europe painted animals and people inside caves. Graffiti has also been found on old buildings in Greece, Italy, Syria, and Iraq. In the Roman town of Pompeii, archaeologists found many graffiti messages in Latin. These messages were about religion, politics, love, and even magic spells!

original: The first is DART – the Double Asteroid Redirection Test. Plans are scheduled to test DART on the moon of an asteroid called Didymos. 'Didymoon' is 150 metres wide, orbiting its 800-metre mother, and hopefully the impact of DART will knock it out of its orbit enough for Earth-based telescopes to pick up.
simplified:
The first thing is DART.
DART means Double Asteroid Redirection Test.
An asteroid is a big rock in space.
This test wants to change an asteroid's path.
They will test DART on a space rock.
This rock is called Didymos.
Didymos has a small moon.
The moon is called Didymoon.

Didymos is 800 meters wide.

reference: The first project is DART- the Double Asteroid Redirection Test. It will be tested on the moon of an asteroid called Didymos. This moon is called "Didymoon." It is 150 metres wide and goes around its bigger "mother" asteroid, which is 800 metres wide. Scientists hope that when DART hits Didymoon, it will change its path enough for telescopes on Earth to see.

original: Not content with one amazing trip, some of today's adventurers go from challenge to challenge. Meagan McGrath from Canada has climbed the highest mountain on each continent, ridden a bike across Canada and run a long-distance race in the Sahara Desert in 45ºC heat. But perhaps her most remarkable journey was a skiing trip to the South Pole. On the first day, she fell into a glacier and had to be rescued. Many of us would have given up at that point, but Meagan decided to carry on. She reached the South Pole forty days later, having pulled a sledge with a tent and all her food behind her through freezing conditions and ice storms.
simplified:
Some people love adventures. They do many hard things.

But one trip was very special. She skied to the South Pole.
On the first day, she fell into a big ice river. Someone had to help her.
Many people would stop. But Meagan did not stop.
She got to the South Pole. It took her 40 days. She pulled a small cart for snow. Her tent and food were in it. It was very cold. There were ice storms.
reference: Some adventurers today like to do many difficult trips. Meagan McGrath from Canada climbed the tallest mountain on each continent, rode her bike across Canada, and ran a long race in the Sahara Desert, where it was 45ºC. But maybe her most special trip was skiing to the South Pole. On the first day, she fell into a glacier and needed help to get out. Many people would stop there, but Meagan continued. After forty days, she reached the South Pole, pulling a sledge with her tent and food through very cold weather and ice storms.

In the past, explorers used maps and compasses, but now they use modern tools like GPS and satellite phones. Many of them love nature and want to tell people about environmental problems. Others want to help people in need and collect money for charities.

original: People might not realise they are part of the disposable clothing problem because they donate their unwanted clothes to charities. But charity shops can't sell all those unwanted clothes. 'Fast fashion' goes out of fashion as quickly as it came in and is often too poor quality to recycle; people don't want to buy it second-hand. Huge quantities end up being thrown away, and a lot of clothes that charities can't sell are sent abroad, causing even more economic and environmental problems.

Fast fashion quickly goes out of style and is often poor in quality, so people don't want to buy second-hand. A lot of clothes are thrown away, and many clothes that charities cannot sell are sent to other countries. This causes money and environmental problems.

reference: Ed Stafford is from the UK. He is the first person to walk along the Amazon River. He started in the Andes mountains in Peru and finished in Brazil. Ed was in danger, but he only got bitten by mosquitoes and ants.

original: The two men looked towards the northern end of the property. It stretched as far as the eye could see. Even the fences were barely visible from where they stood. However bored and rebellious a teenage boy might get, it wasn't possible to escape on foot. Sam looked at the biggest of the horses, kicking at the ground with its heavy hooves. Could the boy ride? he wondered. There was a whole load of trouble a good rider could get into out here, miles away from anyone. But maybe there was even more trouble for someone who knew nothing about horses and wanted to get away from his father.

original: Having decided to go to school, Auggie then has to face his first day. Like every child starting at a new school, he is really anxious. But because of the way he looks, it's an agonising experience. Nobody wants to sit next to him and he notices other kids staring at him or talking about him behind their hands. Fortunately, he makes friends with Jack, a boy in his class, and Summer, a girl he chats with at lunch. But it's not just the first day that's hard. Auggie soon learns that his classmates don't want to touch him for fear of catching 'the plague'. As he goes through the school year, Auggie goes through many intense ups and downs till finally an unexpected and traumatic event at a school camp changes things completely.
simplified:
Auggie decides to go to school. It is his first day.
All children feel nervous at a new school. Auggie feels very nervous too.
But Auggie looks different. This makes it very hard for him.
No one wants to sit with him. Kids look at him. They talk about him quietly.
Luckily, he makes a friend. His name is Jack. Jack is in his class. He also makes a friend called Summer. He talks to her at lunch.

Auggie soon learns something. His classmates do not want to touch him. They are afraid of getting sick. They call it 'the plague'.
Auggie spends the year at school. He has good times and bad times. Then something happens at school camp. It is a big surprise. It is also very sad. This changes everything for Auggie.
reference: Auggie decides to go to school and face his first day. He is very nervous, like other new students. But because of how he looks, it is very hard. No one wants to sit near him, and he sees children looking at him and talking about him. He is lucky to make two friends: Jack, a boy in his class, and Summer, a girl he meets at lunch. Still, life at school is not easy. Some kids think they will get a sickness, called "the plague," if they touch him. During the school year, he has many good and bad moments. Then, at a school camp, something shocking and difficult happens that changes everything.

original: If we look around us at the things we have purchased at some point in our lives, we would no doubt notice that not everything we own is being put to good use: the thick woollen coat which we thought looked trendy despite the fact that we live in a tropical country, the smartphone that got put away when we bought ourselves the newest model, the car that only gets used at the weekends, or even the guest room in our house that somehow got turned into a storeroom.

original: Both of these kinds of accidents are extremely rare, but boats and trains can cause a bridge to collapse for different reasons. With trains, it's the velocity of the impact that can bring a bridge down. With boats, it's the very large mass they have that can bring about the collapse, even if they are moving very slowly when it occurs. The best way to avoid bridge failures is to plan for them. Modern technologies that can detect structural weakness, safer working environments and better designs can all help to reduce these terrible accidents.
simplified:
These accidents are very rare. But boats and trains can make a bridge fall down. They do this for different reasons.

We can stop bridges from falling. We must plan for this. New tools can find weak parts. Safer places to work help. Better plans for bridges help too. All these things can stop bad accidents.
reference: Accidents with bridges do not happen often. But sometimes trains or boats can make a bridge fall. A fast train crash can break a bridge. A boat is very heavy, so even a slow boat can make a bridge collapse. The best way to stop this is to plan good. New technology can find weak parts of a bridge. Safer building work and better designs can also help prevent these accidents.

Some dogs can even use the city metro to go from one place to another! Scientists do not know how they know when to get off the train. Maybe they use their strong smell to know their favourite places. Or maybe they listen to the names of the stations. Today, people on the metro are so used to the dogs.

original: Some of the biggest and most expensive transportation projects in the world have involved building bridges. original: In Britain, the average person spends more than £1,000 on new clothes a year, which is around four per cent of their income. British people currently owe approximately £670 per adult to credit card companies. That's 66 per cent of the average wardrobe budget. Also, not only are people spending money they don't have, they're using it to buy things they don't need. Britain throws away 300,000 tons of clothing a year, most of which goes into landfill sites.

original: Maybe dreams are the result of our mind organising the thoughts we have during the day, but they appear in dreams with symbolic meaning. original: Having good relationships is a big part of being happy. You also need at least one person who you discuss personal feelings with – called 'self-disclosure'. Just one person for a heart-to-heart is enough, together with a network of other relationships. It's not enough to have lots of friends just to do things with or chat to about music or football. That deeper connection is all-important. Some people need to learn how to listen effectively to others in order to develop stronger relationships.

Good friends make you happy.

reference: Good relationships help us to be happy. A study showed that happy people usually have close family and friends, and they visit them often. It is not enough to only have many friends to chat with about music or football. What is important is a deeper connection. Some people also need to learn to listen to others to make stronger friendships.

original: One of the most important modern functions of zoos is supporting international breeding programmes, particularly for endangered species. In the wild, some of the rarest species have difficulty in finding mates and breeding, and they might also be threatened by poachers, loss of their habitat and predators. A good zoo will enable these species to live and breed in a secure environment. In addition, as numbers of some wild species drop, there is an increased danger of populations becoming too genetically similar. Breeding programmes provide a safeguard: zoo-bred animals can be released into the wild to increase genetic diversity.
simplified:
Zoos have an important job.
They help animals have babies.
This is for animals in danger.
"Endangered" means very few are left.

Some animals are very rare.
They live in nature.
It is hard for them to find a partner.
It is hard for them to have babies.
Bad people hunt them.
These people are called "poachers".
Animals might lose their home.
Their home is their "habitat".
Other animals hunt them.
These are called "predators".

Good zoos help these animals.
Animals can live safely there.
They can have babies safely.

Fewer animals live in nature.
This can cause a problem.
Animals can become too much alike.
This means they are "genetically similar".

Having babies in zoos helps.
This protects the animals.
Zoo animals can go back to nature.
This makes animal groups stronger.
This is called "genetic diversity".
reference: Zoos has an important role. They help animals that are endangered, which means very few in the world, by running breeding programmes. In the wild, rare animals often cannot find a mate to have babies. They can also be killed by hunters, lose their homes, and be eaten by other animals. In a good zoo, they can live safely and have babies. When the number of wild animals gets very small, they can become too similar in their genes. Breeding in zoos helps this. Later, the young animals can go back to the wild and make the group stronger.

original: Personally, I think it's fascinating to consider how we'll speed up our evolution as a species by augmenting our bodies. Imagine if you could implant a computer inside our brain! reference: I think it exciting to think about how people can change with technology. One day, we might put a computer inside the brain. This could help us be better at maths, see and hear better, and remember more things. In the future, this idea will be more common.

original: Wasfia has dedicated her life to supporting human rights and has witnessed numerous international humanitarian projects in her homeland to educate and train women and girls, but once too often they have been left with nothing when such projects have stopped running. original: It was a fascinating talk and the speaker really hit the nail on the head with a couple of things. Take parental influence, for instance. original: Early in her career, the psychologist Carol Dweck of Stanford University gave a group of ten-year-olds problems that were slightly too hard for them. One group reacted positively, said they loved challenge and understood that their abilities could be developed. She says they had a 'growth mindset' and are focused on what they can achieve in the future. But another group of children felt that their intelligence was being judged and they had failed. They had a 'fixed mindset' and were unable to imagine improving. Some of these children said they might cheat in the future; others looked for someone who had done worse than them to boost their self-esteem.
simplified:
Carol Dweck is a scientist. She studies the mind.
She gave tasks to ten-year-old children. The tasks were a bit hard for them.

One group of children felt good. They liked hard tasks. They knew they could learn new skills.
Carol calls this a 'growth mindset'. This means they believe they can get better.
They think about what they can do in the future.

But another group felt bad. They thought people were judging how smart they were. They felt they had failed.
Carol calls this a 'fixed mindset'. This means they believe they cannot change.
They could not imagine getting better.

Some children said they might cheat later. Others looked for someone who did worse. This made them feel better about themselves.
reference: When Carol Dweck started her work as a psychologist at Stanford University, she gave some ten-year-old children some easy problems. One group of children reacted well. They liked the challenge and believed they could learn more in the future. Dweck called this a 'growth mindset'. But the other group felt bad. They thought the problems showed they were not smart, and they could not imagine improving. Dweck called this a 'fixed mindset'. Some children with this mindset said they might cheat next time, and others tried to feel better by looking at kids who did worse than they.

original: Horror films love uninhabited places. This could be an abandoned hospital, a scary empty house or a ghost town. There's something about lonely, empty places. What was it like when people lived there? Why did they leave? Maybe it's also that they are so quiet, which can be very scary too. Of course, abandoned places are also handy for horror film directors in that it's more believable that you will have no phone coverage there either.
simplified: Scary movies like empty places. They use old hospitals. Or empty houses. Or towns with no people. Empty places feel strange. What was it like when people lived there? Why did they leave? Also, they are very quiet. This can be scary. Scary movie makers like these places. Your phone will not work there. This helps the story.
reference: Horror films often happen in empty places. They can be an old hospital, a house or a town without people. Empty places make us think what it was like when people lived there? Why did they leave? These places are also very quiet and scary. For film directors, such places are good too, as it makes sense that there is no phone signal.

original: Psychologist and 'growth mindset' proponent Carol Dweck spoke of the plasticity of the brain and our ability to develop skills and talents that we might not have been good at to start with. Many of us tend to focus our praise on the end result and seemingly innate talents, e.g. 'You really have an eye for details' or 'You have a real talent for organising events'. However, research suggests that by focusing on the process of how things are done – praising effort, experimentation and problem-solving strategies – we can encourage the development of new skills and the continued honing of talents.
simplified:
Carol Dweck is a mind doctor.
She talks about a "growth mindset."
This means you can learn new things.
Your brain can change.
You can get better at skills.
You can get better at talents.
Even if you were not good before.

We often praise people.
We praise the final thing they do.
We praise their natural skills.
For example, "You see small things well."
Or, "You are good at planning."

But studies show a better way.
Praise *how* people do things.
Praise their hard work.
Praise when they try new ideas.
Praise how they fix problems.
This helps them learn new skills.
They get better at what they do.
reference: Psychologist Carol Dweck talks about the 'growth mindset'. This means the brain can change, and we can learn skills even if we are not good at them at the start. Often, people give praise only for the final result or for natural talent. For example: "You notice small details well" or "You are good at organising events." But research shows it is better to praise the way people work. Saying something like "Good effort" or "Good for trying new ideas" helps people learn new skills and improve their talents.

original: In an attempt to inject some positivity into their feedback, many managers rely on sandwiching negative feedback between two positive comments. However, when feedback becomes such a routine, employees can start to perceive positive feedback as simply a form of sugarcoating the negatives, thus diminishing its value. Instead, positive feedback should not simply be seen as something to cushion the negative, but should be delivered so as to reinforce and encourage good performance.
simplified:
Managers want to give good feedback.
They often put bad comments between good ones.
This is like a sandwich.
But this can become a habit.
Workers might think good words hide bad ones.
So, the good words are not useful.
Good comments should not just make bad news softer.
They should help people do better work.
They should make good work stronger.
reference: Some managers give feedback in a "sandwich" format. They say something good, then something bad, and then something good again. But if they do this too many times, workers may think the good things are fake. They may also think the good ones are there to hide the bad ones. This makes the good feedback weak. Positive feedback should be real. It should help workers feel proud and keep doing the good work.

original: Your manager stops you and says she needs to have a word about your performance in the recent project. You worry about it all weekend, wondering what you might have done wrong. When you step into her office on Monday morning she begins by praising you for the good work you've done on the project, and you wonder if this is the obligatory praise that starts off the typical 'feedback sandwich'. You know how the feedback sandwich goes: say something nice, say what you really want to say, say something nice again.
simplified:
Your manager stops you. She wants to talk about your work. It is about the last project.
You worry all weekend. You think: "What did I do wrong?"
On Monday, you go to her office. She starts. She says your work on the project was good. You think: "Is this just nice words?" This is how a 'feedback sandwich' starts.
You know this 'sandwich'. First, she says something good. Then, she says the real problem. Last, she says something good again.
reference: Your manager tells you she wants to talk to you about your work on the last project. You feel worried all weekend and think you may have done something wrong. On Monday, you go to her office. She begins by saying good things about your work. You are not sure if this is the "feedback sandwich." The feedback sandwich is when someone says something good, then says something bad, and then says something good to finish.

original: As for news stories that make us think the world is an increasingly violent place, there is cause for some optimism too. Between the end of World War II and 1990, there were 30 wars that killed more than 100,000 people. Today there are still civil wars, but countries are mostly co-existing more peacefully than in the past. However, terrorism has shot up in the last few years and, since World War II, wars have killed many more civilians than soldiers. Even for civilians, though, the statistics are not all bad. Although deaths are nine times more likely to be a result of violent crime than political conflict, the global murder rate fell slightly, from 8 per 100,000 people in 2000 to about 5.3 in 2015.
simplified:
News can make us think the world is dangerous. But there is also good news.

From 1945 to 1990, there were 30 big wars. Many people died in these wars. Today, some countries still have wars inside them. But countries live together more peacefully now.

But terrorism is now a bigger problem. Wars have killed many normal people. They killed more normal people than soldiers.

For normal people, the news is not all bad. More people die from crime. Fewer people die from political fights.

The number of murders went down. In 2000, 8 people out of 100,000 were murdered. In 2015, it was 5.3 people. This is good news.
reference: The news often makes us think the world is getting more violent, but there is some hope. Between the end of World War II and 1990, 30 wars killed more than 100,000 people each. Today, there are still civil wars, but many countries live more peacefully than before. Terrorism has grown in the last years, and since World War II, wars have killed more peopl than soldiers. But not all statistics are bad. People are nine times more likely to die from violent crime than from war, but the world murder rate has gone down, from 8 per 100,000 people in 2000 to about 5.3 in 2015.

original: The majority of people believe that developing countries are in a terrible situation: suffering from incredible poverty, governed by dictators and with little hope for any meaningful change. But, surprisingly, this is far from the truth. The reality is that a great transformation is occurring. Over the past 20 years, more than 700 million people have increased their income and come out of poverty. Additionally, six million fewer children die every year from disease, millions more girls are in school and millions of people have access to clean water.
simplified:
Many people think poor countries are in a bad situation. They are very poor. Bad leaders rule them. People think things will not get better. But this is not true. A big change is happening.

In the last 20 years, 700 million people got more money. They are not poor anymore. Also, 6 million fewer children die from sickness each year. Many more girls go to school. Many people have clean water.
reference: Most people believe that poor countries have no hope. They think these countries only have poverty, bad leaders, and no change. But this is not true. A big change is happening. In the past 20 years, 700 million people got more money and are no longer poor. Every year, six million fewer children die from illness. More gilrls go to school now, and people can drink clean water.

original: Businesses have caught on to the profitability of the sharing economy and are seeking to gain from making use of those underutilised resources. A business model that has rapidly risen in popularity sees companies providing an online platform that puts customers in contact with those who can provide a particular product or service. Companies like Airbnb act as a middleman for people to cash in on their unused rooms and houses and let them out as lucrative accommodation. Another example is Uber, which encourages people to use their own personal cars as taxis to make some extra cash in their free time.
simplified:
Companies want to make money. They use things people do not use all the time.
A new business idea is popular. Companies make a website or app. This connects people. Some people have things. Other people want to use them.
Look at Airbnb. It helps people. People have rooms or houses. They do not use them all the time. They can rent these places. They earn money.
Uber is another example. People can use their own cars. They drive them like taxis. They can earn more money. They do this in their free time.
reference: Many businesses know they can make money from the sharing economy. This means using things that people are not using all the time. One idea is to make a website or app to connect people who can provide a service. For example, Airbnb helps people rent out their free rooms or houses to travellers. Another example is Uber. It lets people use their own cars as taxis and earn some extra cash.

original: Gary Collins, an off-duty policeman, was watching the London riots on TV. He immediately recognised several people and cut his holiday short to help with identification. He ended up spending six months going through the CCTV film and managed to identify 190 people, many from their eyes alone. His help was of decisive importance in the investigation. Even with 200,000 hours of footage, facial recognition software managed to identify just one person.
simplified:
Gary Collins was a policeman.
He was on holiday.
He watched the London riots on TV.
He knew many people.
He stopped his holiday early.
He wanted to help find them.
He spent six months.
He watched videos from cameras.
He found 190 people.
He knew many just by their eyes.
His help was very important.
It helped the police work.
There were 200,000 hours of video.
A computer program looked at faces.
It found only one person.
reference: Gary Collins, a policeman on holiday, was watching the London street fight on TV. He saw some people he knew and stopped his holiday to help. In six months, he studied CCTV videos and found 190 people, many just by looking at their eyes. His help was very important in the police work. The computer software for face identification only found one person in 200,000 hours of film.

original: This horror film cliché was especially popular with horror films of the late 20th century. It starts with a group of teenagers all enjoying themselves, and it ends with everyone dead except one girl. At the beginning the girl is usually innocent, shy and not particularly strong. By the end, she has become the toughest and most resourceful person in the world. The last girl almost always wins in the end.
simplified:
This is a common story in scary movies.
It was very popular in old films.
It starts with young people having fun.
Then, everyone dies.
But one girl lives.
At first, the girl is good.
She is shy.
She is not strong.
At the end, she is very strong.
She is also very clever.
The last girl usually wins.
reference: This type of movie was very common in the late 20th century. At the beginning, many teenagers are having fun. At the end, only one girl is still active. At first, the girl is shy, quiet and not strong. But later, she becames brave and clever. In the end, the "last girl" usually wins.

original: A fast-paced, foot-tapping rock album, Born in the USA's lyrics nevertheless carry emotional weight. Behind the catchy rock melodies that drive these powerhouse classics are stories of the dark side of the American dream. Many tracks deal with the struggles of hard-working ordinary people and the bitterness and anger they feel as life doesn't bring them riches or glory. The song Glory Days, for example, is about people in a small town looking back at when they were young and had the world at their feet while Downbound Train tells the story of a young man whose life is ruined when he loses his job. It's not hard to imagine that the artist is channelling real people he knew and the life he might have had if he hadn't become a star. The album will leave you in no doubt of the unique and extraordinary talent of the Boss.
simplified:
Born in the USA is a rock album. It is fast and fun. But the words are sad.
The music is good. But the songs tell stories. They show the hard parts of life in America.
Many songs are about normal people. They work hard. But they have problems. They feel sad and angry. They do not get rich or famous.
For example, Glory Days is a song. It is about people in a small town. They remember when they were young. They had a good future then. Downbound Train is another song. It is about a young man. His life becomes bad. He loses his job.
We can think this. The artist writes about people he knew. He writes about the life he could have had. This is if he was not famous.
This album will show you. The Boss has a special skill. He is very good.
reference: Born in the USA is a rock album with fast music that makes you want to move, but the words of the songs are serious. They tell stories about the hard side of the American dream. Many songs are about working people who try hard but do not get rich or famous. For example, Glory Days is about people in a small town remembering when they were young, and Downbound Train is about a young man who loses his job and his life becomes sad. The singer seems to sing about real people he knew, and the life he might have had if he were not a star. The album shows that "the Boss" has special talent.

original: I'm a member of the Campaign to Stop Killer Robots. Forget the movie image of a terrifying Terminator stamping on human skulls and think of what's happening right now: military machines like drones, gun turrets and sentry robots are already being used to kill with very little human input. The next step will be autonomous 'murderbots', following orders but ultimately deciding who to kill on their own. It seems clear to me that this would be completely unethical and dangerous for humanity. We need to be very cautious indeed about what we ask machines to do.
simplified:
I am in a group. This group wants to stop robots that kill.
Don't think about scary robots from films. Think about today.
Army machines are used now.
These machines are like drones. (A drone is a flying robot.)
They are also like guns that shoot alone.
These machines can kill people. Humans do not control them much.
Soon, there will be new robots. They will get orders.
But these robots will choose who to kill. They will decide by themselves.
I think this is very bad. It is dangerous for everyone.
We must be very careful. We must think about what machines do.
reference: I belong to the Campaign to Stop Killer Robots. Don't think about movie robots like the Terminator. Think about this now: armies already use machines like drones, big guns, and guard robots to kill with little help from people. The next step may be "murderbots". These are robots that take orders but then choose for themselves who to kill. I think this is very bad and dangous for people. We must be very careful about what we make the machine do.

original: Best-selling author Terrie Sharp knows how to tell a good story or two, having twice won the Olive Crime Writer Award. Born on the housing estate with the highest crime rate in Glasgow, she learned to keep quiet, stay out of trouble and how to open car doors with a knife. Luckily, she only used her knowledge to write her novels and she's not so quiet these days, appearing on popular daytime shows like Police Today and at writing conferences throughout the UK.
simplified:
Terrie Sharp writes popular books.
She tells good stories.
She won the Olive Crime Writer Award two times.
She grew up in Glasgow.
Her area had a lot of crime.
She learned to be quiet.
She learned to avoid problems.
She also learned to open car doors with a knife.
But she only used this skill for her books.
Now she is not quiet.
She is on TV shows like 'Police Today'.
She also goes to writing events.
These are all over the UK.
reference: Terrie Sharp is a very popular writer, and her books sell well. She has won the Olive Crime Writer Award two times. She was born in Glasgow, a place with a lot of crime. As a child, she learned to be quiet, stay safe, and even how to open car doors with a knife. Luckily, she only used this for her stories. Now she is not quiet, she goes on TV shows like Police Today and gives talks at writing conferences in the UK.

original: The Scallion is printed weekly and distributed free in faculty buildings, with a readership of approximately 10,000 students. It is written and produced entirely by students. The survey shows that the newspaper is highly valued by university students and staff for entertainment, cultural enrichment and work experience. The cost of printing newspapers is significant. Furthermore, some students do not have easy access to the paper, since the only way to obtain a copy is to physically go to university. An additional environmental issue is that a large number of copies end up as litter on campus.
simplified:
The Scallion is a newspaper. It is printed every week. You can get it for free. It is in university buildings. About 10,000 students read it.

Students write and make it. A study says this. Students like the paper. Teachers like it too. It is fun. You can learn about culture. Students get work experience.

Printing the paper costs a lot. Some students cannot get it easily. They must go to the university. This is the only way to get a copy.

There is another problem. Many papers become trash. This is bad for nature. It happens at the university.
reference: The Scallion is a student newspaper. It is printed every week and given out free in university buildings. Around 10,000 students read it. Students write and produce the paper. A survey says students and teachers like it for fun, culture, and work experience. But printing costs a lot. Some students cannot get the paper easily, as they have to go to the university to take a copy. There is also an environmental problem: many copies are left as rubbish on campus.

original: Spider venom is present in most species and serves the purpose of stunning or killing their prey rather than attacking humans. In fact, only 25 of the known spider species produce venom which can actually harm humans, and although spider bites can be painful, they are rarely deadly. Australia's notorious Sydney funnel-web spider has not produced any fatalities since anti-venom was developed in 1981. However, take care not to rub hairy spiders like tarantulas up the wrong way. When they feel in danger, they defend themselves by ejecting a cloud of urticating hairs. These irritating hairs then embed themselves in the skin or eyes of the attacker.
simplified:
Most spiders have venom. Venom is a special liquid. They use it to catch food. They do not use it to hurt people.

Only a few kinds of spiders have venom that can hurt people. Spider bites can hurt. But they usually do not kill.

A spider in Australia is called the Sydney funnel-web. No one has died from its bite since 1981. This is because of a special medicine. It is called anti-venom.

But be careful with hairy spiders. Like tarantulas. Do not make them angry.

If they feel scared, they protect themselves. They shoot out tiny hairs. These hairs can sting. These hairs stick in your skin or eyes.
reference: Most spiders have venom, but it is for catching food, not for hurting people. Only about 25 kinds of spiders can harm humans. A spider bite can be painful, but it rarely kills. In Australia, the Sydney funnel-web spider has not killed anyone since doctors made an anti-venom in 1981. But be careful with hairy spiders like tarantulas. If they feel danger, they throw out tiny hairs. These hairs can get into your skin or eyes and make them very sore.

original: In older horror films, when protagonists were in desperation, it was difficult or impossible for them to call for help or call the police. Mobile phones have made that situation a bit less believable now. What's the solution to maintain suspense? No phone coverage! If you're a hero in a horror film, it's almost certain that at a key moment, just when you absolutely need to call for help, you will not have any coverage at all. Or your phone battery will die just as you are making the call. Or both.
simplified:
In old scary movies, main characters were in trouble. They could not call for help. They could not call the police. It was hard to do.

Cell phones make this less real now. What is the answer? How to keep it scary? No phone signal!

You are a hero in a scary movie. You need to call for help. But you will have no signal. This is often true at a key time. Or your phone battery dies. This happens when you call. Or both things happen.
reference: In old horror films, the main characters could not easily call for help or the police. But now people have mobile phones, so this problem looks less true. How do films keep the story scary? The answer is no phone signal! In many horror films, when the hero really needs to call, there is no signal. Or the phone battery dies while they are calling. Sometimes both happen.

original: It is society, not nature, that tells us girls should favour arts and humanities and leave maths and physics to the boys. Coupled with this is the lack of positive female role models youngsters see doing science-related jobs. Cartoons and stories often show the crazy scientist, genius inventor, or adventurous astronaut as a man. Furthermore, there is an unfortunate perception that scientists are geeky, have poor social skills or that their work is lonely and detached from the rest of the world. These are false stereotypes portrayed by the media, but they may mean that girls do not identify with scientists, and see science as an unappealing career path. If girls saw more positive female role models in science it would give them more confidence and a greater sense of belonging in those subjects.
simplified:
People tell girls to like art. They tell boys to like science. This is not how we are born.

Girls do not see many women in science jobs. A role model is someone you look up to.
TV shows and books often show men as scientists. They show them as inventors. Or as astronauts.

Some people think scientists are strange. They think scientists are not good with people. They think scientists work alone.

These ideas are not true. TV and books show them.
Girls might not want to be scientists. They might think science is not a good job.

If girls saw more women scientists, they would feel better. They would feel like they belong.
reference: Society tells us that girls should choose arts and humanities, and boys should choose maths and physics. Another problem is that children do not often see women working in science. In cartoons and stories, the scientist, inventor, or astronaut is usually a man. People also think scientists are strange, not good at talking to others, or always working alone. These ideas are not true, but they can make girls feel that science is not for them. If girls saw more women in science, they would feel more confident and feel that they belong in those subjects.

original: So much of what the speaker said rang true. I honestly believe there's a danger that the more connected we are, the more isolated we feel. I don't think this is such an issue for my generation who've lived without technology for so long. We know how to be alone and, more importantly, we know that it's OK to be alone. But the under 20s are another kettle of fish. They're so busy communicating that they never experience the feeling of solitude and run the risk of not learning how to enjoy their own company. In addition, they're learning conversation through messages that can be edited and changed at the expense of learning the art of real conversation in real time with the person in front of you.
simplified:
The speaker said many true things.
I think there is a problem.
We talk to many people online.
But we feel more alone.
This is not a problem for people my age.
We lived without technology for a long time.
We know how to be alone.
We know it is okay to be alone.
But young people are different.
They talk online a lot.
They do not have quiet time.
They might not learn to like being alone.
Also, they learn to talk by messages.
They can change these messages.
They do not learn real talks.
Real talks are with people in person.
reference: I agreed with much of what the speaker said. I think that when people are more connected, they can sometimes feel lonelier. For my generation, this is not such a big problem, because we lived many years without modern technology. We know how to be alone, and we know it is OK. But for people under 20, it is different. They spend so much time sending messages that they do not feel real solitude. They may not learn how to enjoy being alone. They also talk by messages that can be changed, instead of learning face-to-face conversations.

original: In the 1950s, Central American commercial banana growers were facing the death of their most lucrative product, the Gros Michel banana, known as Big Mike. And now it's happening again to Big Mike's successor – the Cavendish. With its easily transported, thick-skinned and sweet-tasting fruit, the Gros Michel banana plant dominated the plantations of Central America. United Fruit, the main grower and exporter in South America at the time, mass-produced its bananas in the most efficient way possible: it cloned shoots from the stems of plants instead of growing plants from seeds, and cultivated them in densely packed fields.
simplified:
In the 1950s, banana farmers in Central America had a problem.
They were losing their best banana.
This banana was called Gros Michel.
People also called it Big Mike.
It was their most important product.

Now, the same problem is happening again.
It is happening to the Cavendish banana.
This banana came after Big Mike.

The Gros Michel banana was good.
It was easy to move.
Its skin was thick.
The fruit tasted sweet.
This banana was on most farms in Central America.

United Fruit was a big company.
They grew and sold many bananas then.
They grew bananas in a special way.
They took small parts from banana plants.
They did not use seeds.
They grew many plants close together.
This made many bananas quickly.
reference: In the 1950s, banana farmers in Central America had a big problem. Their best banana, called Gros Michel or Big Mike, was dying. Now the same problem is happening to its replacement, the Cavendish. Big Mike was very popular because it was sweet, had a thick skin, and was easy to carry and sell. United Fruit, the biggest company, grew these bananas by taking shoots from the plant stems instead of seeds. They planted the bananas very close to each other in larger fields.

original: Overall, more people are learning English than the other languages combined and English is spoken in the highest number of countries. However, Chinese has by far the greatest number of native speakers. There seems to be little correlation between how many native speakers there are of a language and the number of learners, but there is a stronger link between the number of learners and how many countries have speakers.
simplified:
Many people learn English. They learn it more than other languages. English is spoken in many countries.

But many people speak Chinese. They learned it as their first language.

Some languages have many first language speakers. But not many people learn these languages. However, if many countries speak a language, many people learn it.
reference: Today, more people learn English than all other languages. English is also spoken in most countries. But Chinese has the most native speakers, which means people who speak it from birth. There is no big link between the number of native speakers and learners. But there is a stronger link between the number of learners and how many countries speak that language.

original: At Girox Foods, we are experiencing an annual employee turnover of about 12 per cent. Although this might not seem high at first glance, the industry standard is seven per cent. The principal objective of this report is to investigate the causes of employee engagement within the firm and, based on those, offer recommendations to improve the employees' experience of the workplace and increase employee retention.
simplified:
At Girox Foods, many workers leave their jobs. This is called staff turnover.
About 12 out of 100 workers leave each year.
This number may seem fine.
But other companies lose fewer staff.
They lose 7 out of 100 workers.
This report has a main goal.
We want to find out why staff leave.
We also want to know why staff stay.
We will look at how happy workers are.
Then, we will suggest new ideas.
These ideas will make work better for staff.
They will help more workers stay at Girox Foods.
reference: At Girox Foods, around 12% of workers leave the company every year. This looks small, but in the same industry, the normal number is only 7%. The goal of this report is to look at why workers feel they belong in the company and then give ideas to make the workplace better. The goal is that this will help more workers stay in the job.

original: If we want to know where our capability for complex language came from, we need to look at how our brains are different from other animals. This relates to more than just brain size; it is important what other things our brains can do and when and why they evolved that way. And for this there are very few physical clues; artefacts left by our ancestors don't tell us what speech they were capable of making. One thing we can see in the remains of early humans, however, is the development of the mouth, throat and tongue. By about 100,000 years ago, humans had evolved the ability to create complex sounds. Before that, evolutionary biologists can only guess whether or not early humans communicated using more basic sounds.
simplified: We want to know how we learned to speak. We need to look at our brains. Our brains are different from animal brains. It is not just about brain size. What our brains can do is important. We also need to know when and why they changed. We have few clues. Old things from our ancestors do not tell us. They do not tell us how they spoke. But we can see one thing. We can see the bones of old people. Their mouth, throat, and tongue changed. About 100,000 years ago, humans changed. They could make many sounds. Before that time, scientists can only guess. Did old humans use simple sounds to talk?
reference: To know how humans learned complex language, we must look at how our brains are different from animals' brains. It is not only about the size of the brain, but also about what it can do, and when and why it changes. There are not many clues, as old subjects cannot tell us what kind of speech early humans had. But we can see changes in the mouth, throat, and tongue of early human bones. Around 100,000 years ago, humans got the ability to make complex sounds. Before that, scientists could only guess if early humans used simple sounds to talk.

original: Lewis would like to see the number of marine protected areas in the world increase from 3 per cent to 10 per cent in an attempt to reverse the damage caused by human activity such as overfishing, polluting and littering. During his expeditions, Lewis has witnessed this environmental destruction first-hand. He's swum over coral reefs bleached by the increase in water temperature, and observed underwater deserts beneath the shallow waters of the Red Sea, devoid of life and strewn with plastic. Pugh believes that nature can recover if it is given space to do so, but the clock is ticking. If we don't start looking after our seas, we may soon have an unsolvable problem on our hands.
simplified:
Lewis wants more safe places in the sea.
He wants 10% instead of 3%.
This will fix harm from people.
People catch too many fish.
They make the sea dirty.
They throw rubbish.
Lewis saw this harm on his trips.
He saw it with his own eyes.
He swam over sea corals.
The corals lost their colour.
This was because the water was warmer.
He saw empty places under the sea.
These were in the Red Sea.
There was no life there.
They were full of plastic.
He thinks nature can get better.
We must give it room.
But we do not have much time.
We must take care of our seas.
If not, we will have a big problem.
We cannot fix it.
reference: Lewis wants more parts of the sea to be protected. At the moment, only 3% is protected, and he wants this to be 10%. He hopes this will help fix the damage people cause, like too much fishing, pollution, and rubbish in the sea. On his trips, Lewis saw this damage himself. He swam over coral that had lost its colour because the water was too hot. In the Red Sea, he saw places with no fish, but plastic. Pugh believes nature can heal if we give it space, but we must do it quickly. If we do not take care of the sea now, it may soon be too late.

original: Are things getting worse every day? Is progress an impossible goal? In Enlightenment Now, Steven Pinker looks at the big picture of human progress and finds good news. We are living longer, healthier, freer and happier lives. The real problem, Pinker argues, is that the Enlightenment values of reason and science are under attack. When commentators and demagogues appeal to people's tribalism, fatalism and distrust, then we are in danger of causing irreparable damage to important institutions like democracy and world co-operation.
simplified:
Are things getting worse every day?
Is it impossible to make things better?

Steven Pinker wrote a book.
It is called 'Enlightenment Now'.
He looks at how humans get better.
He finds good news.

We live longer.
We are healthier.
We are more free.
We are happier.

But Pinker says there is a problem.
Some people do not like good ideas.
These ideas are about thinking and science.

Some people talk badly.
They make people angry and afraid.
This can hurt important things.
Like how we choose our leaders.
Or how countries work together.
reference: Are things getting worse? Is progress impossible? In his book Enlightenment Now, Steven Pinker says there is good news. People now live longer, healthier, and happier lives with more freedom. But Pinker also warns us. He says that clear thinking and science are under attack. Some people make people follow only their own group, lose hope, and stop trusting others. If this happens, imporatant things like democracy and countries working together may be badly damaged.

original: Don't always follow positive feedback with negative feedback. When positive and negative feedback always appear to go hand in hand, the positives can become devalued and ignored. Ensure there are times when positive feedback is given for its own sake and resist the temptation to offer constructive criticism.
simplified:
Give good words. Do not always add advice to make things better.
If you always give good words and advice together, the good words lose their power.
People might not listen to them.
Sometimes, only give good words.
Give them just because they are good.
Do not give advice to make things better then.
Even if you want to help.
reference: Do not always say something bad after saying something good. If good and bad comments always come together, the good words may not feel real. Sometimes, give good feedback only, and try not to add any criticism.

original: One of the most interesting cases of wild animals living in a city are the wild dogs of Moscow. In Moscow, there are approximately 35,000 wild dogs living on the streets. Some of the dogs were born wild, while others are pets that have been abandoned by their owners. Some dogs live alone and others live in packs. In 2010, scientists studied the dogs and found that the dogs have adapted remarkably successfully to urban life. They have learned that it is safer to cross the street with people and some dogs appear to understand traffic lights.
simplified: The wild dogs of Moscow are a very interesting example of wild animals that live in a city. In Moscow, there are about 35,000 wild dogs, which have made the city streets their home. Some of these dogs were born wild, while others were pets that their owners left behind. Some dogs live alone, however, others prefer to live in groups, which are called packs. In 2010, scientists researched these dogs and discovered that they had adapted very well to city life. Some of them were born in the wild, and others were once pets but were left by their owners. Some dogs live alone, and some stay in groups. In 2010, scientists studied them and found that the dogs have learned to live well in the city. They often cross the street with people, and some even seem to understand traffic lights.

simplified: Chloe has two pet rats, Zena and Roxy. original: Is graffiti art or vandalism? This depends on your point of view, but in many countries, writing or painting on public or private property is considered vandalism. simplified: People often ask if graffiti is art or vandalism, and the answer depends on your personal opinion. Many artists who create street art have been stopped by the police, and some of them have even paid fines because of this. reference: Some people see graffiti as art, while others think it is vandalism. In many countries, painting or writing on public or private property is against the law. Street artists are often stopped by the police, and some are fined. City councils often complain about how expensive it is to clean graffiti from walls, buses, and trains.

original: By bringing people and animals together, zoos have the potential to educate the public about conservation issues and inspire people to protect animals and their habitats. simplified: Zoos bring people and animals together, so they can teach the public about protecting nature and encourage them to protect animals and their natural homes. reference: Zoos connect people with animals and help teach the public about protecting animals and the environment. Some zoos give a safe home to animals that were treated badly in circuses or pets that were abandoned. Zoos also do important research on animal behaviour and how to treat their illnesses.

original: Your dreams might show you all kinds of insights into things that you didn't realise you were thinking about. Common dreams like being able to fly or falling, your teeth falling out or having no clothes on in a public place probably mean something similar in most people. But the key to understanding exactly what they mean to you is to connect them to the events and feelings in your daily life.
simplified: Your dreams might show you many insights into things that you did not know you were thinking about. Common dreams, like flying, falling, losing your teeth, or being naked in public, probably have a similar meaning for many people. However, to truly understand what these dreams mean for you, you must connect them to the events and feelings in your daily life.
reference: Dreams can tell us something about our thoughts and feelings, even if we don't realise it. Many people have similar dreams, like flying, falling, losing teeth, or being in public without clothes. These dreams often have the same meaning for most people. To really understand your dream, you should think about your daily life and emotions.

original: A large number of bridge accidents occur during the construction of the bridge itself. These accidents are often due to an error made by the engineers, such as a miscalculation. The bridge collapses under its own weight, and this can be deadly for the workers on it at the time.

reference: Many bridge accidents happen during construction. These are often caused by mistakes made by engineers, such as wrong calculations. When this happens, the bridge may collapse under its own weight, which can be deadly for the workers on it at the time.

original: Many city residents in Berlin, Germany complained that shooting pigs was unnecessarily cruel and there were heated arguments between hunters and animal lovers. simplified: Many city residents in Berlin, Germany, complained that shooting pigs was unnecessarily cruel, which led to strong arguments between hunters and animal lovers. Time will tell if this strategy works, although it might be a difficult fight because warmer winters mean there are more pigs than before.
reference: In Berlin, Germany, many local people complained that shooting pigs was too cruel. This caused strong arguments between hunters and animal lovers. Because of the protests, the city council chose a more peaceful solution. They put up fences and made it against the law to feed wild pigs. It's not clear if the plan will work, since warmer winters have caused the number of pigs to grow more than before.

original: An important inspiration for the Hunger Games book comes from Suzanne's love of classical Greek mythology. When she was a child, one of her favourite stories was Theseus and the Minotaur. simplified: An important inspiration for The Hunger Games book comes from Suzanne's love of classical Greek mythology. When she was a child, one of her favourite stories was Theseus and the Minotaur. reference: One big inspiration for The Hunger Games came from Suzanne Collins' love of ancient Greek myths. As a child, one of her favourite stories was Theseus and the Minotaur. In the story, Athens is controlled by Crete, and every year the king of Crete, Minos, makes the Athenians send seven boys and seven girls. These children are sent into a maze where a monster, the Minotaur, lives. Theseus, one of the children, kills the monster. Suzanne sees her character Katniss as a modern version of Theseus.

original: What does the art world think of graffiti and street art? Recently, there has been a growing recognition of its value as an art form. simplified: The art world is now starting to accept graffiti and street art as a real art form. reference: How does the art world view graffiti and street art? Recently, more people have started to see it as a real form of art. Large exhibitions featuring street art have been held in cities like Paris, London, and Los Angeles. In 2008, American artist Elura Emerald organised a street art exhibition in a New York gallery. She supported street artists, saying they are simply expressing themselves and not doing harm, and that they should be respected and celebrated.

original: Cape Town can be a dangerous place for baboons. Some have been injured or killed in car accidents and others have been electrocuted as they played with electric cables.
