The monitors' job is to chase baboons out of urban areas or catch them and release them in the countryside. This policy has had some success, though it is proving hard to stop baboons from coming back to the city once they see it as a source of easy food.
simplified: Cape Town can be a dangerous place for baboons. Some baboons have been hurt or killed in car accidents, and others have received electric shocks when they played with electric cables. Baboons are an endangered species, which is why the city council has hired a team of Baboon Monitors to protect them and reduce conflicts with people. The job of these monitors is to chase baboons out of city areas or catch them and then release them in the countryside. This plan has had some success, although it is difficult to stop baboons from returning to the city because they find easy food there.
reference: Cape Town is a risky place for baboons. Some are injured or killed by cars, and others are electrocuted when they touch electric wires. Because baboons are an endangered species, the city has hired a group called Baboon Monitors. Their job is to keep baboons out of the city by chasing them away or catching them and releasing them in the countryside. This plan has worked somewhat, but it's difficult to stop the baboons from returning since they see the city as a place to find easy food.

original: Social media, magazines and shop windows bombard people daily with things to buy, and British consumers are buying more clothes and shoes than ever before. simplified: Social media, magazines, and shop windows often show people many things to buy, and British consumers are buying more clothes and shoes than ever before. original: Sam squinted against the sun at the distant dust trail raked up by the car on its way up to the Big House. The horses kicked and flicked their tails at flies, not caring about their owner's first visit in ten months. Sam waited. Mr Carter didn't come out here unless he had to, which was just fine by Sam. The more he kept out of his boss's way, the longer he'd have a job. Mr, Carter wiped the sweat from the back of his neck. The damp patches on his shirt drew together like shapes in an atlas. His skin was already turning ruddy in the June sun. Otherwise he had the indoor tan of a man that made money while other people did the work.
simplified: Sam squinted at the distant dust trail, which the car made as it went up to the Big House. The horses kicked and flicked their tails at flies, but they did not care about their owner's first visit in ten months. Sam waited, because Mr Carter did not come here unless it was necessary, which Sam liked. The more he kept out of his boss's way, the longer he would have his job. Mr Carter wiped the sweat from the back of his neck. The damp patches on his shirt came together like shapes in an atlas. His skin was already becoming reddish in the June sun. Otherwise, he had the pale skin of a man who made money while other people did the work.
reference: Sam narrowed his eyes at the dust in the distance. A car was coming up to the Big House. The horses kicked and moved their tails to stop the flies, not caring that their owner hadn't visited for ten months. Sam stood and waited. Mr. Carter only came when necessary, and Sam was happy about that. The less he saw his boss, the safer his job was. Mr. Carter wiped sweat from his neck. His shirt had wet spots, and his skin was getting red from the summer sun. Normally, he stayed indoors, making money while others did the hard work.

original: I work for a global IT company, but because their headquarters is in the States, I do all my work online from home. The downside is that without clear office hours, I tend to work well into the evening, sometimes skipping dinner to finish a task.
simplified: I work for a large technology company, but because its main office is in the United States, I do all my work online from home. reference: I work for a global IT company, but since the main office is in the United States, I do all of my work from home online. I can take time off if my children have something at school or if I need to go to the dentist. However, there is a disadvantage. Without clear office hours, I often work late into the evening and sometimes miss dinner just to finish a task.

original: A different trend is springing up in opposition to consumerism – the 'buy nothing' trend. The idea originated in Canada in the early 1990s and then moved to the US, where it became a rejection of the overspending and overconsumption of Black Friday and Cyber Monday during Thanksgiving weekend. On Buy Nothing Day people organise various types of protests and cut up their credit cards. Throughout the year, Buy Nothing groups organise the exchange and repair of items they already own.
simplified: A new trend is appearing against consumerism, which is called the 'buy nothing' trend. This idea started in Canada in the early 1990s and then came to the US, where it opposed the huge spending and buying of Black Friday and Cyber Monday during Thanksgiving weekend. reference: A new movement against consumerism is growing – it's called the 'buy nothing' trend. It started in Canada in the early 1990s and then spread to the US. People involved in this movement want to avoid overspending, especially during shopping events like Black Friday and Cyber Monday. On Buy Nothing Day, they hold protests and even cut up their credit cards. Throughout the year, they also organise activities to repair or exchange used items instead of buying new ones.

original: The Hunger Games takes place in the future, after the destruction of North America. The country is called Panem and is made up of twelve poor districts governed by the wealthy Capitol. The Capitol controls the entire country. Each district has its own job and sends goods to the Capitol. The story begins in District 12, which produces coal. original: Another suggested defence against a PHA on course to hit Earth is to blow it up using a nuclear weapon. It may sound like a plot from a film, and it was the subject of the 1998 film Armageddon, but the Hypervelocity Asteroid Mitigation Mission for Emergency Response (HAMMER) is a genuine NASA proposal. The eight-ton rockets would be fired at an approaching asteroid with the hope of bumping it off course. If the asteroid was too close to Earth for this plan to work, the rockets would carry nuclear bombs to blow it up instead.
simplified: Another possible way to protect Earth from a dangerous asteroid that is coming towards it is to destroy it with a nuclear weapon. The plan involves firing eight-ton rockets at an approaching asteroid, which would hopefully push it off its course. If the asteroid was too close to Earth for this method to succeed, the rockets would carry nuclear bombs to destroy it instead.
reference: Another way to stop an asteroid from hitting Earth is to destroy it with a nuclear weapon. This may sound like a film story, and it was actually in the 1998 film Armageddon. However, the Hypervelocity Asteroid Mitigation Mission for Emergency Response (HAMMER) is a real project from NASA. The plan was to send eight-ton heavy rockets towards an asteroid to push it away from its path. If the asteroid is already too close to Earth, the rockets could carry nuclear bombs to break it apart.

original: Often wild animals come into cities to look for food. In Cape Town, South Africa, baboons have started coming into residential areas on the edge of the city to feed. They open rubbish bins and eat fruit from gardens and orchards. Some brave baboons have even come into people's houses and taken food from kitchen cupboards and fridges! Baboons can be aggressive and have attacked a lot of pet animals, so understandably, many city residents don't welcome their presence.
simplified: Wild animals often come into cities because they are looking for food. reference: Wild animals often enter cities in search of food. In Cape Town, South Africa, baboons have begun coming into areas where people live. They open rubbish bins and eat fruit from gardens and orchards. Some even go into homes and take food from kitchen cupboards and fridges. Since baboons can be aggressive and have attacked many pets, it's easy to understand why many city residents don't want them nearby.

original: If most people have four to six dreams every night after the age of ten, that's as many as 2,000 dreams per year. So, by the time they reach 80 years old the average person might have had 140,000 dreams. Even if we forget 95–99 per cent of our dreams, that's still a few thousand remembered dreams across a lifetime. It's not too difficult to believe that, by coincidence, a dream event is followed by a real-life event that's similar to it, especially if the subject of the dream is something that happens often in everyday life.
simplified: If most people have four to six dreams every night after they are ten years old, this means about 2,000 dreams each year. Therefore, when people reach 80 years old, the average person might have had 140,000 dreams. However, even if we forget 95–99 percent of our dreams, we still remember a few thousand dreams during our lives. It is not difficult to believe that a dream event might, by chance, be followed by a real-life event which is similar, especially if the dream's subject is something that often happens in daily life.
reference: After the age of ten, most people have between four and six dreams each night. That adds up to about 2,000 dreams a year. By the time someone turns 80, they may have had around 140,000 dreams. Even though we forget most dreams–about 95 to 99 percent–we still remember thousands over a lifetime. So, it's not hard to believe that sometimes a dream is followed by a real-life event that feels similar, especially when it's about something that happens often in everyday life.

original: George Lucas was one of the early film directors to directly base his story on the 17 stages of the hero's journey. simplified: George Lucas was an important film director who created his stories using the 17 stages of the hero's journey. reference: George Lucas was one of the first film directors to base a story on the 17 stages of the hero's journey. original: Underutilised items may seem useless to some, but could be an asset to others. simplified: Items that people do not use often may seem useless to some, but they could be an asset to others. reference: Some things that are not often used may look useless to people, but they can be valuable to others. With the internet, online groups have found a way to make money by sharing unused items. With websites and social media pages that help people buy and sell second-hand goods, it is now easier for people to share items with each other. This is called the sharing economy.

original: In some areas, councils have tried to encourage artists not to paint graffiti randomly on walls by allowing them to work in designated areas. simplified: In some places, local councils have tried to encourage artists not to paint graffiti anywhere on walls, by allowing them to work in special areas. original: Psychologist and 'growth mindset' proponent Carol Dweck spoke of the plasticity of the brain and our ability to develop skills and talents that we might not have been good at to start with. Many of us tend to focus our praise on the end result and seemingly innate talents, e.g. 'You really have an eye for details' or 'You have a real talent for organising events'. However, research suggests that by focusing on the process of how things are done – praising effort, experimentation and problem-solving strategies – we can encourage the development of new skills and the continued honing of talents.
simplified: Carol Dweck, a psychologist and supporter of the 'growth mindset', spoke about the brain's ability to change and our power to develop skills and talents that we lacked at first. However, research shows that by focusing on how things are done – praising effort, trying new things, and strategies for solving problems – we can help new skills grow and talents improve.
reference: Psychologist Carol Dweck, who supports the idea of a 'growth mindset', spoke about how the brain can change and how we can develop skills and talents, even if we were not good at them at firstt. Many people usually give praise for the final result or for natural talent, for example: "You are good at noticing details" or "You are great at organising events." But research shows it is better to focus on the process. By prarisising effort, trying new things, and problem-solving, we can help people build new skills and improve their talents.

original: Are things getting worse every day? Is progress an impossible goal? In Enlightenment Now, Steven Pinker looks at the big picture of human progress and finds good news. We are living longer, healthier, freer and happier lives. The real problem, Pinker argues, is that the Enlightenment values of reason and science are under attack. When commentators and demagogues appeal to people's tribalism, fatalism and distrust, then we are in danger of causing irreparable damage to important institutions like democracy and world co-operation.
simplified: Many people ask if life is getting worse every day or if progress is an impossible goal. However, in his book "Enlightenment Now," Steven Pinker examines the general situation of human progress and discovers positive information. He explains that people are now living longer, healthier, freer, and happier lives, which shows real progress. Nevertheless, Pinker believes that the real problem is that important ideas from the Enlightenment, which include reason and science, are being challenged. When certain speakers and leaders use people's strong group loyalty, their belief that nothing can change, and their distrust, they put important systems like democracy and global co-operation in serious danger.
reference: Are things getting worse every day? Is progress impossible? In Enlightenment Now, Steven Pinker studies the history of human progress and finds much good news. People live longer, healthier, freer, and happier lives. But Pinker warns that the real danger is the attack on Enlightenment values such as reason and science. When leaders and commentators encourage people to think only of their own group, to give up hope, or to stop trusting others, we risk damaging democracy and world co-operation in a way that can't be fixed.

original: Spider venom is present in most species and serves the purpose of stunning or killing their prey rather than attacking humans. Australia's notorious Sydney funnel-web spider has not produced any fatalities since anti-venom was developed in 1981. However, take care not to rub hairy spiders like tarantulas up the wrong way. When they feel in danger, they defend themselves by ejecting a cloud of urticating hairs. These irritating hairs then embed themselves in the skin or eyes of the attacker.
simplified: Most spider species have venom, which they use to stun or kill their prey, not to attack humans. Only 25 known spider species have venom that can harm people, and although their bites can be painful, they are rarely deadly. Australia's notorious Sydney funnel-web spider has not caused any deaths since anti-venom was developed in 1981. However, you should be careful not to upset hairy spiders, such as tarantulas, because they might react badly. When they feel in danger, they defend themselves by releasing a cloud of irritating hairs, which can cause problems. These irritating hairs then stick into the attacker's skin or eyes, which can be very uncomfortable.
reference: Most spiders have venom, but it is mainly used to catch or kill their prey, not to attack humans. In fact, only 25 spider species are dangerous to people. Spider bites can hurt, but they almost never cause death. For example, Australia's famous Sydney funnel-web spider has not killed anyone since an anti-venom was created in 1981. You should be careful with hairy spiders like tarantulas.When they feel in danger, they release tiny sharp hairs that can stick in the skin or eyes of the attacker and cause irritation.

original: This horror film cliché was especially popular with horror films of the late 20th century. It starts with a group of teenagers all enjoying themselves, and it ends with everyone dead except one girl. At the beginning the girl is usually innocent, shy and not particularly strong. By the end, she has become the toughest and most resourceful person in the world. The last girl almost always wins in the end.
simplified: This common idea in horror films was very popular in movies from the end of the 20th century. This type of film usually starts with a group of teenagers who are enjoying themselves, but it ends with everyone dead except one girl. At the beginning of the story, the girl is usually innocent, shy, and not very strong. However, by the end of the film, she has become the strongest and most clever person, which helps her survive. This final girl, who is now very strong, almost always wins in the end.
reference: This horror film cliché was especially popular in the late 20th century. The story usually begins with a group of teenagers having fun, but it ends with all of them dead except for one girl. At first, this girl is often  quite, shy and not very strong. By the end, she becomes brave, smart, and strong enough to survive. The "last girl" almost always win the danger at the end.

original: If we want to know where our capability for complex language came from, we need to look at how our brains are different from other animals. This relates to more than just brain size; it is important what other things our brains can do and when and why they evolved that way. And for this there are very few physical clues; artefacts left by our ancestors don't tell us what speech they were capable of making. One thing we can see in the remains of early humans, however, is the development of the mouth, throat and tongue. By about 100,000 years ago, humans had evolved the ability to create complex sounds. Before that, evolutionary biologists can only guess whether or not early humans communicated using more basic sounds.
simplified: If we want to know how our ability for complex language began, we must look at how our brains are different from other animals. This is more than just brain size; we also need to understand what other things our brains can do, and when and why they developed. However, there are only a few physical clues, because objects which our ancestors left do not tell us what speech they could make. One thing that we can see in the remains of early humans, however, is how their mouth, throat, and tongue developed. By about 100,000 years ago, humans had developed the ability to create complex sounds. Before that time, evolutionary biologists can only guess whether early humans communicated using more basic sounds.
reference: If we want to know where our ability for complex language came from, we need to look at how the human brain is different from the brains of other animals. It is not only about brain size, but also about what our brains can do, when these abilities appreared and why. There are a few physical clues about this, because objects from early humans cannot show us what kind of speech thry used. But one thing we can study is the development of the mouth, throat and tongue. Around 100,000 years ago, humans developed the ability to make complex sounds. Before that, scientists could only guess if early humans used simpler sounds to communicate.

original: The Scallion is printed weekly and distributed free in faculty buildings, with a readership of approximately 10,000 students. It is written and produced entirely by students. The survey shows that the newspaper is highly valued by university students and staff for entertainment, cultural enrichment and work experience. The cost of printing newspapers is significant. Furthermore, some students do not have easy access to the paper, since the only way to obtain a copy is to physically go to university. An additional environmental issue is that a large number of copies end up as litter on campus.
simplified: The Scallion, which is written and produced completely by students, is published every week and given away for free in university buildings, reaching about 10,000 students. A survey shows that university students and staff value the newspaper greatly for entertainment, cultural learning, and work experience. However, printing these newspapers is quite expensive, and some students find it difficult to get a copy because they must go to the university buildings in person to find one. Another problem for the environment is that many copies become rubbish on the university grounds.
reference: The Scallion is printed every week and given out for free in university buildings, with about 10,000 student readers. It is written and produced only by students. The survey shows that both students and staff value the paper for fun, culture, and work experience.However, printing the paper is expensive. Also, some students can not get it easily, as the only way to get a copy is to go to the university. Another problem is the environment: many copies are thrown away as rubbish on campus.

original: At Girox Foods, we are experiencing an annual employee turnover of about 12 per cent. Although this might not seem high at first glance, the industry standard is seven per cent. The principal objective of this report is to investigate the causes of employee engagement within the firm and, based on those, offer recommendations to improve the employees' experience of the workplace and increase employee retention.
simplified: At Girox Foods, about 12 per cent of our employees leave the company each year. However, although this number might not seem high at first, the usual rate for our industry is seven per cent. The main aim of this report is to understand why employees feel connected to our company, and then, based on this, to suggest ways to make their work better and keep them longer.
reference: At Girox Foods, around 12% of employees leave the company each year. This might not look high at first, but the normal level in the industy is about 7%. The main aim of this report is to study the reasons for employee engagement in the company. Based on those, give suggestions to make the workplace better and keep more employees.

original: Chloe has two pet rats, Zena and Roxy. Chloe knows they're not typical pets and she has lost count of the times she's patiently tried to explain to people that rats aren't dirty and they make fantastic pets if you look after them correctly. But she understands why people react badly. She didn't like rats either until her friend Martin showed her his pet rats and she saw how affectionate and intelligent they were. Last year, when one of Martin's rats had babies, Chloe decided she'd like to have two of them.
simplified: Chloe has two pet rats. Their names are Zena and Roxy. Chloe knows rats are not normal pets. She often tells people that rats are clean. She says they are very good pets if you take care of them well. But she knows why people don't like rats. Chloe didn't like rats before. Then her friend Martin showed her his rats. She saw they were friendly and clever. Last year, Martin's rat had babies. Chloe wanted two of them.
reference: Chloe has two pet rats, called Zena and Roxy. She knows that rats are not usual pets, and many people think they are dirty. Chloe often tells people that rats can be very good pets if you take care of them. She didn't like rats before, but her friend Martin showed her his rats. She saw they were kind and clever. Last year, one of Martin's rats had babies. Chloe chose two of them to keep.

original: Your dreams might show you all kinds of insights into things that you didn't realise you were thinking about. Common dreams like being able to fly or falling, your teeth falling out or having no clothes on in a public place probably mean something similar in most people. But the key to understanding exactly what they mean to you is to connect them to the events and feelings in your daily life.
simplified: Your dreams can show you things you think about, but you don't know it. Many people have common dreams. For example, they dream they can fly or they are falling. They might dream their teeth fall out, or they are naked in a public place. These dreams often mean the same thing for many people. But to understand what your dreams mean for *you*, you need to think about your life and how you feel every day.
reference: People have different dreams when they sleep. Some common dreams are flying, falling, losing teeth, or being outside with no clothes. These dreams often mean the same thing for many people. To know what your dream means, think about what is happening in your life and how you feel.

original: Wonder is New Yorker RJ Palacio's first novel. On her website, she explains that the idea for the book came to her after seeing a girl with facial deformities on the street one day. Wonder has been a bestseller in the United States and has already won several awards. Many schools are using it as a starting point for discussions about bullying, friendship and what it's like to be different. A film version is being made, and many, including me, are waiting eagerly to see what RJ Palacio writes next.
simplified: Wonder is the first book by RJ Palacio. She said she got the idea for the book after she saw a girl with a different face on the street. Many people bought Wonder in America. It won many prizes too. Many schools use this book to talk about being mean, being friends, and how it feels to be different. They are making a movie from the book. Many people, like me, want to know what RJ Palacio will write next.
reference: Wonder is the first book by RJ Palacio, a writer from New York. She got the idea after seeing a girl with a face that looked different. The book is very popular in the United States and has won many awards. Many schools use the book to talk about bullying, friendship, and being different. A movie is now being made, and many people want to know what RJ Palacio will write next.

original: Cape Town can be a dangerous place for baboons. Some have been injured or killed in car accidents and others have been electrocuted as they played with electric cables. Baboons are an endangered species and to save them and minimise conflicts between humans and baboons, the city council has employed a team of Baboon Monitors. The monitors' job is to chase baboons out of urban areas or catch them and release them in the countryside. This policy has had some success, though it is proving hard to stop baboons from coming back to the city once they see it as a source of easy food.
simplified:
Cape Town is not safe for baboons. Some baboons get hurt or die in car crashes. Others die from electric wires when they play with them. There are not many baboons left. So, the city wants to save them. They also want to stop problems between people and baboons.

The city has people called Baboon Monitors. These people chase baboons away from the city. Or they catch them and take them to the country. This plan helps a little. But it is hard to stop the baboons from coming back to the city. They come back because they find food easily there.
reference: Cape Town can be dangerous for baboons. Some are hurt or die in car accidents. Some die from playing with electric wires. Baboons are animals that are in danger of disappearing. To help them, the city now has a team called Baboon Monitors. These people try to move baboons out of the city and take them back to the countryside. This plan works a little, but the baboons often come back because they find food in the city.

original: One of the most interesting cases of wild animals living in a city are the wild dogs of Moscow. In Moscow, there are approximately 35,000 wild dogs living on the streets. Some of the dogs were born wild, while others are pets that have been abandoned by their owners. Some dogs live alone and others live in packs. In 2010, scientists studied the dogs and found that the dogs have adapted remarkably successfully to urban life. They have learned that it is safer to cross the street with people and some dogs appear to understand traffic lights.
simplified:
Wild dogs in Moscow are a good example of animals living in cities. About 35,000 wild dogs live on the streets there. Some dogs were born wild. Other dogs were pets, but their owners left them. Some dogs live alone, and some live in groups.

In 2010, scientists studied these dogs. They saw that the dogs learned to live very well in the city. They learned it is safer to cross the street with people. Some dogs even seem to understand traffic lights.
reference: There are many wild dogs in Moscow, about 35,000. Some were born wild, and some were pets but left by their owners. Some live alone and others live in groups. In 2010, scientists studied the dogs. They found that the dogs have learned how to live in the city. Some dogs wait and cross the street with people. A few dogs even seem to know traffic lights.

original: In the 1990s, graffiti continued but there was also an explosion in street art around the world. Some artists wanted to make political points and produced art that tried to make people think about war, inequality and discrimination. Other street artists were more concerned with producing beautiful, attractive work. In South America, many street artists went to work in poor areas adding colour, life and beauty to grey, city walls.
simplified: In the 1990s, people still made graffiti. But street art also became very popular everywhere. Some artists wanted to show ideas about politics. They made art to make people think about war, unfairness, and not treating people well. Other street artists just wanted to make beautiful art. In South America, many street artists painted in poor areas. They made the grey city walls colourful and beautiful.
reference: In the 1990s, street art became more popular. Some artists wanted to show ideas about war, unfair treatment, and other problems. Other artists only wanted to make the streets look beautiful. In South America, many artists painted in poor areas. Their art added colour and life to the grey walls.

original: An important inspiration for the Hunger Games book comes from Suzanne's love of classical Greek mythology. When she was a child, one of her favourite stories was Theseus and the Minotaur. In this story the city of Athens is ruled by Crete, but the Athenians rebel. As a punishment, Minos the king of Crete forces the Athenians to send seven boys and seven girls to Crete every year. The youths are thrown into the labyrinth and eaten by a monster that lives there called the Minotaur. But one of the youths, named Theseus, fights the Minotaur and kills it. Suzanne sees Katniss Everdeen as a futuristic Theseus.
simplified:
Suzanne loved old Greek stories. These stories gave her ideas for the Hunger Games book.
When she was a child, she really liked one story. It was called Theseus and the Minotaur.
In this story, the city of Athens was controlled by Crete. But the people of Athens fought back.
To punish them, King Minos of Crete made the people of Athens send seven boys and seven girls to Crete every year.
These young people were put into a big maze. A monster called the Minotaur lived there and ate them.
But one young man, Theseus, fought the Minotaur and killed it.
Suzanne thinks Katniss Everdeen is like Theseus, but in the future.
reference: The writer of The Hunger Games, Suzanne, got the idea from old Greek stories. When she was young, she liked the story of Theseus and the Minotaur. In the story, the city of Athens must send children to a monster called the Minotaur every year. The Minotaur lives in a maze and eats the children. One boy, Theseus, fights the monster and kills it. Suzanne thinks Katniss, the main character in The Hunger Games, is like Theseus, but in the future.

original: Social media, magazines and shop windows bombard people daily with things to buy, and British consumers are buying more clothes and shoes than ever before. Online shopping means it is easy for customers to buy without thinking, while major brands offer such cheap clothes that they can be treated like disposable items – worn two or three times and then thrown away.
simplified: Every day, social media, magazines, and shop windows show people many things to buy. People in Britain buy more clothes and shoes now than before. It is easy to buy things online without thinking. Big shops sell very cheap clothes. So, people wear them only a few times. Then they throw them away.
reference: Every day, people see many clothes and shoes on social media, in magazines, and in shops. In the UK, people are buying more than before. Online shopping makes it easy to buy without thinking. Big brands sell clothes that are very cheap. Some people wear them only a few times and then throw them away.

original: A different trend is springing up in opposition to consumerism – the 'buy nothing' trend. The idea originated in Canada in the early 1990s and then moved to the US, where it became a rejection of the overspending and overconsumption of Black Friday and Cyber Monday during Thanksgiving weekend. On Buy Nothing Day people organise various types of protests and cut up their credit cards. Throughout the year, Buy Nothing groups organise the exchange and repair of items they already own.
simplified:
A new idea is starting. It is called 'buy nothing'. It is against buying too many things.

This idea started in Canada in the 1990s. Then it went to the USA. There, people said no to buying too much on special shopping days like Black Friday and Cyber Monday.

On 'Buy Nothing Day', people protest. They even cut their credit cards.

All year, 'Buy Nothing' groups help people swap things they have. They also help people fix things.
reference: Some people are starting a new idea called the 'buy nothing' trend. It began in Canada in the 1990s and then went to the USA. These people don't like buying too much on days like Black Friday and Cyber Monday. On 'Buy Nothing Day', people protest and cut their credit cards. During the year, they also fix and trade things instead of buying new ones.

original: By bringing people and animals together, zoos have the potential to educate the public about conservation issues and inspire people to protect animals and their habitats. Some zoos provide a safe environment for animals which have been mistreated in circuses, or pets which have been abandoned. Zoos also carry out important research into subjects like animal behaviour and how to treat illnesses.
simplified: Zoos bring people and animals together. They can teach people how to help animals and their homes. This can make people want to protect animals. Some zoos give a safe home to animals that had a bad life, for example, in circuses. They also help pets that people left alone. Zoos also do important studies. They learn about how animals act and how to make sick animals better.
reference: Zoos bring people and animals together. They help people learn how to protect animals and nature. Some zoos give homes to animals that were hurt in circuses or left by their owners. Zoos also study animal behavior and how to help sick animals.

original: Many city residents in Berlin, Germany complained that shooting pigs was unnecessarily cruel and there were heated arguments between hunters and animal lovers. In response to protests, the city council decided to take more peaceful action against pigs. Instead of shooting them, they have put up fences and made it illegal to feed the pigs. Time will tell if this strategy works, though it may be a losing battle as warmer winters mean that pig numbers are greater than in the past.
simplified: Many people in Berlin, Germany, did not like shooting pigs. They said it was not kind. Hunters and animal lovers had big arguments. So, the city government changed its plan. They decided to stop the pigs in a quiet way. They did not shoot them. Instead, they built fences. They also made a rule: it is now not allowed to feed the pigs. We do not know if this plan will work. It might be difficult because winters are warmer now. This means there are more pigs than in the past.
reference: In Berlin, Germany, many people were upset because hunters were killing pigs. They thought it was too cruel. The city listened and changed the plan. Now people cannot feed pigs, and fences have been built. This is a kinder way to stop pigs. But there are still many pigs, because the winters are getting warmer.

original: I work for a global IT company, but because their headquarters is in the States, I do all my work online from home. That means that I don't waste time commuting or making idle chit-chat with colleagues. I work on a project basis, and this flexibility is very valuable to me because it means that I can easily take some time off when my children need me to go to their school performances or if I need to schedule an appointment with the dentist. The downside is that without clear office hours, I tend to work well into the evening, sometimes skipping dinner to finish a task.
simplified:
I work for a big computer company. Its main office is in America. So, I work from home using the internet.

This means I don't travel to work. I also don't talk much with other people at work.

I work on different jobs. This is good for me. I can take time off easily. For example, if my children have school shows. Or if I need to go to the dentist.

But there is a problem. I don't have fixed work times. So, I often work late at night. Sometimes I don't eat dinner because I need to finish my work.
reference: I work for a large IT company, but I work from home because the office is in the USA. I do everything online. This is good because I don't waste time going to work or talking too much with coworkers. I work on different projects, and this is helpful. I can take time off if my children have a school show or if I need to see the dentist. But there is a problem: I don't have fixed hours, so I often work late and sometimes skip dinner to finish my work.

original: A large number of bridge accidents occur during the construction of the bridge itself. These accidents are often due to an error made by the engineers, such as a miscalculation. The bridge collapses under its own weight, and this can be deadly for the workers on it at the time.
simplified: Many accidents happen when people build bridges. Often, these accidents happen because engineers make a mistake. For example, they make a mistake with numbers. The bridge falls down because it is too heavy. This can kill the workers who are on the bridge.
reference: Many accidents with bridges happen while they are being built. These accidents often happen because engineers make mistakes, like wrong numbers. The bridge can fall down from its own weight. This is very dangerous for the workers on the bridge.

original: Is graffiti art or vandalism? This depends on your point of view, but in many countries, writing or painting on public or private property is considered vandalism. Many street artists have been stopped by the police and some have had to pay fines. Many city councils complain about the high cost of cleaning graffiti off buildings, buses and trains.
simplified:
Is graffiti art or a bad thing? What do you think?
In many countries, writing or painting on walls or other people's things is not allowed.
Police stop many street artists. Some artists must pay money.
City leaders say it costs a lot of money to clean graffiti from buildings, buses, and trains.
reference: Some people think graffiti is art. Others think it is bad. In many countries, painting on public or private places is not allowed. The police often stop street artists, and some must pay fines. Many cities say that cleaning graffiti from buildings and buses costs a lot of money.

original: The Hunger Games takes place in the future, after the destruction of North America. The country is called Panem and is made up of twelve poor districts governed by the wealthy Capitol. The Capitol holds absolute power over the nation. Each district is responsible for producing different things for the Capitol. District 12, where the story begins, provides all the coal for the country. There used to be a thirteenth district but they rebelled against the Capitol in the past and were destroyed.
simplified:
The story 'The Hunger Games' happens in the future. North America is gone.
There is a country called Panem. It has twelve poor areas. A rich city called the Capitol rules them.
The Capitol has all the power in the country.
Each area makes different things for the Capitol.
The story starts in District 12. This area gives all the coal to the country.
There was once a thirteenth area. But they fought the Capitol a long time ago. So, the Capitol destroyed them.
reference: The Hunger Games happens in the future, after North America is gone. The new country is called Panem. It has 12 poor districts and one rich city, the Capitol. The Capitol has full power. Each district makes something for the Capitol. District 12, where the story starts, gives coal. There was a District 13, but it fought against the Capitol and was destroyed.

original: Often wild animals come into cities to look for food. In Cape Town, South Africa, baboons have started coming into residential areas on the edge of the city to feed. They open rubbish bins and eat fruit from gardens and orchards. Some brave baboons have even come into people's houses and taken food from kitchen cupboards and fridges! Baboons can be aggressive and have attacked a lot of pet animals, so understandably, many city residents don't welcome their presence.
simplified: Wild animals often come into cities to find food. In Cape Town, South Africa, baboons now come to houses near the city. They want to eat. They open trash cans. They eat fruit from gardens and from fruit trees. Some baboons are very brave. They even go into people's houses. They take food from kitchen cabinets and fridges! Baboons can be mean. They have hurt many pets. So, people in the city do not want them there.
reference: Wild animals often go into cities to look for food. In Cape Town, South Africa, baboons now go into areas near people's homes. They open rubbish bins and eat fruit from gardens. Some baboons are very brave and go into houses to take food from kitchens. Baboons can be dangerous and sometimes hurt pet animals. Many people in the city do not want them around.

original: If most people have four to six dreams every night after the age of ten, that's as many as 2,000 dreams per year. So, by the time they reach 80 years old the average person might have had 140,000 dreams. Even if we forget 95–99 per cent of our dreams, that's still a few thousand remembered dreams across a lifetime. It's not too difficult to believe that, by coincidence, a dream event is followed by a real-life event that's similar to it, especially if the subject of the dream is something that happens often in everyday life.
simplified: Most people have 4 to 6 dreams every night after they are 10 years old. This means they have about 2,000 dreams each year. So, when people are 80, they might have had 140,000 dreams. We forget almost all our dreams, maybe 95% or 99%. But we still remember some dreams, maybe a few thousand, in our life. Sometimes, we dream something, and then it happens in real life. This is often just by chance. It is easy to think this, especially if the dream is about something that happens a lot every day.
reference: Most people have 4 to 6 dreams every night after they turn 10. That means around 2,000 dreams every year. By age 80, a person may have about 140,000 dreams. Even if we forget 95?C99% of our dreams, we still remember many. So, it's not strange if something we dream later happens in real life, especially if it is something we often see in daily life.

original: What does the art world think of graffiti and street art? Recently, there has been a growing recognition of its value as an art form. There have been major exhibitions of street art in galleries in Paris, London and Los Angeles. The American artist Elura Emerald organised a street art exhibition at a New York gallery in 2008. She defended street artists, saying 'artists who paint on the street are merely expressing themselves, not hurting anyone. They should be appreciated and celebrated'.
simplified:
What do people who like art think about graffiti and street art?
Now, more people think it is real art.
There have been big shows of street art in galleries in Paris, London, and Los Angeles.
An American artist, Elura Emerald, made a street art show in a New York gallery in 2008.
She said good things about street artists. She said, "Artists who paint on the street just show their ideas. They don't hurt anyone. People should like their art and say it is good."
reference: What do people in the art world think about street art and graffiti? Today, more people see it as a true kind of art. Big art shows in Paris, London, and Los Angeles have shown street art. In 2008, an American artist, Elura Emerald, made a street art show in New York. She said street artists only want to share their ideas and are not doing anything wrong.

original: Sam squinted against the sun at the distant dust trail raked up by the car on its way up to the Big House. The horses kicked and flicked their tails at flies, not caring about their owner's first visit in ten months. Sam waited. Mr Carter didn't come out here unless he had to, which was just fine by Sam. The more he kept out of his boss's way, the longer he'd have a job. Mr, Carter wiped the sweat from the back of his neck. The damp patches on his shirt drew together like shapes in an atlas. His skin was already turning ruddy in the June sun. Otherwise he had the indoor tan of a man that made money while other people did the work.
simplified:
Sam looked at the sun. It was very bright. He saw dust far away. A car made the dust. The car was going to the big house.
The horses moved their legs and tails because of flies. They did not care that their owner was coming. He had not visited for ten months.
Sam waited.
Mr Carter only came here if he had to. Sam liked this. Sam did not want to see his boss. If he did not see his boss, he could keep his job.
Mr Carter wiped the sweat from his neck. His shirt had wet spots. His skin was already red from the sun. Usually, his skin was pale. He was a rich man. Other people worked for him.
reference: Sam looked at a car coming to the Big House. The car made a lot of dust. The horses moved their tails to stop the flies. They didn't care that their owner was coming after ten months. Sam waited. Mr. Carter came only when he had to, and Sam liked that. If he stayed away from his boss, he could keep his job. Mr. Carter wiped his neck. His shirt was wet from sweat. His skin was red from the hot June sun. Normally, he stayed inside and made money while others worked.

original: According to Campbell, the hero at first refuses the call to adventure, but a mentor appears who helps them and they decide to 'cross the threshold' and travel into the 'special world' where the adventure happens. The next stage consists of passing tests, fighting enemies and meeting friends as the hero prepares to face their biggest challenge. For Luke the mentor is, of course, Obi-Wan, the friends are Han Solo and the robots R2D2 and C3PO and the enemy is Darth Vader inside the special world of the Death Star.
simplified: Campbell says that a hero first does not want to go on an adventure. But a helper comes and helps them. So, the hero goes to a new, special place for the adventure. Then, the hero does difficult things. They fight bad people and meet friends. They get ready for their biggest fight. For example, in the story of Luke, Obi-Wan is the helper. His friends are Han Solo and the robots R2D2 and C3PO. His enemy is Darth Vader. This happens in a special place called the Death Star.
reference: Campbell says that first, the hero does not want to go on the adventure. Then a teacher, also a mentor, comes to help. The hero then goes into a "special world" where the adventure happens. In this world, the hero has to do tests, fight enemies, and meet new friends before the biggest fight. Luke's teacher is Obi-Wan, his friends are Han solo and the robots R2D2 and C3PO, and his enemy is Darth Vader inside the Death Star.

original: Another suggested defence against a PHA on course to hit Earth is to blow it up using a nuclear weapon. It may sound like a plot from a film, and it was the subject of the 1998 film Armageddon, but the Hypervelocity Asteroid Mitigation Mission for Emergency Response (HAMMER) is a genuine NASA proposal. The eight-ton rockets would be fired at an approaching asteroid with the hope of bumping it off course. If the asteroid was too close to Earth for this plan to work, the rockets would carry nuclear bombs to blow it up instead.
simplified: People have another idea to stop a big space rock that is coming to Earth. They want to blow it up with a special bomb. This sounds like a story from a movie, like 'Armageddon'. But NASA has a real plan for this. It is called HAMMER. They would send big rockets to the space rock. The rockets would push it away from Earth. If the space rock is too close, the rockets would have special bombs. These bombs would break the space rock into many small pieces.
reference: One way to stop an asteroid from hitting Earth is to break it with a strong bomb, which is nuclear weapon. This may sound like a movie, and it was in the 1998 film Armageddon. But NASA had a real plan on this. The plan was to send big rockets, about eight tons, to hit the asteroid and push it away. If the asteroid is already too close to Earth, the rocket would take the nuclear bomb to blow it up.

original: Underutilised items may seem useless to some, but could be an asset to others. With the advent of the internet, online communities have figured out a way to generate profit from the sharing of those underused assets. Using websites and social media groups that facilitate the buying and selling of second-hand goods, it is now easier than ever for peer-to-peer sharing activities to take place. And this is known as the sharing economy.
simplified:
You might have things you don't use often. You may think they are not useful. But other people might want them.

Now, we have the internet. People online found a way to make money. They share things that are not used much.

There are websites and social media groups. They help people buy and sell used things. So, it is very easy for people to share things with each other. We call this the "sharing economy."
reference: Things that we don't use much may look useless, but other people may need them. With the internet, people have found a way to share these things and make money. Website and social media groups now help people to buy and sell used goods. It is easy for people to share with each other in this way. This is the sharing economy.

original: Around the 18th and 19th centuries two main ideas about dreams became popular. One was the idea that the things we see in our dreams represent things hidden from our conscious mind. Freud believed that if we understand what dreams are telling us, we can understand our hidden feelings and the problems they cause. However, the other theory was the opposite. It said that dreams are just a collection of random activity in the brain while it's organising memories and events from the day. When we wake up, we try to make sense of these random images and feelings and put them into some sort of story.
simplified:
A long time ago, people had two main ideas about dreams.
One idea was that dreams show us things we don't know we think.
A man called Freud thought that if we understand our dreams, we can understand our secret feelings and problems.
But the other idea was very different.
It said that dreams are just mixed-up things our brain does when we sleep.
Our brain is putting together things from the day.
When we wake up, we try to understand these mixed-up pictures and feelings.
We try to make a story from them.
reference: In the 18th and 19th centuries, people had two main ideas about dreams. The first idea was that dreams show things that we dont know in our mind. Freud believed that if we look at dreams, we can understand our hidden feelings and problems. The second idea was opposite. It said dreams are only random things in the brain when it is cleaning and organising the day's memories. When we wake up, we try to make a story from these pics and feelings.

original: George Lucas was one of the early film directors to directly base his story on the 17 stages of the hero's journey. Typically the hero starts the story living an ordinary life, but something happens that calls them to an adventure that changes everything. At the beginning of Star Wars, Luke lives an ordinary life with his aunt and uncle, repairing robots. When he finds Princess Leia's message to Obi-Wan Kenobi inside the robot R2D2, it is 'the call to adventure' that starts the hero on his journey.
simplified:
George Lucas was a movie maker. He used a special story idea for his films. This idea is called 'the hero's journey'.
Usually, the main character lives a normal life. But then something happens, and they must go on an adventure. This adventure changes everything for them.
In the film Star Wars, Luke lives a normal life with his aunt and uncle. He fixes robots. One day, he finds a message from Princess Leia. It is for Obi-Wan Kenobi and it is inside the robot R2D2. This is the start of Luke's adventure.
reference: George Lucas was one of the first movie makers to use 'the hero's journey' idea. In this story, the hero starts with a normal life. Then something happens that begins an adventure. In Star Wars, Luke lives with his aunt and uncle and fixes robots. One day, he finds a message from Princess Leia. This is the start of his journey.

original: Religion is important to Pi. Though his family is Hindu, he is curious about other religions and he makes friends with a Christian priest and a Muslim baker. To everyone's surprise, Pi declares himself to be simultaneously Hindu, Muslim and Christian. When his family and teachers ask him to choose just one religion, Pi refuses, saying 'I just want to love God'. simplified: Religion is important to Pi. His family is Hindu. But Pi wants to learn about other religions. He makes friends with a Christian priest and a Muslim baker. reference: Religion is important for Pi. His family is Hindu, but he is also interested in other religions. He makes friends with a Christian priest and a Muslim baker. One day, Pi says that he is Hindu, Muslim, and Christian at the same time. His family and teachers ask him to choose only one religion, but Pi says, "I just want to love God." After this, his family and teachers let him choose his way.

original: People might not realise they are part of the disposable clothing problem because they donate their unwanted clothes to charities. But charity shops can't sell all those unwanted clothes. 'Fast fashion' goes out of fashion as quickly as it came in and is often too poor quality to recycle; people don't want to buy it second-hand. Huge quantities end up being thrown away, and a lot of clothes that charities can't sell are sent abroad, causing even more economic and environmental problems.
simplified: People do not know they make a problem with clothes. They give their old clothes to shops that help people. But these shops cannot sell all of these clothes. New, cheap clothes are not popular for a long time. They are often bad quality. So, people cannot use them again. People do not want to buy them when they are second-hand. Many clothes go in the bin. Also, many clothes that shops cannot sell go to other countries. This makes more problems for money and for the planet.
reference: Some people don't know they are part of the clothing waste problem because they give old clothes to charities. But charity shops cannot sell all of them. Fast fashion quickly goes out of style and is often poor in quality, so people don't want to buy second-hand. A lot of clothes are thrown away, and many clothes that charities cannot sell are sent to other countries. This causes money and environmental problems.

original: Some people think writing your dreams down can open your mind to lucid dreaming. Lucid dreams are dreams where you're not only aware you're dreaming but you can make decisions to affect the events of your dreams. So, maybe you can turn a nightmare into a safe-feeling dream, or you can direct the plot of your dream like a film director. Then, instead of just working out the meaning of your dreams, you'll be creating them, though you might want to continue having some dreams that allow your subconscious to tell you what's on your mind!
simplified: Some people say that writing your dreams can help you have lucid dreams. In a lucid dream, you know you are dreaming. You can also choose what happens in your dream. So, you can change a bad dream into a good dream. You can choose the story of your dream, like a movie director. Then, you don't just think about what your dreams mean. You make your dreams. But sometimes, you might want dreams that show you what you are really thinking or feeling.
reference: Some people think that writing down dreams in a notebook can help them have lucid dreams. A lucid dream is when you know you are dreaming, and you can change what happens. For example, you can make a bad dream feel safe, or you can control the story like a movie director. In this way, you are not only looking for the meaning of your dreams, but also making them. But sometimes, you may still want dreams that show what is in your mind.

original: Blek le Rat started out painting rats on the walls of his home city, Paris. Nowadays, he tries to make people think about different social issues and problems. He paints pictures of homeless people in big cities to encourage residents to think about the problem of homelessness.
simplified: Blek le Rat first painted rats on walls in his city, Paris. Now, he paints homeless people in cities. He wants people to think about problems in the world, like people with no home.
reference: Blek le Rat began by painting rats on the walls of Paris, his home city. Now, he uses his art to talk about social problems. In big cities, he paints pictures of homeless people to make others think about homelessness.

original: In some areas, councils have tried to encourage artists not to paint graffiti randomly on walls by allowing them to work in designated areas. Taiwan is one such place and there are 'graffiti zones' where artists are free to paint and write on walls. In São Paulo in Brazil, the city council has even allowed some graffiti artists to paint on the city's subway trains.
simplified:
Some cities want artists to paint in special places. They don't want artists to paint on walls everywhere.

original: Faith47 is from Cape Town in South Africa. She paints big, colourful pictures of people and animals and likes to explore different locations. Her work is found on pavements, in empty factories and on abandoned cars. She likes the fact that most street art is temporary and will soon be removed by weather or cleaners from the city council. simplified: Faith47 lives in Cape Town, South Africa. She paints big, colourful pictures of people and animals. She likes to paint in many different places. For her, this shows that life changes a lot. Things end, and new things start.
reference: Faith47 comes from Cape Town in South Africa. She paints big, colourful pictures of people and animals. She likes to paint in many places, like on pavements, in empty factories, and on old cars. And we can see her work in these places. She enjoys that street art does not last forever and will be removed by rain or by city cleaners. For her, this shows that life is always changing, with things ending and new beginnings.

original: When Gabriela became aware of the cultural differences between her and her team, she took the initiative to have an open conversation with them about their feelings about her leadership. Pleased to be asked for their thoughts, Gabriela's team openly expressed that they were not used to being told what to do. They enjoyed having more room for initiative and creative freedom. When she told her team exactly what she needed them to do, they felt that she didn't trust them to do their job well. They realised that Gabriela was taking it personally when they tried to challenge or make changes to her decisions, and were able to explain that it was how they'd always worked.
simplified: Gabriela saw that she and her team had different ideas. She talked to them about how she led them. The team was happy she asked. They told Gabriela they did not like being told what to do. They liked to decide things themselves and be creative. When Gabriela told them exactly what to do, they felt she did not trust them. reference: When Gabriela saw that she and her team had cultural differences, she chose to talk with them openly about her leadership. original: I'm a freelancer and work for myself. This is great because I am in control of what I do and how I spend my time. At first, I was working from home, but I found it really hard to concentrate. There were just too many distractions around: housework that needed doing, another cup of tea, my family members wanting my attention for various things. So I started to go to a nearby café to work, but the Wi-Fi connection wasn't ideal and I found myself drinking too much coffee. In the end, I decided to rent a desk in a co-working space with five other freelancers like myself. I liked getting dressed to go to work in the morning and being able to focus in an office environment.
simplified:
I work for myself. This is good because I can choose what I do and when I work.
At first, I worked from home. But it was hard to focus. Many things stopped me from working. For example, housework, tea, and my family wanted me.
So I went to a café near my home to work. But the internet was not good, and I drank too much coffee.
Finally, I decided to rent a desk in an office. Five other people who work for themselves were there too.
I liked getting ready for work in the morning. I could focus well in the office.
reference: I am a freelancer, so I work for myself. This is good as I can choose what to do and how to spend my time. At first, I worked at home, but it was hard to focus. There were many things around me, like housework, making tea and families asking for attention. Then I tried to work in a cafe, but the internet was not good and I drank too much coffee. original: Whether NASA can find the remaining middle-sized NEOs depends on getting the money to build NEOCam, a 0.5-metre space telescope which would use infrared light to locate asteroids. If it did get the money, it could probably achieve its goal in ten years. Once logged, the planetary defence team would still need to work out how to defend the planet against being hit by the truly worrying asteroids – the PHAs.
simplified: NASA wants to find more space rocks. They need money to build a special telescope called NEOCam. This telescope will be in space and will help them find the rocks. If NASA gets the money, they can probably find all these rocks in ten years. After they find the rocks, a special team still needs to think about how to stop the dangerous ones from hitting Earth.
reference: NASA needs money to build NEOCam, a space telescope with a small lens, to find the rest of the middle-sized asteriods. This telescope would use infrared light to look for them. If NASA gets the money, it could finish this in 10 years. After that, the team must still plan how to stop the very dangerous asteriods, called PHAs, from hitting Earth.

original: People have been painting and writing on walls throughout history. In prehistoric times, people in Africa and Europe used to paint pictures of animals and people in caves. Graffiti has been found on buildings at ancient sites in Greece, Italy, Syria and Iraq. In the Roman town of Pompeii, archaeologists have found numerous examples of graffiti written in Latin. simplified: People have always painted and written on walls. A very long time ago, people in Africa and Europe painted animals and people in caves. original: Historically, more bridges were made of wood and were much more susceptible to fire. This was particularly true of old-fashioned train bridges, where the spark created by the steel wheels and steel tracks could sometimes cause a bridge to catch fire and burn to the ground.
simplified: In the past, many bridges were made of wood. Wood burns easily, so these bridges could easily catch fire. This happened a lot with old train bridges. Train wheels and tracks are made of metal. Sometimes, they made sparks. These sparks could make the wooden bridge burn down completely.
reference: In the past, many bridges were made of wood. Wood can burn easily. Train bridges had a big problem, because the steel wheels on the steel tracks made sparks. The sparks could make the wooden bridge burn.

original: The 'buy nothing' trend has now reached influencers on social media who usually share posts of clothing and make-up that they recommend for people to buy. Some YouTube stars now encourage their viewers not to buy anything at all for periods as long as a year. Two friends in Canada spent a year working towards buying only food. For the first three months they learned how to live without buying electrical goods, clothes or things for the house. For the next stage, they gave up services, for example haircuts, eating out at restaurants or buying petrol for their cars. In one year, they'd saved $55,000.
simplified:
There is a new idea called 'buy nothing'. Famous people on social media usually show clothes and make-up for people to buy. But now, some of them tell people not to buy anything.

Some famous people on YouTube ask their fans not to buy anything for a long time, even for a year.

Two friends in Canada tried to buy only food for one year. For the first three months, they did not buy electric things, clothes, or things for their home.

After that, they also stopped paying for services. For example, they did not get haircuts, eat in restaurants, or buy gas for their cars.

In one year, they saved $55,000.
reference: The "buy nothing" idea is now gaining popularity among social media influencers. Normally, they show clothes and make-up for people to buy. But now, some YouTubers tell their fans not to buy anything, even for one year. Two friends in Canada did this and only bought food for a year. In the first three months, they stopped buying electronics, clothes, and things for the house. Later, they also stopped paying for services, like haircuts, eating in restaurants, and petrol for their cars. In one year, they saved $55,000.

original: In her previous work environment, Gabriela was used to a high power distance culture where power and authority are respected and everyone has their rightful place. In such a culture, leaders make the big decisions and are not often challenged. Her Swedish team, however, were used to working in a low power distance culture where subordinates often work together with their bosses to find solutions and make decisions. Here, leaders act as coaches or mentors who encourage independent thought and expect to be challenged.
simplified: Gabriela's old job was a place where bosses had a lot of power. People always listened to the bosses. The bosses made all the big decisions, and people did not often say "no" to them. But her new team in Sweden was different. In Sweden, workers and bosses often work together. They find answers and make choices together. Here, bosses are like teachers. They want people to think for themselves and ask questions.
reference: In her old job, Gabriela worked in a place with high power distance. This means people respect authority, and leaders make the big decisions. Workers do not usually question their bosses. But her Swedish team worked in a low power distance culture. Here, workers and bosses make decisions together. Leaders act like coaches or teachers, and they want workers to think for themselves and even question them.

original: It is impossible to know how street art will develop in the future but certain trends are emerging. Although we don't know what will happen to street art in the future, we can be sure that it is here to stay!
simplified: We don't know how street art will change in the future. But we can see some new things happening. Most street artists are young. They paint in their city or town. But now, many artists travel to other countries to paint. Other artists use the internet. They talk to each other and show pictures of their art. Also, people who like art now think street art is real art. They like it more. We don't know how street art will be in the future. But we know it will always be here!
reference: We don't know what street art will be like in the future, but we can see some changes now. Most street artists are young and paint in their own city. original: Erik Weihenmayer from the United States is a multi-adventurer. He's ridden a bike through the deserts of Morocco, kayaked through the Grand Canyon and climbed Everest. original: Have you ever dreamt of climbing Mount Everest or walking to the South Pole? If so, you're not alone. simplified:
Do you ever dream about climbing Mount Everest or walking to the South Pole? Many people do.

Many explorers love nature. They travel to tell people about problems with the Earth. Other explorers want to help people. They get money for groups that help others.
reference: Have you ever dreamed of climbing Mount Everest or going to the South Pole? Many people have. Every year, thousands of people try to climb the highest mountains or walk across continents. In the past, explorers used maps and compasses, but now they use modern tools like GPS and satellite phones. Many of them love nature and want to tell people about environmental problems. original: Suzanne Collines has always found news programmes of wars upsetting. When she was a child, her father was a pilot in the US Air Force and he fought in Vietnam. Her mother tried to protect her by not telling her what was happening in the war, but she still saw news programmes about the war and knew that her dad was there. original: Democratised online platforms are providing a chance for people to make a quick buck or two. To give an example, busy parents previously might not have bothered with setting up a stall at the local market or car boot sale to sell their children's old equipment, but with online marketplaces, parents are now able to sell on those hardly worn baby clothes that their children have outgrown and the expensive pushchairs and baby equipment they have invested in, so as to put some cash back into their pockets.
simplified: Websites on the internet help people get money quickly. For example, before, busy parents did not want to sell their children's old things at a market. It was too much work. original: In 2010, the planetary defence team at NASA had identified and logged 90 per cent of the asteroids near Earth measuring 1km wide. These 'near-Earth objects', or NEOs, are the size of mountains and include anything within 50 million kilometres of Earth's orbit. With an estimated 50 left to log, NASA says none of the 887 it knows about are a significant danger to the planet.
simplified: In 2010, a team at NASA found almost all the big space rocks near Earth. These rocks are 1 kilometer wide. They are like mountains. They fly close to our planet. NASA found 887 of these rocks. They still need to find about 50 more. NASA says these rocks will not hurt Earth.
reference: In 2010, NASA found 90% of the big asteroids near Earth that are 1km wide. They are callled 'near-Earth objects'. They are very large like mountains and they move close to Earth's path. NASA thinks about 50 are still missing, but the 887 already found are not dangerous to Earth.

original: Pi and Richard Parker spend 227 days in the lifeboat. They live through hunger, illness and exhaustion. simplified: Pi and Richard Parker are on a small boat for 227 days. They are very hungry, sick, and tired. They have big storms and very hot sun. But they stay alive. reference: Pi and Richard Parker stay in a lifeboat for 227 days. They are usually hungry, sick and very tired. They live through big storms and the hot sun of the Pacific Ocean, but they are alive. original: The first is DART – the Double Asteroid Redirection Test. Plans are scheduled to test DART on the moon of an asteroid called Didymos. 'Didymoon' is 150 metres wide, orbiting its 800-metre mother, and hopefully the impact of DART will knock it out of its orbit enough for Earth-based telescopes to pick up.
simplified: First, there is DART. DART means 'Double Asteroid Redirection Test'. Scientists want to test DART on a small moon. This moon is around a big rock called Didymos. The small moon is called 'Didymoon'. It is 150 meters wide. It goes around the big rock, which is 800 meters wide. DART will hit Didymoon. We hope this hit will push Didymoon a little. Then, telescopes on Earth can see this change.
reference: The first project is DART- the Double Asteroid Redirection Test. It will be tested on the moon of an asteroid called Didymos. This moon is called "Didymoon." It is 150 metres wide and goes around its bigger "mother" asteroid, which is 800 metres wide. Scientists hope that when DART hits Didymoon, it will change its path enough for telescopes on Earth to see.

original: Writing about your dreams will mean you start to remember more details about the dream, so think about the people and place where the dream happened as they might add to the meaning too. original: Chloe arrived home from school, made herself a cup of coffee and took it up to her bedroom. She had some homework to do, but that could wait for later. She wanted to enjoy the quiet hour before her parents arrived home and the house filled up with the evening sounds of chatter, television or her dad listening to his beloved jazz while he cooked dinner. simplified: Chloe came home from school. She made some coffee and took it to her bedroom. She had homework, but she wanted to do it later. She wanted to enjoy the quiet time. Her parents would come home soon. Then the house would be noisy with talking, TV, or her dad's favourite jazz music when he cooked dinner.
