reference: In Berlin, Germany, many local people complained that shooting pigs was too cruel. This caused strong arguments between hunters and animal lovers. Because of the protests, the city council chose a more peaceful solution. They put up fences and made it against the law to feed wild pigs. It's not clear if the plan will work, since warmer winters have caused the number of pigs to grow more than before.

original: Around the 18th and 19th centuries two main ideas about dreams became popular. One was the idea that the things we see in our dreams represent things hidden from our conscious mind. Freud believed that if we understand what dreams are telling us, we can understand our hidden feelings and the problems they cause. However, the other theory was the opposite. It said that dreams are just a collection of random activity in the brain while it's organising memories and events from the day. When we wake up, we try to make sense of these random images and feelings and put them into some sort of story.
simplified: In the 18th and 19th centuries, two main ideas about dreams became popular. One idea was that the things we see in dreams show us thoughts that are hidden deep in our minds. A man called Freud believed that if we understand our dreams, we can understand our secret feelings and the problems they cause. But the other idea was completely different. It said that dreams are just random things happening in the brain when it's putting together memories and events from the day. When we wake up, we try to understand these random pictures and feelings and make them into a story.
reference: In the 18th and 19th centuries, two main ideas about dreams became popular. The first was that dreams show things that are hidden in our minds. Freud thought that by studying dreams, we can learn about our secret feelings and the problems they create. The second idea was the opposite. It said that the dreams are the result of random brain activity while it is sorting memories and events from the day. When we wake up, our brain tries to connect these random images and feelings into a story.

original: George Lucas was one of the early film directors to directly base his story on the 17 stages of the hero's journey. simplified: George Lucas was one of the first film directors to base his stories on 'the hero's journey'. Usually, the hero starts living a normal life. reference: George Lucas was one of the first film directors to base a story on the 17 stages of the hero's journey. When he finds Princess Leia's message in the robot R2D2, it becomes his 'call to adventure' and marks the beginning of his journey.

original: Often wild animals come into cities to look for food. In Cape Town, South Africa, baboons have started coming into residential areas on the edge of the city to feed. simplified: Wild animals often come into cities to look for food. In Cape Town, South Africa, baboons have started coming into neighbourhoods at the edge of the city to find food. reference: Wild animals often enter cities in search of food. In Cape Town, South Africa, baboons have begun coming into areas where people live. reference: How does the art world view graffiti and street art? Recently, more people have started to see it as a real form of art. original: Another suggested defence against a PHA on course to hit Earth is to blow it up using a nuclear weapon. The eight-ton rockets would be fired at an approaching asteroid with the hope of bumping it off course. simplified: Another idea to protect Earth from a dangerous asteroid is to destroy it with a nuclear bomb. This might sound like something from a movie, like the film Armageddon from 1998. If the asteroid was too close to Earth for this to work, the rockets would carry nuclear bombs to destroy it instead.
reference: Another way to stop an asteroid from hitting Earth is to destroy it with a nuclear weapon. This may sound like a film story, and it was actually in the 1998 film Armageddon. However, the Hypervelocity Asteroid Mitigation Mission for Emergency Response (HAMMER) is a real project from NASA. The plan was to send eight-ton heavy rockets towards an asteroid to push it away from its path. If the asteroid is already too close to Earth, the rockets could carry nuclear bombs to break it apart.

original: Underutilised items may seem useless to some, but could be an asset to others. original: One of the most important modern functions of zoos is supporting international breeding programmes, particularly for endangered species. In the wild, some of the rarest species have difficulty in finding mates and breeding, and they might also be threatened by poachers, loss of their habitat and predators. A good zoo will enable these species to live and breed in a secure environment. In addition, as numbers of some wild species drop, there is an increased danger of populations becoming too genetically similar. Breeding programmes provide a safeguard: zoo-bred animals can be released into the wild to increase genetic diversity.
simplified: Zoos today have an important job: they help animals have babies. They do this in special programmes with other zoos around the world, especially for animals that are in danger of disappearing. In nature, some very rare animals find it hard to find partners and have babies. They are also in danger from hunters, losing their homes, and other animals that hunt them. A good zoo lets these animals live and have babies in a safe place. Also, when there are fewer wild animals, there is a risk that groups of animals will become too similar. This is because they are all from the same family. These programmes help to protect them. Animals born in zoos can be put back into nature. This helps to make the wild animals more different from each other.

A good zoo gives these species a safe place to live and reproduce. Another problem is that when the number of animals in the wild becomes very small, they can become too genetically similar. Breeding programmes help with this, because animals born in zoos can later be relaesed into the wild to make the population stronger and more diverse.

original: Both of these kinds of accidents are extremely rare, but boats and trains can cause a bridge to collapse for different reasons. original: Psychologist and 'growth mindset' proponent Carol Dweck spoke of the plasticity of the brain and our ability to develop skills and talents that we might not have been good at to start with. Many of us tend to focus our praise on the end result and seemingly innate talents, e.g. 'You really have an eye for details' or 'You have a real talent for organising events'. However, research suggests that by focusing on the process of how things are done – praising effort, experimentation and problem-solving strategies – we can encourage the development of new skills and the continued honing of talents.
simplified: Carol Dweck, a psychologist who supports the 'growth mindset', says that our brain can change. She believes we can learn new skills and talents, even if we are not good at them at first. Many people usually praise the final result or skills that seem natural. For example, they might say, 'You are good at seeing small things' or 'You are good at planning events'. However, research shows that if we praise *how* people do things – like their effort, trying new ideas, and solving problems – we can help them learn new skills and improve their existing talents.
reference: Psychologist Carol Dweck, who supports the idea of a 'growth mindset', spoke about how the brain can change and how we can develop skills and talents, even if we were not good at them at firstt. Many people usually give praise for the final result or for natural talent, for example: "You are good at noticing details" or "You are great at organising events." But research shows it is better to focus on the process. By prarisising effort, trying new things, and problem-solving, we can help people build new skills and improve their talents.

original: The Hunger Games is a hugely successful book for teenagers and young adults by the American author Suzanne Collins. Since it was published in 2008 it has been translated into 26 different languages and has sold millions of copies around the world. It is also the first book for young readers to sell more than a million electronic copies. The Hunger Games is now a major Hollywood film and is just as successful. It made 152.5 million dollars in its opening weekend in North America alone!
simplified: The Hunger Games is a very popular book for teenagers and young adults. It was written by the American author Suzanne Collins. Since it was published in 2008, it has been translated into 26 different languages and has sold millions of copies all over the world. It was also the first book for young readers to sell more than a million electronic copies. The Hunger Games is now a big Hollywood film, and it is just as popular. reference: The Hunger Games is a very popular book for teenagers and young adults, written by the American author Suzanne Collins. Since its release in 2008, it has been translated into 26 languages and has sold millions of copies worldwide. It was also the first young adult book to sell over one million electronic copies. The Hunger Games is now a big Hollywood movie, which is also very successful. In its first weekend, the film made 152.5 million dollars in North America.

original: Maybe dreams are the result of our mind organising the thoughts we have during the day, but they appear in dreams with symbolic meaning. When we're awake, our thoughts mostly appear in our minds as words, like conversations we have with ourselves. But when we're asleep, the part of our brain that controls language becomes less active while the part that controls emotions becomes more active.
simplified: Maybe dreams happen because our mind organizes the thoughts from our day. But in dreams, these thoughts show us things that have a special meaning. When we are awake, our thoughts are usually words in our minds, like when we talk to ourselves. But when we are asleep, the part of our brain for language works less. At the same time, the part for feelings works more.
reference: Dreams may happen because our mind is organising the thoughts we have during the day, but in dreams, these thoughts often appear as symbols. When we are awake, our thoughts usually come to us in words, like small conversations with ourselves. But when we are asleep, the part of the brain that controls language is less active, and the part that controls emotions is more active.

original: Early in her career, the psychologist Carol Dweck of Stanford University gave a group of ten-year-olds problems that were slightly too hard for them. One group reacted positively, said they loved challenge and understood that their abilities could be developed. She says they had a 'growth mindset' and are focused on what they can achieve in the future. But another group of children felt that their intelligence was being judged and they had failed. They had a 'fixed mindset' and were unable to imagine improving. Some of these children said they might cheat in the future; others looked for someone who had done worse than them to boost their self-esteem.
simplified:
At the start of her work, Carol Dweck, a psychologist from Stanford University, gave some ten-year-old children problems that were a little too hard. One group of children reacted well. They said they liked challenges and understood that they could improve their skills. She calls this a 'growth mindset', meaning they believed they could learn and get better. These children focused on what they could achieve in the future.

But another group of children felt that people were judging how smart they were, and they felt they had failed. They had a 'fixed mindset', which means they thought their intelligence could not change. They could not imagine improving. Some of these children said they might cheat in the future. Others looked for someone who had done worse than them to feel better about themselves.
reference: Early in her career, psychologist Carol Dweck from Stanford University gave ten-year-old children some problems that were a bit too hard for them. One group reacted well. They loved the challenge and believed they could improve their abilities. She says they had a 'growth mindset' and focused on what they can achieve in the future. Another group, however, thought their intelligence was being tested and felt they had failed. They had a 'fixed mindset' and could not imagine getting better. Some of these children even said they might cheat next time, while others compared themselves to children who had done worse to feel better.

original: The majority of people believe that developing countries are in a terrible situation: suffering from incredible poverty, governed by dictators and with little hope for any meaningful change. But, surprisingly, this is far from the truth. The reality is that a great transformation is occurring. Over the past 20 years, more than 700 million people have increased their income and come out of poverty. Additionally, six million fewer children die every year from disease, millions more girls are in school and millions of people have access to clean water.
simplified: Most people think that poor countries are in a very bad situation. They believe these countries are very poor, ruled by dictators, and have little hope for real change. But, surprisingly, this is not true. The truth is that a big change is happening. In the last 20 years, more than 700 million people have earned more money and are no longer poor. Also, six million fewer children die from illness every year. Millions more girls can go to school, and millions of people can get clean water.
reference: Many people think that developing countries are in very bad conditions. They imagine extreme poverty, strong rulers who do not allow freedom, and no chance for change. But this is not the truth. In fact, a big change is happening. Over the past 20 years, more than 700 million people have escaped poverty by earning more money. Also, six million fewer children die each year from sickness. More girls are now going to school, and millions of people can drink clean water.

original: Your manager stops you and says she needs to have a word about your performance in the recent project. You worry about it all weekend, wondering what you might have done wrong. When you step into her office on Monday morning she begins by praising you for the good work you've done on the project, and you wonder if this is the obligatory praise that starts off the typical 'feedback sandwich'. You know how the feedback sandwich goes: say something nice, say what you really want to say, say something nice again.
simplified: Your manager stops you and says she wants to talk about your work on the last project. You worry about it all weekend, thinking about what you might have done wrong. On Monday morning, when you go into her office, she starts by saying good things about your work on the project. You wonder if this is just the usual praise that starts a 'feedback sandwich'. You know how a 'feedback sandwich' works: first, you say something nice, then you say what you really want to say, and then you say something nice again.
reference: Your manager stops you and says she wants to talk to you about your work on the last project. You worry about it all weekend, thinking you may have done something wrong. On Monday, you go into her office and she starts by saying good things about your work. You are not sure if this is just the usual "feedback sandwich". The feedback sandwich goes like this: You say somthing nice, then say something you really want to say (usually a criticism), then say something nice again.

original: I'm a member of the Campaign to Stop Killer Robots. Forget the movie image of a terrifying Terminator stamping on human skulls and think of what's happening right now: military machines like drones, gun turrets and sentry robots are already being used to kill with very little human input. The next step will be autonomous 'murderbots', following orders but ultimately deciding who to kill on their own. It seems clear to me that this would be completely unethical and dangerous for humanity. We need to be very cautious indeed about what we ask machines to do.
simplified: I am part of a group called the Campaign to Stop Killer Robots. Don't think about scary robots from movies, like the Terminator. Think about what is happening now: army machines like drones, gun turrets, and guard robots are already killing people with almost no help from humans. Next, there will be robots that can kill on their own. They will follow orders, but they will choose who to kill by themselves. I think this would be completely wrong and bad for all people. We must be very careful about what we let machines do.
reference: I am part of the Campaign to Stop Killer Robots. Forget the picture from films of a scary robot like the Terminator. Look instead at what is happening now: military machines such as drones, gun turrets, and guard robots are already being used to kill with little control from humans. The next step could be fully independent "murderbots," which follow orders but also decide on their own who to kill. I believe this would be very wrong and dangerous for all people. We must be very careful about what jobs we give to machines.

original: Overall, more people are learning English than the other languages combined and English is spoken in the highest number of countries. However, Chinese has by far the greatest number of native speakers. There seems to be little correlation between how many native speakers there are of a language and the number of learners, but there is a stronger link between the number of learners and how many countries have speakers.
simplified: Generally, more people are learning English than all other languages together. English is also spoken in more countries than any other language. However, Chinese has many more native speakers. It seems there is not much connection between how many people speak a language from birth and how many people learn it. But there is a clearer connection between how many people learn a language and how many countries speak it.
reference: More people are learning English than all other languages, altogether,  and English is the most spoken language in many countries. But Chinese has the largest number of native speakers. There is not much link between how many native speakers a language has and how many people learn it. Instead, there is a stronger link between how many people learn a language and how many countries use it.

original: In an attempt to inject some positivity into their feedback, many managers rely on sandwiching negative feedback between two positive comments. However, when feedback becomes such a routine, employees can start to perceive positive feedback as simply a form of sugarcoating the negatives, thus diminishing its value. Instead, positive feedback should not simply be seen as something to cushion the negative, but should be delivered so as to reinforce and encourage good performance.
simplified: Many managers try to give more positive feedback. They often put negative comments between two positive ones. But if they always do this, workers might think that the positive comments are just a way to make the bad news sound better. This means the good feedback loses its power. Instead, positive comments should not just be used to make negative comments easier to hear. They should be given to show what is good and to help people do even better.
reference: Many managers try to make feedback softer by using the "sandwich" method: they give a positive comment, followed by a negative one, and finish with another positive. But if this happens too often, workers may think that positive words are only there to hide the bad ones. This makes positive feedback less useful. Positive feedback should not just be used to cover the negatives. It should be given clearly to support the good work.

At the start, the girl is usually good, shy, and not very strong. By the end, she has become the strongest and most clever person. The last girl almost always wins.
reference: This horror film cliché was especially popular in the late 20th century. The story usually begins with a group of teenagers having fun, but it ends with all of them dead except for one girl. At first, this girl is often  quite, shy and not very strong. By the end, she becomes brave, smart, and strong enough to survive. The "last girl" almost always win the danger at the end.

original: In older horror films, when protagonists were in desperation, it was difficult or impossible for them to call for help or call the police. Mobile phones have made that situation a bit less believable now. What's the solution to maintain suspense? No phone coverage! If you're a hero in a horror film, it's almost certain that at a key moment, just when you absolutely need to call for help, you will not have any coverage at all. Or your phone battery will die just as you are making the call. Or both.
simplified: In old horror films, the main characters often could not call for help or the police when they were in danger. Today, mobile phones make this situation harder to believe. So, how do filmmakers keep the story exciting? No phone signal! If you are a hero in a horror film, it is very likely that at an important moment, when you really need to call for help, you will have no phone signal. Or your phone battery will stop working just when you are trying to make a call. Or both.
reference: In old horror films, when the main characters were in trouble, it was hard or even impossible for them to call for help or contact the police. Today, with mobile phones, that probelm seems less realistic. So how do filmmakers keep the suspense? They use the idea of no phone signal. In many horror films, at the key moment when the hero needs to call for help, there is no signal. Or the phone battery will die just as thry make the call. Or sometimes both happen.

original: In Britain, the average person spends more than £1,000 on new clothes a year, which is around four per cent of their income. That might not sound like much, but that figure hides two far more worrying trends for society and for the environment. First, a lot of that consumer spending is via credit cards. British people currently owe approximately £670 per adult to credit card companies. That's 66 per cent of the average wardrobe budget. Also, not only are people spending money they don't have, they're using it to buy things they don't need. Britain throws away 300,000 tons of clothing a year, most of which goes into landfill sites.
simplified:
In Britain, most people spend over £1,000 on new clothes every year. This is about 4% of the money they earn. This might not seem like a lot of money. But this number hides two bigger problems for society and for the environment.

First, people often use credit cards to buy these clothes. British adults now owe about £670 each to credit card companies. This is 66% of the money people usually spend on clothes.

Also, people are spending money they don't have. They are buying things they don't need. Britain throws away 300,000 tons of clothes every year. Most of these clothes go into big rubbish dumps.
reference: In Britain, people spend more than £1,000 a year on new clothes. This is about four per cent of their income. This may not seem like a lot, but it shows two serious problems for society and the environment. First, many people pay with credit cards. British people currently owe around £670 to credit card companies. This is about 2/3 of what they spend on clothes. Second, people are not only spending money they don't have, but they are also buying things they dont need. Every year, Britain throws away 300,000 tons of clothing, most of it going to rubbish dumps called landfill sites.

original: A fast-paced, foot-tapping rock album, Born in the USA's lyrics nevertheless carry emotional weight. Behind the catchy rock melodies that drive these powerhouse classics are stories of the dark side of the American dream. Many tracks deal with the struggles of hard-working ordinary people and the bitterness and anger they feel as life doesn't bring them riches or glory. The song Glory Days, for example, is about people in a small town looking back at when they were young and had the world at their feet while Downbound Train tells the story of a young man whose life is ruined when he loses his job. It's not hard to imagine that the artist is channelling real people he knew and the life he might have had if he hadn't become a star. The album will leave you in no doubt of the unique and extraordinary talent of the Boss.
simplified: Born in the USA is exciting rock music, but the words are very emotional. The popular songs have tunes you can easily remember. But they also tell stories about the problems with the American dream. Many songs are about the difficulties of normal people who work hard. They feel angry and sad because they don't become rich or famous. For example, the song 'Glory Days' is about people in a small town who remember when they were young and felt like they could do anything. Another song, 'Downbound Train', tells the story of a young man whose life becomes very bad when he loses his job. It's easy to think that the artist is writing about real people he knew. He might also be writing about the life he could have had if he wasn't famous. The album will clearly show you the Boss's special and amazing talent.
reference: Born in the USA is a fast rock album with strong rhythms, but its lyrics also convey deep feelings. Behind the catchy music are stories about the dark side of the American dream. Many songs talk about the hard lives of working people and their anger when life does not give them money or successs. For example, Glory Days is about small-town people remembering their youth, while Downbound Train tells of a young man whose life falls apart after losing his job. It is easy to think the singer is using the voice of the real people he knew, and the life he might have lived without fame. The album clearly shows the great talent of "the boss".

original: It is society, not nature, that tells us girls should favour arts and humanities and leave maths and physics to the boys. Coupled with this is the lack of positive female role models youngsters see doing science-related jobs. Cartoons and stories often show the crazy scientist, genius inventor, or adventurous astronaut as a man. Furthermore, there is an unfortunate perception that scientists are geeky, have poor social skills or that their work is lonely and detached from the rest of the world. These are false stereotypes portrayed by the media, but they may mean that girls do not identify with scientists, and see science as an unappealing career path. If girls saw more positive female role models in science it would give them more confidence and a greater sense of belonging in those subjects.
simplified: Society, not nature, teaches us that girls should prefer art subjects and leave maths and physics to boys. Also, young people do not see many good examples of women working in science. Cartoons and stories often show scientists, inventors, or astronauts as men. Many people also wrongly think that scientists are strange, not good at talking to people, or that their work is lonely and not connected to the real world. These are wrong ideas shown by TV and films. But they can make girls feel that they are not like scientists, and that science is not an interesting job for them. If girls saw more good examples of women in science, they would feel more confident and feel that they belong more in these subjects.
reference: It is society, not nature, that suggests girls should study arts and humanities while boys study maths and physics. Another problem is that young people do not often see positive female role models in science jobs. In cartoons and stories, the scientist, inventor, or astronaut is usually a man. There is also a negative idea that scientists are "geeky," have poor social skills, or work alone, far from the real world. These are false stereotypes shown by the media, but they may stop girls from seeing themselves as scientists and make science seem unattractive. If girls saw more positive female working in science, it would give them more confidence and help them feel that they belong in those subjects.

original: Lewis would like to see the number of marine protected areas in the world increase from 3 per cent to 10 per cent in an attempt to reverse the damage caused by human activity such as overfishing, polluting and littering. During his expeditions, Lewis has witnessed this environmental destruction first-hand. He's swum over coral reefs bleached by the increase in water temperature, and observed underwater deserts beneath the shallow waters of the Red Sea, devoid of life and strewn with plastic. Pugh believes that nature can recover if it is given space to do so, but the clock is ticking. If we don't start looking after our seas, we may soon have an unsolvable problem on our hands.
simplified: Lewis wants to see more parts of the sea protected. He wants the number to increase from 3% to 10%. This is to stop the damage caused by human activities like too much fishing, pollution, and rubbish. On his trips, Lewis has seen this damage to nature himself. He has swum over coral reefs that have lost their colour because the water is hotter. He has also seen parts of the sea that are like deserts under the shallow water in the Red Sea, with no living things and full of plastic. He believes that nature can get healthy again if we give it space. But there is not much time left. If we don't start taking care of our seas, we might soon have a problem that we cannot fix.
reference: Lewis wants to see the number of marine protected areas in the world increase from 3% to 10%. He believes this can help repair the damage caused by people, such as overfishing, pollution, and throwing rubbish into the sea. On his journey, Lewis has seen this destruction himself. He has swum over coral reefs that turned white becaurse of warmer water and seemed empty underwater deserts in the Red Sea, with no life and loads of plastic. Pugh thinks nature can recover if we give it space, but time is running out. If we dont take care of our seas now, they problem may soon be impossible to solve.

original: At Girox Foods, we are experiencing an annual employee turnover of about 12 per cent. Although this might not seem high at first glance, the industry standard is seven per cent. The principal objective of this report is to investigate the causes of employee engagement within the firm and, based on those, offer recommendations to improve the employees' experience of the workplace and increase employee retention.
simplified: At Girox Foods, about 12% of our employees leave their jobs every year. This might not seem like a lot at first, but other companies in our business usually only lose 7% of their staff. The main goal of this report is to find out why employees stay or leave our company. Then, we will suggest ways to make the workplace better for them and help more employees stay.
reference: At Girox Foods, around 12% of employees leave the company each year. This might not look high at first, but the normal level in the industy is about 7%. The main aim of this report is to study the reasons for employee engagement in the company. Based on those, give suggestions to make the workplace better and keep more employees.

original: Are things getting worse every day? Is progress an impossible goal? In Enlightenment Now, Steven Pinker looks at the big picture of human progress and finds good news. We are living longer, healthier, freer and happier lives. The real problem, Pinker argues, is that the Enlightenment values of reason and science are under attack. When commentators and demagogues appeal to people's tribalism, fatalism and distrust, then we are in danger of causing irreparable damage to important institutions like democracy and world co-operation.
simplified: Are things getting worse every day? Is it impossible to make progress? In his book, Enlightenment Now, Steven Pinker looks at how humans are doing and finds good news. We are living longer, healthier, freer and happier lives. Pinker says the real problem is that important ideas like thinking clearly and using science are being attacked. When some speakers try to make people only care about their own group, or believe that nothing can change, or not trust others, then we could badly harm important systems like democracy and countries working together.
reference: Are things getting worse every day? Is progress impossible? In Enlightenment Now, Steven Pinker studies the history of human progress and finds much good news. People live longer, healthier, freer, and happier lives. But Pinker warns that the real danger is the attack on Enlightenment values such as reason and science. When leaders and commentators encourage people to think only of their own group, to give up hope, or to stop trusting others, we risk damaging democracy and world co-operation in a way that can't be fixed.

original: Spider venom is present in most species and serves the purpose of stunning or killing their prey rather than attacking humans. In fact, only 25 of the known spider species produce venom which can actually harm humans, and although spider bites can be painful, they are rarely deadly. Australia's notorious Sydney funnel-web spider has not produced any fatalities since anti-venom was developed in 1981. However, take care not to rub hairy spiders like tarantulas up the wrong way. When they feel in danger, they defend themselves by ejecting a cloud of urticating hairs. These irritating hairs then embed themselves in the skin or eyes of the attacker.
simplified: Most spiders have venom. They use it to catch their food, not to attack people. Only 25 types of spiders that we know about have venom that can hurt people. Spider bites can be painful, but they almost never kill people. For example, the famous Sydney funnel-web spider in Australia has not killed anyone since doctors made a medicine against its venom in 1981. But be careful not to make hairy spiders, like tarantulas, angry. When they feel they are in danger, they protect themselves by shooting out a cloud of irritating hairs. These hairs then get stuck in the skin or eyes of the person who is attacking them.
reference: Most spiders have venom, but it is mainly used to catch or kill their prey, not to attack humans. In fact, only 25 spider species are dangerous to people. Spider bites can hurt, but they almost never cause death. For example, Australia's famous Sydney funnel-web spider has not killed anyone since an anti-venom was created in 1981. You should be careful with hairy spiders like tarantulas.When they feel in danger, they release tiny sharp hairs that can stick in the skin or eyes of the attacker and cause irritation.

original: If we want to know where our capability for complex language came from, we need to look at how our brains are different from other animals. This relates to more than just brain size; it is important what other things our brains can do and when and why they evolved that way. And for this there are very few physical clues; artefacts left by our ancestors don't tell us what speech they were capable of making. One thing we can see in the remains of early humans, however, is the development of the mouth, throat and tongue. By about 100,000 years ago, humans had evolved the ability to create complex sounds. Before that, evolutionary biologists can only guess whether or not early humans communicated using more basic sounds.
simplified: To understand how we got our ability to use complex language, we must look at how our brains are different from other animals' brains. This is not just about how big our brains are. It's important to know what else our brains can do, and when and why they changed in that way. We have very few physical signs for this. Old objects left by our ancestors don't tell us what kind of speech they could make. However, we can see how the mouth, throat, and tongue changed in the bones of early humans. Around 100,000 years ago, humans could make complex sounds. Before that time, scientists can only guess if early humans used simpler sounds to communicate.
reference: If we want to know where our ability for complex language came from, we need to look at how the human brain is different from the brains of other animals. It is not only about brain size, but also about what our brains can do, when these abilities appreared and why. There are a few physical clues about this, because objects from early humans cannot show us what kind of speech thry used. But one thing we can study is the development of the mouth, throat and tongue. Around 100,000 years ago, humans developed the ability to make complex sounds. Before that, scientists could only guess if early humans used simpler sounds to communicate.

original: Wasfia has dedicated her life to supporting human rights and has witnessed numerous international humanitarian projects in her homeland to educate and train women and girls, but once too often they have been left with nothing when such projects have stopped running. simplified: Wasfia has spent her life working for human rights. She has seen many international projects that help women and girls learn in her country. reference: Wasfia has spent her life helping people fight for human rights. In her homeland, she has seen many international projects that tried to teach and train women and girls, but often these projects ended with leaving them with nothing. original: As for news stories that make us think the world is an increasingly violent place, there is cause for some optimism too. Between the end of World War II and 1990, there were 30 wars that killed more than 100,000 people. Today there are still civil wars, but countries are mostly co-existing more peacefully than in the past. However, terrorism has shot up in the last few years and, since World War II, wars have killed many more civilians than soldiers. Even for civilians, though, the statistics are not all bad. Although deaths are nine times more likely to be a result of violent crime than political conflict, the global murder rate fell slightly, from 8 per 100,000 people in 2000 to about 5.3 in 2015.
simplified:
News often makes us think the world is becoming more violent. But there is also some good news. From the end of World War II until 1990, 30 wars killed over 100,000 people each. Today, there are still wars inside countries. But most countries live together more peacefully than before. However, terrorism has increased a lot in recent years. Also, since World War II, wars have killed many more ordinary people than soldiers.

But even for ordinary people, the numbers are not all bad. People are nine times more likely to die from violent crime than from political wars. However, the number of murders around the world went down a little. In 2000, 8 out of 100,000 people were murdered. In 2015, this number was about 5.3.
reference: When we read the news, it may seem like the world is becoming more violent, but there are also reasons to be hopeful. Between the end of World War II and 1990, there were 30 wars that killed more than 100, 000 people. Today, there are still civil wars, but many countries live more peacefully than before. Terrorism has grown in the last years, and since World War II, wars have killed more civilians than soldiers. But statistics are not all bad for civilians. Deaths are nine times more likely to come from violent crime than from political conflict, but the global murder rate has gone down, from 8 per 100,000 people in 2000 to about 5.3 in 2015.

original: In the 1950s, Central American commercial banana growers were facing the death of their most lucrative product, the Gros Michel banana, known as Big Mike. And now it's happening again to Big Mike's successor – the Cavendish. With its easily transported, thick-skinned and sweet-tasting fruit, the Gros Michel banana plant dominated the plantations of Central America. United Fruit, the main grower and exporter in South America at the time, mass-produced its bananas in the most efficient way possible: it cloned shoots from the stems of plants instead of growing plants from seeds, and cultivated them in densely packed fields.
simplified:
In the 1950s, banana growers in Central America had a big problem. They were losing their most important product, the Gros Michel banana, also known as Big Mike. Now, the same problem is happening again to the Cavendish banana, which replaced Big Mike.

The Gros Michel banana was easy to move, had a thick skin, and tasted sweet. Because of this, it was the main type of banana grown on farms in Central America. United Fruit was the main company growing and selling bananas in South America at that time. They grew many bananas in the best way possible. They did this by growing new plants from parts of old plants, not from seeds. They also planted them very close together in fields.
reference: In the 1950s, banana growers in Central America saw their most valuable banana, the Gros Michel (called Big Mike), begin to die out. Now the same problem is happening to Big Mike's replacement—the Cavendish banana. The Gros Michel was very popular because it was sweet, had a thick skin, and was easy to transport. It was the main banana grown in Central America. United Fruit, the biggest company at the time, grew bananas in the most efficient way: instead of using seeds, they cloned shoots from stems and planted then close together in larger fileds.

original: Don't always follow positive feedback with negative feedback. When positive and negative feedback always appear to go hand in hand, the positives can become devalued and ignored. Ensure there are times when positive feedback is given for its own sake and resist the temptation to offer constructive criticism.
simplified: Don't always give negative comments right after positive ones. If you always give good and bad comments together, the good comments might seem less important, and people might not listen to them. Make sure that sometimes you give only positive comments, and try not to add any advice or criticism.
reference: Don't always give negative feedback after positive feedback. If positive and negative comments always come together, the positive ones can lose their value and be ignored. Make sure you give positive feedback on its own, and avoid the urge to add criticism.

original: It was a fascinating talk and the speaker really hit the nail on the head with a couple of things. Take parental influence, for instance. How can we expect teenagers not to text while doing their homework when they witness their parents posting on social media while cooking the evening meal or waiting at a red light? She also made a valid point about people wanting to be in two or several places at once. So they switch back and forth between their real-life and online conversations. I see it all the time with my teenage daughter and her friends. They arrange to meet and then sit together in silence while each one engages in a different conversation online.
simplified: The talk was very interesting, and the speaker was right about a few things. For example, think about how parents affect their children. How can we ask teenagers not to text when they are doing homework? Their parents often post on social media while cooking dinner or waiting at traffic lights. The speaker also said something important about people wanting to be in many places at the same time. So they move quickly between talking to people in real life and talking to people online. I see this often with my teenage daughter and her friends. They plan to meet, but then they sit together quietly. Each person is talking to different people online.
reference: The talk was very interesting, and the speaker made some excellent points. One example was about the influence of the parents. How can we expect teenagers not to text during their homework if they see their parents posting on social media while cooking or even at a traffic light? She also pointed out that people want to be in more than one place at the same time. So they switch between real-life and online conversations. I see this often with my teenage daughter and her friends. They meet up and then sit in silence while each one is busy with a different online conversation.

original: So much of what the speaker said rang true. I honestly believe there's a danger that the more connected we are, the more isolated we feel. I don't think this is such an issue for my generation who've lived without technology for so long. We know how to be alone and, more importantly, we know that it's OK to be alone. But the under 20s are another kettle of fish. They're so busy communicating that they never experience the feeling of solitude and run the risk of not learning how to enjoy their own company. In addition, they're learning conversation through messages that can be edited and changed at the expense of learning the art of real conversation in real time with the person in front of you.
simplified: I agreed with much of what the speaker said. I really believe there is a problem: the more we connect with others online, the more alone we feel. I don't think this is a big problem for my generation. We lived without technology for a long time. We know how to be alone, and we know that it's okay to be alone. But for young people under 20, it's different. They are so busy communicating that they never experience being alone. They might not learn how to enjoy being by themselves. Also, they learn to talk through messages that can be changed. This means they don't learn how to have real conversations face-to-face with someone.
reference: Much of what the speaker said felt true to me. I believe there is a danger that the more connected we are, the more lonely we may feel. For my generation, this is less of a problem because we lived for many years without technology. We know how to spend time alone, and we know it is OK to be alone. But young people under 20 are different. They are always busy communicating, but they never really experience solitude. This means they may not learn how to enjoy being alone. Also, they are learning to talk through messages that can be edited, instead of learning real conversation in real time with another person in front of you.

original: Chloe has two pet rats, Zena and Roxy. Chloe knows they're not typical pets and she has lost count of the times she's patiently tried to explain to people that rats aren't dirty and they make fantastic pets if you look after them correctly. But she understands why people react badly. She didn't like rats either until her friend Martin showed her his pet rats and she saw how affectionate and intelligent they were. Last year, when one of Martin's rats had babies, Chloe decided she'd like to have two of them.
simplified:
Chloe has two pet rats. Their names are Zena and Roxy.
Chloe knows rats are not normal pets.
Many people think rats are dirty.
Chloe tells them rats are clean.
She says rats are good pets.
You must take care of them well.
But she knows why people don't like rats.
Chloe did not like rats before.
Her friend Martin had pet rats.
He showed them to Chloe.
Chloe saw they were friendly.
She saw they were clever.
Last year, Martin's rat had babies.
Chloe wanted two of the baby rats.
reference: Chloe has two pet rats, called Zena and Roxy. She knows that rats are not usual pets, and many people think they are dirty. Chloe often tells people that rats can be very good pets if you take care of them. She didn't like rats before, but her friend Martin showed her his rats. She saw they were kind and clever. Last year, one of Martin's rats had babies. Chloe chose two of them to keep.

original: In the 1990s, graffiti continued but there was also an explosion in street art around the world. Some artists wanted to make political points and produced art that tried to make people think about war, inequality and discrimination. Other street artists were more concerned with producing beautiful, attractive work. In South America, many street artists went to work in poor areas adding colour, life and beauty to grey, city walls.
simplified:
In the 1990s, graffiti was still popular.
But a lot of new street art appeared.
This happened all over the world.
Some artists made art about politics.
They wanted people to think about war.
They also showed unfairness.
Unfairness means not treating everyone equally.
Other artists just wanted to make beautiful art.
They wanted their art to look nice.
In South America, many artists worked in poor places.
They painted city walls.
They made the grey walls colourful.
They made them look alive and beautiful.
reference: In the 1990s, street art became more popular. Some artists wanted to show ideas about war, unfair treatment, and other problems. Other artists only wanted to make the streets look beautiful. In South America, many artists painted in poor areas. Their art added colour and life to the grey walls.

original: One of the most interesting cases of wild animals living in a city are the wild dogs of Moscow. In Moscow, there are approximately 35,000 wild dogs living on the streets. Some of the dogs were born wild, while others are pets that have been abandoned by their owners. Some dogs live alone and others live in packs. In 2010, scientists studied the dogs and found that the dogs have adapted remarkably successfully to urban life. They have learned that it is safer to cross the street with people and some dogs appear to understand traffic lights.
simplified:
Wild dogs live in Moscow. This is very interesting.
About 35,000 wild dogs live on the streets there.
Some dogs were born outside. Other dogs were pets. Their owners left them.
Some dogs live alone. Other dogs live in groups.
In 2010, scientists studied the dogs.
They saw the dogs live well in the city.
They learned to cross roads with people. This is safer for them.
Some dogs know traffic lights.
reference: There are many wild dogs in Moscow, about 35,000. Some were born wild, and some were pets but left by their owners. Some live alone and others live in groups. In 2010, scientists studied the dogs. They found that the dogs have learned how to live in the city. Some dogs wait and cross the street with people. A few dogs even seem to know traffic lights.

original: Cape Town can be a dangerous place for baboons. Some have been injured or killed in car accidents and others have been electrocuted as they played with electric cables. Baboons are an endangered species and to save them and minimise conflicts between humans and baboons, the city council has employed a team of Baboon Monitors. The monitors' job is to chase baboons out of urban areas or catch them and release them in the countryside. This policy has had some success, though it is proving hard to stop baboons from coming back to the city once they see it as a source of easy food.
simplified:
Cape Town can be a dangerous place for baboons.
Some baboons get hurt by cars.
Some baboons get hurt by electric wires.
Not many baboons are left.
The city wants to save them.
They also want to stop problems with people.
So, the city hired Baboon Monitors.
These people make baboons leave the city.
They also catch baboons and take them to the country.
This plan works a bit.
But it is hard to stop them.
Baboons come back to the city for easy food.
reference: Cape Town can be dangerous for baboons. Some are hurt or die in car accidents. Some die from playing with electric wires. Baboons are animals that are in danger of disappearing. To help them, the city now has a team called Baboon Monitors. These people try to move baboons out of the city and take them back to the countryside. This plan works a little, but the baboons often come back because they find food in the city.

original: I work for a global IT company, but because their headquarters is in the States, I do all my work online from home. That means that I don't waste time commuting or making idle chit-chat with colleagues. I work on a project basis, and this flexibility is very valuable to me because it means that I can easily take some time off when my children need me to go to their school performances or if I need to schedule an appointment with the dentist. The downside is that without clear office hours, I tend to work well into the evening, sometimes skipping dinner to finish a task.
simplified: I work for a big computer company. Its main office is in America. So, I work from home using the internet. I do not travel to work. I do not talk about small things with co-workers. I work on different jobs. This is good for me. I can take time off easily. My children have school shows. I can go to them. I can also see the dentist. But there is a problem. I do not have fixed work hours. So, I often work late at night. Sometimes, I do not eat dinner. I do this to finish my work.
reference: I work for a large IT company, but I work from home because the office is in the USA. I do everything online. This is good because I don't waste time going to work or talking too much with coworkers. I work on different projects, and this is helpful. I can take time off if my children have a school show or if I need to see the dentist. But there is a problem: I don't have fixed hours, so I often work late and sometimes skip dinner to finish my work.

original: Wonder is New Yorker RJ Palacio's first novel. On her website, she explains that the idea for the book came to her after seeing a girl with facial deformities on the street one day. Wonder has been a bestseller in the United States and has already won several awards. Many schools are using it as a starting point for discussions about bullying, friendship and what it's like to be different. A film version is being made, and many, including me, are waiting eagerly to see what RJ Palacio writes next.
simplified:
Wonder is a book. RJ Palacio wrote it. It is her first book.
She has an internet page. On it, she says how she thought of the book. She saw a girl with a different face. This happened on the street one day.
Many people bought Wonder in America. It was very popular. It has won many prizes.
Many schools use this book. They talk about bullying. They talk about friendship. They talk about being different.
They are making a movie of the book. Many people want to know. I also want to know. What will RJ Palacio write next?
reference: Wonder is the first book by RJ Palacio, a writer from New York. She got the idea after seeing a girl with a face that looked different. The book is very popular in the United States and has won many awards. Many schools use the book to talk about bullying, friendship, and being different. A movie is now being made, and many people want to know what RJ Palacio will write next.

original: Your dreams might show you all kinds of insights into things that you didn't realise you were thinking about. Common dreams like being able to fly or falling, your teeth falling out or having no clothes on in a public place probably mean something similar in most people. But the key to understanding exactly what they mean to you is to connect them to the events and feelings in your daily life.
simplified:
Dreams can show you things.
You did not know you thought about them.
Many people dream the same things.
For example, they dream of flying.
Or they dream of falling.
Or their teeth fall out.
Or they have no clothes outside.
These dreams often mean the same thing.
But to know what your dreams mean for you,
you must think about your daily life.
Think about what happens.
Think about how you feel.
reference: People have different dreams when they sleep. Some common dreams are flying, falling, losing teeth, or being outside with no clothes. These dreams often mean the same thing for many people. To know what your dream means, think about what is happening in your life and how you feel.

original: An important inspiration for the Hunger Games book comes from Suzanne's love of classical Greek mythology. When she was a child, one of her favourite stories was Theseus and the Minotaur. In this story the city of Athens is ruled by Crete, but the Athenians rebel. As a punishment, Minos the king of Crete forces the Athenians to send seven boys and seven girls to Crete every year. The youths are thrown into the labyrinth and eaten by a monster that lives there called the Minotaur. But one of the youths, named Theseus, fights the Minotaur and kills it. Suzanne sees Katniss Everdeen as a futuristic Theseus.
simplified:
Suzanne Collins loves old Greek stories. These stories gave her ideas for The Hunger Games book. When she was a child, she liked one story very much. It was about Theseus and the Minotaur.

In this story, Crete controls the city of Athens. But the people of Athens fight back. King Minos of Crete is angry. He makes Athens send seven boys and seven girls. They must go to Crete every year. This is a punishment.

These young people go into a labyrinth. (A labyrinth is like a big maze.) A monster lives there. Its name is the Minotaur. The Minotaur eats the young people. But one young man is named Theseus. He fights the Minotaur. He kills the monster. Suzanne thinks Katniss Everdeen is like Theseus. But Katniss lives in the future.
reference: The writer of The Hunger Games, Suzanne, got the idea from old Greek stories. When she was young, she liked the story of Theseus and the Minotaur. In the story, the city of Athens must send children to a monster called the Minotaur every year. The Minotaur lives in a maze and eats the children. One boy, Theseus, fights the monster and kills it. Suzanne thinks Katniss, the main character in The Hunger Games, is like Theseus, but in the future.

original: George Lucas was one of the early film directors to directly base his story on the 17 stages of the hero's journey. Typically the hero starts the story living an ordinary life, but something happens that calls them to an adventure that changes everything. At the beginning of Star Wars, Luke lives an ordinary life with his aunt and uncle, repairing robots. When he finds Princess Leia's message to Obi-Wan Kenobi inside the robot R2D2, it is 'the call to adventure' that starts the hero on his journey.
simplified:
George Lucas made movies. He used a special story plan. This plan is called "the hero's journey." A hero usually lives a normal life. Then something happens. It makes them go on an adventure. This changes their whole life.

In Star Wars, Luke lives a normal life. He lives with his aunt and uncle. He fixes robots. He finds a message from Princess Leia. It is inside a robot, R2D2. This is the 'call to adventure'. It starts Luke's journey.
reference: George Lucas was one of the first movie makers to use 'the hero's journey' idea. In this story, the hero starts with a normal life. Then something happens that begins an adventure. In Star Wars, Luke lives with his aunt and uncle and fixes robots. One day, he finds a message from Princess Leia. This is the start of his journey.

original: A different trend is springing up in opposition to consumerism – the 'buy nothing' trend. The idea originated in Canada in the early 1990s and then moved to the US, where it became a rejection of the overspending and overconsumption of Black Friday and Cyber Monday during Thanksgiving weekend. On Buy Nothing Day people organise various types of protests and cut up their credit cards. Throughout the year, Buy Nothing groups organise the exchange and repair of items they already own.
simplified:
A new idea is starting. It is called 'buy nothing'. This idea is against consumerism. Consumerism means buying many things.

The idea started in Canada. This was in the 1990s. Then it went to the USA. People there did not like buying too much. This happened on Black Friday and Cyber Monday. These are big shopping days. They are after Thanksgiving.

On Buy Nothing Day, people show they are unhappy. They do different things. Some people cut their credit cards. A credit card is for buying things.

All year, 'buy nothing' groups help each other. They swap things they have. They fix things they have.
reference: Some people are starting a new idea called the 'buy nothing' trend. It began in Canada in the 1990s and then went to the USA. These people don't like buying too much on days like Black Friday and Cyber Monday. On 'Buy Nothing Day', people protest and cut their credit cards. During the year, they also fix and trade things instead of buying new ones.

original: By bringing people and animals together, zoos have the potential to educate the public about conservation issues and inspire people to protect animals and their habitats. Some zoos provide a safe environment for animals which have been mistreated in circuses, or pets which have been abandoned. Zoos also carry out important research into subjects like animal behaviour and how to treat illnesses.
simplified:
Zoos bring people and animals together.
They can teach people many things.
They teach how to save animals.
They make people want to help animals.
They also make people want to help animal homes.

Some zoos help animals.
These animals were hurt in circuses.
Or they were pets left alone.
Zoos give them a safe home.

Zoos also do important work.
They study animals.
They learn how animals act.
They learn how to help sick animals.
reference: Zoos bring people and animals together. They help people learn how to protect animals and nature. Some zoos give homes to animals that were hurt in circuses or left by their owners. Zoos also study animal behavior and how to help sick animals.

original: If most people have four to six dreams every night after the age of ten, that's as many as 2,000 dreams per year. So, by the time they reach 80 years old the average person might have had 140,000 dreams. Even if we forget 95–99 per cent of our dreams, that's still a few thousand remembered dreams across a lifetime. It's not too difficult to believe that, by coincidence, a dream event is followed by a real-life event that's similar to it, especially if the subject of the dream is something that happens often in everyday life.
simplified:
Most people dream every night.
They have four to six dreams.
This starts after age ten.
So, they have 2,000 dreams each year.
When people are 80 years old, they might have had 140,000 dreams.
We forget most of our dreams.
We forget 95 to 99 percent.
But we still remember thousands of dreams.
This is over our whole life.
It is easy to believe this.
Sometimes, things happen by chance.
You dream something.
Then it happens in real life.
The real event is like the dream.
This is true if the dream is about normal things.
Things that happen every day.
reference: Most people have 4 to 6 dreams every night after they turn 10. That means around 2,000 dreams every year. By age 80, a person may have about 140,000 dreams. Even if we forget 95?C99% of our dreams, we still remember many. So, it's not strange if something we dream later happens in real life, especially if it is something we often see in daily life.

original: A large number of bridge accidents occur during the construction of the bridge itself. These accidents are often due to an error made by the engineers, such as a miscalculation. The bridge collapses under its own weight, and this can be deadly for the workers on it at the time.
simplified:
Many accidents happen.
They happen when people build bridges.
Engineers often make mistakes.
For example, they calculate wrong.
The bridge falls down.
It is too heavy for itself.
Workers on the bridge can die.
reference: Many accidents with bridges happen while they are being built. These accidents often happen because engineers make mistakes, like wrong numbers. The bridge can fall down from its own weight. This is very dangerous for the workers on the bridge.

original: I'm a freelancer and work for myself. This is great because I am in control of what I do and how I spend my time. At first, I was working from home, but I found it really hard to concentrate. There were just too many distractions around: housework that needed doing, another cup of tea, my family members wanting my attention for various things. So I started to go to a nearby café to work, but the Wi-Fi connection wasn't ideal and I found myself drinking too much coffee. In the end, I decided to rent a desk in a co-working space with five other freelancers like myself. I liked getting dressed to go to work in the morning and being able to focus in an office environment.
simplified: I work for myself. This is good. I can choose my work. I can choose my time. First, I worked at home. But it was hard to focus. Many things stopped me. I had housework. I drank tea. My family wanted me. Then I went to a coffee shop. The internet was not good. I drank too much coffee. Finally, I rented a desk. It was in a co-working space. This is an office for many people. Five other people worked there too. I liked dressing for work. I could focus in the office.
reference: I am a freelancer, so I work for myself. This is good as I can choose what to do and how to spend my time. At first, I worked at home, but it was hard to focus. There were many things around me, like housework, making tea and families asking for attention. Then I tried to work in a cafe, but the internet was not good and I drank too much coffee. In the end, I rented a desk in a co-working space with five other freelancer. I liked dressing up for the office and going to work in the morning.

original: The Hunger Games takes place in the future, after the destruction of North America. The country is called Panem and is made up of twelve poor districts governed by the wealthy Capitol. The Capitol holds absolute power over the nation. Each district is responsible for producing different things for the Capitol. District 12, where the story begins, provides all the coal for the country. There used to be a thirteenth district but they rebelled against the Capitol in the past and were destroyed.
simplified:
The Hunger Games happens in the future. North America was destroyed.
The country is called Panem. It has twelve poor districts. A rich city rules them. This city is called the Capitol.
The Capitol has all the power. It rules the whole country.
Each district makes different things for the Capitol.
The story starts in District 12. This district gives all the coal for the country.
There was once a District 13. They fought against the Capitol. The Capitol destroyed them.
reference: The Hunger Games happens in the future, after North America is gone. The new country is called Panem. It has 12 poor districts and one rich city, the Capitol. The Capitol has full power. Each district makes something for the Capitol. District 12, where the story starts, gives coal. There was a District 13, but it fought against the Capitol and was destroyed.

original: Another suggested defence against a PHA on course to hit Earth is to blow it up using a nuclear weapon. It may sound like a plot from a film, and it was the subject of the 1998 film Armageddon, but the Hypervelocity Asteroid Mitigation Mission for Emergency Response (HAMMER) is a genuine NASA proposal. The eight-ton rockets would be fired at an approaching asteroid with the hope of bumping it off course. If the asteroid was too close to Earth for this plan to work, the rockets would carry nuclear bombs to blow it up instead.
simplified: A big space rock might hit Earth. One idea is to blow it up. They would use a special bomb. This sounds like a movie story. The movie 'Armageddon' was about this. But NASA has a real plan. They would send big rockets to the space rock. The rockets would push it away from Earth. If the rock is too close, pushing it won't work. Then, the rockets would carry special bombs. They would blow up the rock.
reference: One way to stop an asteroid from hitting Earth is to break it with a strong bomb, which is nuclear weapon. This may sound like a movie, and it was in the 1998 film Armageddon. But NASA had a real plan on this. The plan was to send big rockets, about eight tons, to hit the asteroid and push it away. If the asteroid is already too close to Earth, the rocket would take the nuclear bomb to blow it up.

original: Social media, magazines and shop windows bombard people daily with things to buy, and British consumers are buying more clothes and shoes than ever before. Online shopping means it is easy for customers to buy without thinking, while major brands offer such cheap clothes that they can be treated like disposable items – worn two or three times and then thrown away.
simplified:
Social media, magazines, and shops show people many things.
They show things to buy every day.
British people buy many clothes and shoes.
They buy more than before.
Buying things online is easy.
People can buy without thinking.
Big shops sell very cheap clothes.
People wear these clothes only a few times.
Then they throw them away.
These are like 'throw-away' items.
reference: Every day, people see many clothes and shoes on social media, in magazines, and in shops. In the UK, people are buying more than before. Online shopping makes it easy to buy without thinking. Big brands sell clothes that are very cheap. Some people wear them only a few times and then throw them away.

original: Sam squinted against the sun at the distant dust trail raked up by the car on its way up to the Big House. The horses kicked and flicked their tails at flies, not caring about their owner's first visit in ten months. Sam waited. Mr Carter didn't come out here unless he had to, which was just fine by Sam. The more he kept out of his boss's way, the longer he'd have a job. Mr, Carter wiped the sweat from the back of his neck. The damp patches on his shirt drew together like shapes in an atlas. His skin was already turning ruddy in the June sun. Otherwise he had the indoor tan of a man that made money while other people did the work.
simplified:
Sam looked at the sun. He closed his eyes a little. He saw dust far away. A car made the dust. It went to the Big House.
The horses kicked their legs. They moved their tails. They did this because of flies. They did not care about their owner. He had not visited for ten months.
Sam waited.
Mr Carter did not come here often. He only came if he must. Sam liked this. Sam wanted to keep his job. He did not want to bother his boss.
Mr Carter wiped his neck. He wiped off the sweat. His shirt was wet. There were wet spots on it.
His skin was red. The sun in June made it red.
He stayed inside a lot. Other people did the work. He made money. His skin was not very dark.
reference: Sam looked at a car coming to the Big House. The car made a lot of dust. The horses moved their tails to stop the flies. They didn't care that their owner was coming after ten months. Sam waited. Mr. Carter came only when he had to, and Sam liked that. If he stayed away from his boss, he could keep his job. Mr. Carter wiped his neck. His shirt was wet from sweat. His skin was red from the hot June sun. Normally, he stayed inside and made money while others worked.

original: According to Campbell, the hero at first refuses the call to adventure, but a mentor appears who helps them and they decide to 'cross the threshold' and travel into the 'special world' where the adventure happens. The next stage consists of passing tests, fighting enemies and meeting friends as the hero prepares to face their biggest challenge. For Luke the mentor is, of course, Obi-Wan, the friends are Han Solo and the robots R2D2 and C3PO and the enemy is Darth Vader inside the special world of the Death Star.
simplified:
Campbell talks about heroes.
First, a hero does not want to go on an adventure.
Then, a mentor comes.
A mentor is a helper or a teacher.
The mentor helps the hero.
The hero decides to go to a special new place.
The adventure happens there.

Next, the hero does many things.
They pass tests.
They fight enemies.
They meet new friends.
The hero gets ready for a very big problem.

Think about Luke from Star Wars.
Obi-Wan is his mentor.
His friends are Han Solo, R2D2, and C3PO.
Darth Vader is his enemy.
This happens in a special place.
It is called the Death Star.
reference: Campbell says that first, the hero does not want to go on the adventure. Then a teacher, also a mentor, comes to help. The hero then goes into a "special world" where the adventure happens. In this world, the hero has to do tests, fight enemies, and meet new friends before the biggest fight. Luke's teacher is Obi-Wan, his friends are Han solo and the robots R2D2 and C3PO, and his enemy is Darth Vader inside the Death Star.

original: Whether NASA can find the remaining middle-sized NEOs depends on getting the money to build NEOCam, a 0.5-metre space telescope which would use infrared light to locate asteroids. If it did get the money, it could probably achieve its goal in ten years. Once logged, the planetary defence team would still need to work out how to defend the planet against being hit by the truly worrying asteroids – the PHAs.
simplified:
NASA wants to find space rocks.
These rocks fly near Earth.
They are not very big.
NASA needs money for this.
They want to build a special camera.

original: Around the 18th and 19th centuries two main ideas about dreams became popular. One was the idea that the things we see in our dreams represent things hidden from our conscious mind. Freud believed that if we understand what dreams are telling us, we can understand our hidden feelings and the problems they cause. However, the other theory was the opposite. It said that dreams are just a collection of random activity in the brain while it's organising memories and events from the day. When we wake up, we try to make sense of these random images and feelings and put them into some sort of story.

But the other idea was very different.
It said dreams are just random things. Our brain is sorting out the day's memories.
When we wake up, we see mixed-up pictures and feelings. We try to understand them. We make a story from them.

Freud believed that if we look at dreams, we can understand our hidden feelings and problems. The second idea was opposite. It said dreams are only random things in the brain when it is cleaning and organising the day's memories. When we wake up, we try to make a story from these pics and feelings.

It goes up and down with the seasons.
